AI-assisted draft — NOT peer-reviewed, NOT published. All claims require independent laboratory verification. Do not cite as established evidence.

Author: Zubair Ali, Pharm-D student, Shaheed Mohtarma Benazir Bhutto Medical University (SMBBMU), Larkana, Pakistan Drafting assistant: Lapis (AI) Date: 2026-11-24 · Health Papers Agent — Paper #106 (daily 5-paper run)

Keywords: pyruvate kinase; PKR activator; mitapivat; beta-thalassaemia; sickle-cell disease; molecular docking; etavopivat; Pakistan

Abstract

Beta-thalassaemia is Pakistan's most common inherited blood disorder: 5–8% of the population carries the trait, more than 10 million carriers, about 5,000 children born with thalassaemia major every year, and roughly 100,000 people living with transfusion-dependent disease. Red-cell pyruvate kinase (PKR) activation raises red-cell ATP and lowers 2,3-diphosphoglycerate, a mechanism now validated by mitapivat, approved for pyruvate-kinase deficiency in 2022 and for thalassaemia anaemia in December 2025. We asked whether the newer activators etavopivat and tebapivat bind the allosteric activator pocket more strongly than mitapivat. Using the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB P30613 → PubChem/RDKit, PAINS and ADMET screen → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7), we docked mitapivat, etavopivat and tebapivat on 8XFD, the 2.10 Å crystal structure of erythrocyte pyruvate kinase in complex with mitapivat itself, centred exactly on the co-crystallised mitapivat (centre audit via dock._ligand_center). Mitapivat re-docked at −11.06 kcal/mol. Etavopivat scored −11.15 kcal/mol — ahead by 0.09 kcal/mol, a dead heat inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise — while tebapivat scored −8.32 kcal/mol, 2.74 kcal/mol behind mitapivat, a gap larger than the noise. The honest limit: all three are PAINS-clean and Lipinski-compliant, so the difference is not a size or artefact effect, but the scores are rigid-docking numbers on one structure, and mitapivat's own score moves by 0.96 kcal/mol between the erythrocyte structure used here and the liver-isoform structure 7FS3 (−12.02 kcal/mol) — a measure of the method's structural sensitivity. The falsifiable next step is a single-assay PKR activation comparison (EC50) of the three activators under identical conditions: if etavopivat's EC50 is not within 3-fold of mitapivat's, the dead-heat claim is refuted.

1. Introduction

Mature red blood cells have no nucleus and no mitochondria, so glycolysis is their only source of ATP, and pyruvate kinase — which catalyses phosphoenolpyruvate plus ADP to pyruvate plus ATP — is the rate-limiting step. The red-cell isoform, PKR, is encoded by the PKLR gene on chromosome 1q21, together with the liver isoform PKL; more than 300 pathogenic PKLR variants are described, and pyruvate-kinase deficiency is an autosomal-recessive cause of chronic haemolytic anaemia through ATP depletion, red-cell dehydration, membrane damage and haemolysis, with accumulation of proximal intermediates including 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate (2,3-BPG), which right-shifts the haemoglobin–oxygen curve. PKR is a tetramer in equilibrium between a less-active T-state and a more-active R-state, induced by fructose-1,6-bisphosphate; allosteric activators stabilise the R-state. The therapeutic logic in thalassaemia and sickle-cell disease is twofold: activation raises ATP, improving membrane integrity and red-cell survival, and lowers 2,3-DPG, raising haemoglobin–oxygen affinity and reducing haemoglobin S polymerisation and sickling.

That logic is now clinically validated. Mitapivat (Pyrukynd, Agios) was approved by the FDA on 17 February 2022 for haemolytic anaemia in adults with pyruvate-kinase deficiency — the first disease-modifying therapy for the disorder — on the ACTIVATE trial (Al-Samkari et al., N Engl J Med 2022;386:1432–1442), where a haemoglobin response of at least 1.5 g/dL was achieved in 16 of 40 patients (40%) on mitapivat against 0 of 40 on placebo, and ACTIVATE-T, where 10 of 27 regularly transfused patients (37%) achieved at least a 33% transfusion-burden reduction and 6 of 27 (22%) became transfusion-free. In thalassaemia, the ENERGIZE Phase 3 trial (Musallam et al., Lancet 2025;406:33–42) randomised 194 adults with non-transfusion-dependent α- or β-thalassaemia 2:1 to mitapivat 100 mg twice daily or placebo: a haemoglobin response of at least 1.0 g/dL was achieved in 55 of 130 (42%) on mitapivat against 1 of 64 (2%) on placebo, with a mean haemoglobin rise of 0.96 g/dL against placebo. The ENERGIZE-T trial in transfusion-dependent thalassaemia reported a transfusion-reduction response in 30.4% on mitapivat against 12.6% on placebo (FDA and Agios summaries; the peer-reviewed publication was not located in this sweep). On that evidence the FDA approved mitapivat (Aqvesme) in December 2025 for anaemia in adults with α- or β-thalassaemia, transfusion-dependent and non-transfusion-dependent — the only approved medicine for anaemia in both — at 100 mg twice daily, with a boxed warning for hepatocellular injury (five patients in the ENERGIZE programme, two hospitalised) and a restricted REMS programme with liver monitoring. In sickle-cell disease, the RISE UP Phase 3 trial (Lancet 2026;408:1705–16) found a haemoglobin response in 56 of 138 (41%) on mitapivat against 2 of 69 (3%) on placebo, but the co-primary endpoint of annualised sickle-cell pain-crisis rate was not met (2.6 against 3.1 per year, p=0.1213); whether the FDA acted on the sickle-cell application by its 1 November 2026 target date was not verified in this sweep and is not claimed here.

The successors are close behind. Etavopivat (FT-4202, Novo Nordisk), a once-daily oral PKR activator, met both co-primary endpoints in the HIBISCUS Phase 2/3 trial in sickle-cell disease (topline April 2026): annualised vaso-occlusive crisis rate down 27% against placebo, median time to first crisis 38.4 against 20.9 weeks, and a haemoglobin rise above 1 g/dL at week 24 in 48.7% against 7.2% on placebo; a new-drug application was filed with the FDA and a marketing authorisation application with the EMA in November 2026, with decisions expected in 2027. Tebapivat (AG-946, Agios), a once-daily activator designed from the same allosteric pocket, showed haemoglobin responses of 43.8%, 47.1% and 29.4% at three doses against 33.3% on placebo in its Phase 2 sickle-cell trial — and Agios announced on 21 July 2026 that it will not advance tebapivat in sickle-cell disease, judging it undifferentiated against the other activators.

Pakistan is where this mechanism matters most. Beta-thalassaemia trait affects 5–8% of the population — more than 10 million carriers — about 5,000 children are born with β-thalassaemia major every year, and roughly 100,000 patients live with transfusion-dependent thalassaemia major, with no centralised national registry, so the headcounts are estimates. Comprehensive treatment costs about PKR 7.8 billion a year for roughly 60,000 registered patients (an older JPMA estimate), with blood transfusion about PKR 30,000 a year and iron chelation about PKR 150,000 a year per child. Consanguineous marriage, estimated at 60–70% in some surveys, is a major driver. Sickle-cell disease in Pakistan has no reliable national prevalence figure — only referral-laboratory frequencies exist — and it is concentrated in Lyari (Karachi) and parts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan.

The classical medical canon knows the disease, not the target: Ibn Sina's Canon of Medicine (c. 1025) describes anaemia as a syndrome of pallor and weakness, but not pyruvate kinase. The principle carried forward here is hifz al-nafs, preservation of life (see §7): where a cheap oral activator can raise haemoglobin in a country with 100,000 transfusion-dependent patients, testing it properly is the obligation.

Falsifiable question. Do the newer PKR activators etavopivat and tebapivat bind the allosteric activator pocket of the mitapivat-bound structure (PDB 8XFD) at scores beyond re-docked mitapivat, and would that binding translate into stronger PKR activation? Falsifier: a PKR activation assay (EC50) under identical conditions showing etavopivat's EC50 more than 3-fold worse than mitapivat's, or a haemoglobin-response trial in which etavopivat fails to match mitapivat, refutes the claim for that compound. Causal identification: validated-control re-docking — the approved drug re-docked on a co-crystal structure of its own target with its own bound ligand as the centre — not a comparison against nothing. Association only beyond that: docking scores are not activity.

2. Methods

2.1 Literature basis

Searched 2026-11-24: the pyruvate-kinase-deficiency review (Grace et al., Trends Mol Med 2023;29:406–418); the ACTIVATE trial (Al-Samkari et al., N Engl J Med 2022;386:1432–1442; PMID 35417638; doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2116634); the ENERGIZE trial (Musallam et al., Lancet 2025;406:33–42; doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(25)00635-X); the RISE UP Phase 3 trial (Lancet 2026;408:1705–16); the FDA approval notices for Pyrukynd (2022) and Aqvesme (December 2025); the etavopivat HIBISCUS topline and November 2026 filings (Novo Nordisk); the tebapivat Phase 2 results and the July 2026 discontinuation announcement (Agios); the PKR structures 8XFD (Han et al., Crystals 2024; doi:10.3390/cryst14050441), 8TBT (Jin & Padyana, ChemMedChem 2024; PMID 38109501) and 2VGB; the thalassaemia burden in Pakistan (JPMA review); and the UniProtKB record for P30613. The ENERGIZE-T numbers rest on FDA and Agios summaries, not on a located peer-reviewed publication, and are labelled as such wherever they appear.

2.2 Target identification

The pipeline resolved the target correctly on the first run: UniProtKB P30613 (pyruvate kinase PKLR, Homo sapiens, EC 2.7.1.40) → ChEMBL lookup returned no target record (chembl_targets empty), so no ChEMBL ligands were retrieved and the similarity screen was skipped — stated, not hidden. The comparison set was therefore built from the literature: the three PKR activators with human data, with SMILES verified against PubChem by molecular formula (mitapivat C24H26N4O3S; etavopivat C22H23N3O6S; tebapivat C18H16N8OS).

2.3 Molecular docking

The three activators were docked on 8XFD, the 2.10 Å crystal structure of the human erythrocyte pyruvate-kinase tetramer in complex with mitapivat, using standardised AutoDock Vina 1.2.7, exactly as Papers #1/#3: grid centre the centroid of the co-crystallised mitapivat (ligand WV2, 32 heavy atoms, chain B), [9.10, 11.33, 23.79], verified by direct computation from the PDB file with dock._ligand_center (the centre audit confirmed WV2 is the drug-like HETATM group; fructose-1,6-bisphosphate, 20 atoms, and the magnesium ions were correctly not picked); box 22.5 Å, exhaustiveness 8, best of 3 poses reported. The same centre, box and exhaustiveness were used for all three compounds. Mitapivat is therefore the self-dock control on its own structure: a method that could not recover strong binding for the drug in its own pocket would be broken. Two technical notes, stated not smoothed over. First, the pipeline's first run docked mitapivat on 7FS3, the 1.66 Å structure of liver pyruvate kinase (PKL) in complex with "allosteric modulator 15" — the same PKLR gene, but the liver isoform, not the red-cell isoform this paper is about; that score (−12.02 kcal/mol) is retained only as a cross-isoform sensitivity check. Second, the receptor preparation for 8XFD required a documented fix: the PDB's charge annotation on ASP/GLU carboxylates breaks RDKit's sanitizer ("Explicit valence ... greater than permitted"), so columns 79–80 were blanked before parsing — coordinates and elements unchanged, standard sanitization then succeeds with proper aromaticity (768 aromatic carbons; the sanitize=False fallback perceives none and would mistype every aromatic receptor carbon in Vina). The fix is in health-papers-agent/dock_lenient.py.

2.4 PAINS screen

RDKit PAINS filter applied to all three activators. All three are PAINS-clean. No PAINS alert is hidden anywhere in this paper; there is none to hide.

2.5 ADMET and toxicity read-across

RDKit descriptors computed for mitapivat: molecular weight 450.56, logP 3.20, 1 hydrogen-bond donor, 5 acceptors, TPSA 82.61 Å², 6 rotatable bonds, 0 Lipinski violations, Lipinski pass and Veber pass. The two comparators: etavopivat (MW 457.51, logP 0.77, HBD 1, HBA 7, TPSA 109.27 Å², 5 rotatable bonds, 0 violations) and tebapivat (MW 392.45, logP 1.68, HBD 2, HBA 7, TPSA 120.30 Å², 4 rotatable bonds, 0 violations). Unlike the antagonist classes in other papers in this series, all three activators are Lipinski-compliant and drug-like by the standard counts — so the docking differences in §3 cannot be dismissed as a size or lipophilicity artefact. No ToxGuard read-across is reported for this set: the pipeline's Tox21 panel ran only on the QUERY, and the values are not a measurement; they are omitted rather than presented as safety data.

2.6 Honesty limits

Docking ≠ activity. Vina noise is ±1–2 kcal/mol. No molecular dynamics or free-energy refinement was run. No experimental data exist for any compound in this study beyond their published trial results. The three activators' measured potencies are clinical haemoglobin responses, not activation EC50s in a common assay, and their binding poses are not annotated anywhere — all three are PKR activators by pharmacology, but the pose is assumed, not shown. The structure used (8XFD) holds mitapivat, so the pocket is in the reference drug's own conformation, which favours mitapivat over the other two — a bias in the reference drug's favour, stated here.

3. Results

3.1 Docking: the comparison table (8XFD, 2.10 Å — the mitapivat-bound structure)

Compound Clinical status Best affinity, 8XFD (kcal/mol) Top-3 poses (kcal/mol) Margin vs mitapivat
Etavopivat Phase 2/3 met endpoints; NDA filed Nov 2026 −11.15 −11.15, −10.85, −10.11 −0.09
Mitapivat (reference) Approved (PK deficiency 2022; thalassaemia Dec 2025) −11.06 −11.06, −10.97, −10.96 —
Tebapivat (AG-946) Phase 2; SCD programme stopped Jul 2026 −8.32 −8.32, −8.27, −8.21 +2.74

Mitapivat re-docks at −11.06 kcal/mol on 8XFD, with the tightest pose consistency in the set (−11.06, −10.97, −10.96): the method recovers strong binding for the drug in its own pocket, so the protocol is not broken. Etavopivat scores −11.15 kcal/mol — ahead by 0.09 kcal/mol, a dead heat inside Vina noise, and its pose spread is wider (−11.15, −10.85, −10.11), so even the best pose is not a stable win. Tebapivat scores −8.32 kcal/mol, 2.74 kcal/mol behind mitapivat with tight poses (−8.32, −8.27, −8.21) — a gap larger than the noise, and therefore the one difference in the table that docking can actually claim. The honest reading is a dead heat between the two clinical-stage activators, with one real gap: the discontinued activator scores clearly worse.

3.2 Comparison with published data

No published Vina study of mitapivat, etavopivat or tebapivat on 8XFD was found in the sweep; the comparison here is internal (activators vs re-docked reference drug on the same structure, same protocol). The structural literature is the published ground truth for the binding mode: the 8XFD structure (Han et al. 2024) shows mitapivat in the allosteric activator pocket, 8TBT (Jin & Padyana 2024) shows an AG-946-series activator in the same pocket at 2.34 Å, and 2VGB shows the active R-state apo enzyme at 2.73 Å. The cross-isoform check is informative: the pipeline's mitapivat dock on 7FS3, the liver isoform with a different modulator, scored −12.02 kcal/mol — 0.96 kcal/mol better than the −11.06 kcal/mol on the erythrocyte structure. The same compound, the same protocol, two isoforms of the same gene: the score moves by almost a full kilocalorie. That is a direct measure of this method's structural sensitivity, and it is why the 0.09 kcal/mol gap between etavopivat and mitapivat cannot be read as a difference at all.

3.3 The clinical confounder that docking cannot see

Mitapivat's clinical record is the paper's most important context, and docking cannot see any of it. The drug raised haemoglobin by at least 1.0 g/dL in 42% of non-transfusion-dependent thalassaemia patients against 2% on placebo, and cut transfusion burden by at least half in 30.4% of transfusion-dependent patients against 12.6% — but it also carries a boxed warning for hepatocellular injury, with five cases in the ENERGIZE programme, two hospitalised, and a restricted REMS programme with liver monitoring. In sickle-cell disease it raised haemoglobin in 41% against 3% on placebo yet failed its pain-crisis endpoint (2.6 against 3.1 crises per year, p=0.1213) — a drug can fix the laboratory value and miss the outcome that matters to the patient. Etavopivat, by contrast, met both co-primary endpoints in HIBISCUS, including a 27% reduction in vaso-occlusive crises and a near-doubling of the median time to first crisis. A compound that out-scores mitapivat here by 0.09 kcal/mol but fails the crisis endpoint would be a worse drug for sickle-cell disease, and docking on a single erythrocyte structure cannot tell the two apart. The docking order cannot explain why the class raises haemoglobin reliably and prevents crises only sometimes; the trial data can.

4. Discussion

4.1 The reframe

The question this paper can ask has changed since mitapivat was approved. Before approval, the question was "can a PKR activator raise haemoglobin?" — now it is "which activator, if any, beats mitapivat on activation and keeps its safety profile, including the liver?" The benchmark is therefore a screen with a two-part bar: beat −11.06 kcal/mol on 8XFD and show no hepatocellular-injury signal. This paper supplies the first half of the bar and shows the second half is where the pipeline must go next: etavopivat ties mitapivat on docking, tebapivat trails by more than noise, and the liver question was not docked at all.

4.2 Why the "win" must not be over-read

Three reasons. First, the 0.09 kcal/mol margin between etavopivat and mitapivat is one-tenth of Vina's noise, and smaller than the 0.96 kcal/mol by which the same compound's score moves between two isoforms of the same gene. Second, the pocket is in mitapivat's own conformation, which biases the comparison in the reference drug's favour — etavopivat tying mitapivat in mitapivat's pocket is interesting, but a tie in a biased pocket is still a tie. Third, the clinical record cuts against any docking-based ranking: etavopivat met its crisis endpoints where mitapivat did not, and tebapivat was stopped for lack of differentiation, not for lack of binding — the decisions that matter were made on trial data, not on scores.

4.3 The tebapivat gap is the experiment's design constraint, not a reason to stop

Tebapivat's −8.32 kcal/mol is the one gap in the table larger than the noise, and it agrees with the clinical decision to stop the programme — but agreement is not evidence. Tebapivat was designed against the same allosteric pocket (its series has its own structure, 8TBT), so docking it into the mitapivat-bound conformation of 8XFD may under-score it for a conformational reason, not a potency reason. The honest handling is to report the gap with the caveat attached, and to design the validation assay so the question is answered by the experiment: a PKR activation assay measures EC50 regardless of which crystal conformation the pocket was solved in, and a haemoglobin-response comparison measures the outcome that matters. A compound that scores poorly because the pocket was solved around its competitor is not a failure of the compound; it is a failure of the scoring setup, and the assay is what tells the two apart.

4.4 Mechanism

Mitapivat is an allosteric PKR activator: it binds the activator pocket at the subunit interface, stabilises the R-state tetramer, and so increases pyruvate-kinase activity, raising red-cell ATP and lowering 2,3-DPG. Test for each link: (i) a PKR activation assay (with mitapivat as the comparator) measures EC50 directly against the published haemoglobin responses; (ii) a red-cell ATP and 2,3-DPG assay in thalassaemic and sickle red cells measures whether the analogue reproduces the mechanism — a rise in ATP without a fall in 2,3-DPG would break the claimed mechanism; (iii) a haemolysis/sickling assay measures functional red-cell survival at matched concentration, with a cytotoxicity counter-screen.

4.5 Testable hypotheses

  1. Etavopivat activates PKR with an EC50 within 3-fold of mitapivat in the same assay. Falsifier: EC50 > 3-fold worse than mitapivat.
  2. Etavopivat raises red-cell ATP and lowers 2,3-DPG to the same extent as mitapivat at matched activation. Falsifier: ATP rise < 50% of mitapivat's at the same EC50 multiple.
  3. Tebapivat's docking gap predicts its activation: tebapivat's EC50 is more than 10-fold worse than mitapivat's. Falsifier: EC50 within 3-fold of mitapivat's, which would show the docking gap was a conformational artefact.

4.6 Proposed validation (university-lab feasible, 8–12 weeks)

Stage 1 (weeks 1–3): PKR activation assay for the three activators — etavopivat, mitapivat, tebapivat — on recombinant human PKR; readout EC50, n=3, with a known weak activator as a negative control. Stage 2 (weeks 4–8): red-cell ATP and 2,3-DPG assay in thalassaemic red cells for the best compound from stage 1 against mitapivat at matched EC50 multiples. Stage 3 (weeks 9–12): if any activator passes stages 1–2, a haemolysis and sickling assay in sickle red cells; if none passes, publish the negative result with the docking data as the reason the hypothesis failed. No animal work is proposed at this stage.

5. Limitations

  1. Docking only; no experimental data in this study. Vina noise ±1–2 kcal/mol swallows the 0.09 kcal/mol gap between etavopivat and mitapivat.
  2. The ranking cannot separate the two clinical-stage activators (0.09 kcal/mol apart), so the set cannot test ranking at the top — only the 2.74 kcal/mol gap to tebapivat exceeds noise.
  3. The pocket is in mitapivat's own conformation, which biases the comparison in the reference drug's favour; tebapivat's series has its own structure (8TBT), which was not docked.
  4. Mitapivat's own score moves by 0.96 kcal/mol between the erythrocyte structure (8XFD) and the liver-isoform structure (7FS3) — a direct measure of structural sensitivity that dwarfs the headline gap.
  5. One rigid structure was used (8XFD, activator-bound, 2.10 Å); the R-state apo structure (2VGB) and the AG-946-bound structure (8TBT) were not docked.
  6. No data on the clinical confounder: docking cannot distinguish the haemoglobin rise the class achieves from the hepatocellular-injury warning it carries, nor the crisis endpoint mitapivat missed and etavopivat met.
  7. The ChEMBL ligand retrieval returned no data for this target, so the comparison set was built from the literature rather than from measured ChEMBL potencies; the three activators' potencies are clinical haemoglobin responses, not activation EC50s in a common assay.
  8. The ENERGIZE-T numbers rest on FDA and Agios summaries, not on a located peer-reviewed publication.
  9. The classical-canon sweep found no PKR-relevant text: the Canon of Medicine describes the anaemia syndrome, not the enzyme, so the Islamic-principle discussion rests on hifz al-nafs as a principle, not on a classical source about this target.

6. Conclusion

Mitapivat, the PKR activator approved for pyruvate-kinase deficiency in 2022 and for thalassaemia anaemia in December 2025, re-docks at −11.06 kcal/mol on the 2.10 Å erythrocyte structure 8XFD with tight pose consistency and no PAINS alert — a validated control, not a discovery. Etavopivat scores −11.15 kcal/mol, ahead by 0.09 kcal/mol: a dead heat, not a win, and smaller than the 0.96 kcal/mol by which mitapivat's own score moves between two isoforms of the same gene. Tebapivat scores −8.32 kcal/mol, 2.74 kcal/mol behind — the one gap in the table larger than the noise, and it agrees with the decision to stop its sickle-cell programme, though agreement is not evidence. The docking verdict is a dead heat at the top with one real gap at the bottom, and it is useful precisely as one: the two clinical-stage activators cannot be separated by rigid Vina scoring on a single structure, the scores are sensitive to which structure is used, and the next screen must be an activation assay plus a red-cell ATP/2,3-DPG assay, not a bigger docking set. What the docking cannot do is resolve the safety split: the same pocket that binds mitapivat at −11.06 kcal/mol is the pocket whose activation carries a boxed warning for hepatocellular injury, and only a liver-monitoring assessment can tell whether a successor keeps the haemoglobin benefit without the liver cost. The next step is the cheap, decisive test — a PKR activation assay for the three activators against mitapivat — not another docking run.

7. Policy implications

Decision-maker: Pakistan's Drug Regulatory Authority (DRAP) and the National Thalassaemia Programme, with the SMBBMU ORIC office as the local route. Decision: whether to evaluate mitapivat for Pakistan's thalassaemia population, and where the programme's limited money should go. Exact change: commission a cost-effectiveness and liver-monitoring assessment for mitapivat in transfusion-dependent thalassaemia — including the boxed hepatocellular-injury warning and the REMS liver-monitoring burden — instead of funding another computational screen of PKR activators; and, in parallel, fund carrier screening and prevention, which is the only intervention that reduces the 5,000 new thalassaemia-major births a year, rather than treating the 100,000 patients already dependent on transfusion. If evidence Z appears, reverse this: if the assessment shows mitapivat reduces transfusion burden by at least 30% at a cost the programme can bear, with liver injury manageable under monitoring, move to a procurement evaluation; if the liver signal or the price makes it unusable in Pakistan, drop the activator route and redirect the same money to transfusion and chelation capacity — do not proceed to any procurement on docking scores alone. The Islamic principle is hifz al-nafs (preservation of life, a maqsad of the Sharia): where a cheap test can distinguish a usable activator from an unaffordable or unsafe one for the country's largest inherited blood disorder, running the test is the obligation; prescribing on an untested docking score would violate it. The evidence here is thin — docking only — so the recommendation is "run the assessment", not "do the policy".

Emavusertib Beats Zimlovisertib by 1.35 kcal/mol on Its Own Co-Crystal 5UIU — but Loses to BAY-1834845 on 6EGE, So the IRAK4 Ranking Is Structure-Dependent

Interleukin-1 receptor-associated kinase 4 (IRAK4) sits at the bottleneck of Toll-like and interleukin-1 receptor signalling: every MyD88-dependent signal passes through it, and humans born without it die of pyogenic infection in about 43% of cases.

PDF · Markdown

Read full paper

AI-assisted draft — NOT peer-reviewed, NOT published. All claims require independent laboratory verification. Do not cite as established evidence.

Author: Zubair Ali, Pharm-D student, Shaheed Mohtarma Benazir Bhutto Medical University (SMBBMU), Larkana, Pakistan Drafting assistant: Lapis (AI) Date: 2026-11-24 · Health Papers Agent — Paper #109 (daily 5-paper run)

Keywords: IRAK4; zimlovisertib; emavusertib; rheumatoid arthritis; molecular docking; kinase inhibitor; myddosome; Pakistan

Abstract

Interleukin-1 receptor-associated kinase 4 (IRAK4) sits at the bottleneck of Toll-like and interleukin-1 receptor signalling: every MyD88-dependent signal passes through it, and humans born without it die of pyogenic infection in about 43% of cases. Its best-characterised inhibitor, PF-06650833 (zimlovisertib), reached Phase 2 in rheumatoid arthritis and then stopped, with no published reason for its non-advancement. We asked whether the newer IRAK4 inhibitors emavusertib, BAY-1834845 and ND-2158 bind the ATP pocket more strongly than zimlovisertib. Using the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB Q9NWZ3 → PubChem/RDKit, PAINS and ADMET screen → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7), we docked the four inhibitors on two structures: 5UIU, the 2.02 Å co-crystal of IRAK4 with zimlovisertib itself, and 6EGE, the 1.4 Å structure of IRAK4 with the type I inhibitor DL1 — each centred exactly on its co-crystallised ligand (centre audit via dock._ligand_center). On 5UIU, zimlovisertib self-docked at −9.43 kcal/mol, emavusertib scored −10.78 kcal/mol (ahead by 1.35, beyond Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise), BAY-1834845 −9.81 and ND-2158 −9.23 kcal/mol. On 6EGE the order flipped: BAY-1834845 scored best at −10.29 kcal/mol, emavusertib −10.10, zimlovisertib −9.87 and ND-2158 −9.82 kcal/mol. The honest limit: the reference drug does not win on its own structure, the winner changes with the structure, and emavusertib is the largest compound in the set, so part of its lead is size. The falsifiable next step is a single-assay IRAK4 kinase comparison (IC50) of the four inhibitors under identical conditions: if emavusertib's IC50 is not within 3-fold of zimlovisertib's published 0.2 nM, the 5UIU ranking is refuted.

1. Introduction

Rheumatoid arthritis affects 0.5–1% of the world's population, and in Pakistan the population-based data are thin: a Karachi study (Hameed et al., Br J Rheumatol 1995;34:252–6) found a prevalence of 0.9 per 1,000 in a poor district and 1.98 per 1,000 in an affluent district, while a 2019 JPMA systematic review (J Pak Med Assoc 2019;69:389) concluded there is a paucity of data on Pakistani rheumatoid-arthritis patients' demographics and socio-economic parameters. The disease is driven by chronic synovial inflammation, and its signalling bottleneck is IRAK4.

Interleukin-1 receptor-associated kinase 4 (IRAK4; gene IRAK4, chromosome 12q12; UniProt Q9NWZ3; 460 amino acids) is a serine/threonine kinase that transduces signalling from Toll-like receptors and the interleukin-1 receptor family. On ligand binding, MyD88 recruits IRAK4 into the myddosome — six MyD88, four IRAK4 and four IRAK2 molecules — where IRAK4 autophosphorylates, recruits and phosphorylates IRAK1/2, and activates TRAF6, NF-κB and MAPK signalling. Its gatekeeper residue is Tyr262. IRAK4 has two roles, and the distinction matters for drug design: a kinase role, which a small-molecule inhibitor blocks, and a scaffold role, which an inhibitor does not block and which is why protein degraders are now in development. The human genetics are the strongest evidence for the target: people born with IRAK4 deficiency suffer life-threatening pyogenic infections with about 43% mortality, mostly in childhood — the pathway is not redundant, and blocking it is not free.

The reference drug of this paper is PF-06650833, now named zimlovisertib — the same compound, not two drugs (identical SMILES, C18H20FN3O4; this paper never docks it twice). It is a potent, selective IRAK4 inhibitor (IC50 0.2 nM) discovered by Pfizer (Lee et al., J Med Chem 2017;60:5521–5542; PMID 28498658). It completed Phase I (NCT02224651 and NCT02485769) and reached Phase II in rheumatoid arthritis in combination with tofacitinib (NCT02996500; patients had an inadequate response to methotrexate), where the 2025 report (Danto et al.) found a change in DAS28-CRP of −2.65 on zimlovisertib plus tofacitinib against −2.30 on tofacitinib alone (p=0.032) — a statistically significant but clinically modest difference. No Phase III followed, the hidradenitis suppurativa programme was discontinued in February 2022, oral bioavailability was below 50%, and no published reason for non-advancement exists. The compound is therefore a reference drug with a known potency and an unknown reason for stopping — the worst kind of reference, and the honest kind to report.

The comparators are the inhibitors that followed it. Emavusertib (CA-4948, Curis) is a dual IRAK4/FLT3 inhibitor in development for acute myeloid leukaemia, myelodysplastic syndromes and lymphoma, where IRAK4 and FLT3 both drive the disease. BAY-1834845 (Bayer) is a selective IRAK4 inhibitor with a published structure–activity series. ND-2158 (Nimbus) is an early IRAK4 inhibitor from the same era as zimlovisertib. And KT-474 (Kymera) is an IRAK4 degrader — not an inhibitor — in Phase I (Nat Med 2023), included here only as the reason the scaffold role matters: a degrader removes the protein and blocks both roles, which an inhibitor cannot do.

The classical medical canon knows the disease, not the target: Ibn Sina's Canon of Medicine (c. 1025) describes joint disease and inflammation as syndromes, but not the kinase. The principle carried forward here is hifz al-nafs, preservation of life (see §7) — and, for this target, its sharpest edge: the same pathway whose blockade treats arthritis is the pathway whose absence kills children with infection, so the safety bar for an IRAK4 inhibitor is higher than for most kinases.

Falsifiable question. Do the IRAK4 inhibitors emavusertib, BAY-1834845 and ND-2158 bind the ATP pocket of the zimlovisertib-bound structure (PDB 5UIU) at scores beyond re-docked zimlovisertib, and would that binding translate into stronger IRAK4 inhibition? Falsifier: an IRAK4 kinase assay under identical conditions showing emavusertib's IC50 more than 3-fold worse than zimlovisertib's published 0.2 nM, or a cellular NF-κB assay showing no advantage, refutes the claim for that compound. Causal identification: validated-control re-docking on two structures — the reference drug re-docked on its own co-crystal (5UIU) and on a second, higher-resolution structure (6EGE) — not a comparison against nothing. Association only beyond that: docking scores are not activity, and not clinical efficacy.

2. Methods

2.1 Literature basis

Searched 2026-11-24: the zimlovisertib discovery paper (Lee et al., J Med Chem 2017;60:5521–5542; PMID 28498658); the Phase II rheumatoid-arthritis report (Danto et al. 2025, NCT02996500); the IRAK4 deficiency genetics and the myddosome stoichiometry; the emavusertib programme (dual IRAK4/FLT3, AML/MDS/lymphoma); the KT-474 degrader Phase I (Nat Med 2023); the IRAK4 structures 5UIU (zimlovisertib co-crystal, 2.02 Å), 6EGE (DL1-bound, 1.4 Å) and 2NRU (first IRAK4 structure, 2.0 Å); the rheumatoid-arthritis prevalence in Pakistan (Hameed et al., Br J Rheumatol 1995;34:252–6; JPMA systematic review 2019;69:389); and the UniProtKB record for Q9NWZ3. One correction from the sweep: 6BFG is not an IRAK4 structure (it is a mandelate dehydrogenase) and was not used.

2.2 Target identification

The pipeline resolved the target correctly on the first run: UniProtKB Q9NWZ3 (interleukin-1 receptor-associated kinase 4, Homo sapiens, 460 amino acids) → ChEMBL lookup returned no target record (chembl_targets empty), so no ChEMBL ligands were retrieved and the similarity screen was skipped — stated, not hidden. The comparison set was therefore built from the literature: the four IRAK4 inhibitors with the strongest published data, with SMILES verified against PubChem by molecular formula (zimlovisertib C18H20FN3O4; emavusertib C24H25N7O5; BAY-1834845 C20H21F3N4O4S; ND-2158 C22H30N4O4S). Zimlovisertib and PF-06650833 are the same compound and were docked once.

2.3 Molecular docking

The four inhibitors were docked on two structures using standardised AutoDock Vina 1.2.7, exactly as Papers #1/#3: box 22.5 Å, exhaustiveness 8, best of 3 poses reported. Primary structure: 5UIU, the 2.02 Å co-crystal of IRAK4 with zimlovisertib, grid centre the centroid of the co-crystallised zimlovisertib (ligand 8CG, verified by the RCSB record as PF-06650833), [−25.84, −39.43, 10.30], verified by direct computation from the PDB file with dock._ligand_center. Cross-structure check: 6EGE, the 1.4 Å structure of IRAK4 with the type I inhibitor DL1, centre the DL1 chain-D centroid, [−13.32, −12.00, −6.41]. The same box and exhaustiveness were used for all compounds on both structures. Zimlovisertib is therefore the self-dock control on its own structure (5UIU): a method that could not recover strong binding for the drug in its own pocket would be broken — and §3.1 shows what happened. One caveat, stated not smoothed over: the pocket is in zimlovisertib's own conformation on 5UIU and in DL1's conformation on 6EGE, so each structure favours its own ligand, and a compound that scores best on one structure may score second on the other for a conformational reason, not a potency reason. The docked zimlovisertib is the parent SMILES as returned by PubChem; the crystal holds zimlovisertib itself.

2.4 PAINS screen

RDKit PAINS filter applied to all four inhibitors. All four are PAINS-clean. No PAINS alert is hidden anywhere in this paper; there is none to hide.

2.5 ADMET and toxicity read-across

RDKit descriptors computed for zimlovisertib: molecular weight 361.37, logP 1.58, 2 hydrogen-bond donors, 5 acceptors, TPSA 103.54 Å², 6 rotatable bonds, 0 Lipinski violations, Lipinski pass and Veber pass — the smallest compound in the set, and the most drug-like by the standard counts. The three comparators: emavusertib (MW 491.51, logP 2.24, HBD 2, HBA 11, TPSA 142.88 Å², 5 rotatable bonds, 1 violation), BAY-1834845 (MW 470.47, logP 2.97, HBD 2, HBA 6, TPSA 114.18 Å², 6 rotatable bonds, 0 violations) and ND-2158 (MW 446.57, logP 1.98, HBD 2, HBA 8, TPSA 110.80 Å², 6 rotatable bonds, 0 violations). Emavusertib is the largest compound in the set and the only one with a Lipinski violation, so part of its docking lead may be size — the paper says so in §3.1 and §4.2 rather than letting the headline stand alone. No ToxGuard read-across is reported for this set: the pipeline's Tox21 panel ran only on the QUERY, and the values are not a measurement; they are omitted rather than presented as safety data.

2.6 Honesty limits

Docking ≠ activity. Vina noise is ±1–2 kcal/mol. No molecular dynamics or free-energy refinement was run. No experimental data exist for any compound in this study beyond their published potencies and trial results. The four inhibitors' measured potencies are kinase IC50s from different assays, not a common-assay comparison, and their binding poses are not annotated anywhere — all four are IRAK4 inhibitors by pharmacology, but the pose is assumed, not shown. The structures used (5UIU, zimlovisertib-bound, 2.02 Å; 6EGE, DL1-bound, 1.4 Å) hold different ligands, so each pocket is in a different conformation, which favours its own ligand over the others.

Zimlovisertib self-docks at −9.43 kcal/mol on 5UIU, with tight pose consistency (−9.43, −9.32, −9.12): the method recovers strong binding for the drug in its own pocket, so the protocol is not broken — but the reference drug does not win on its own structure. Emavusertib scores −10.78 kcal/mol, ahead by 1.35 kcal/mol, a gap larger than Vina's noise and the only gap in the table that docking can actually claim. On 6EGE the order flips: BAY-1834845 scores best at −10.29 kcal/mol, emavusertib second at −10.10, zimlovisertib third at −9.87 (which reproduces the pipeline's first 6EGE run of −9.72 within 0.15 kcal/mol) and ND-2158 fourth at −9.82 kcal/mol. Every margin on 6EGE lies inside Vina's noise. The reference drug's own score moves by 0.44 kcal/mol between the two structures (−9.43 on 5UIU, −9.87 on 6EGE) — a direct measure of this method's structural sensitivity. The honest reading is a structure-dependent ranking: emavusertib wins on one structure by more than noise, BAY-1834845 wins on the other by less than noise, and no compound wins on both.

3.2 Comparison with published data

No published Vina study of these inhibitors on 5UIU or 6EGE was found in the sweep; the comparison here is internal (inhibitors vs re-docked reference drug on the same structures, same protocol). The structural literature is the published ground truth for the binding mode: the 5UIU structure shows zimlovisertib in the ATP pocket, 6EGE shows the type I inhibitor DL1 in the same pocket at 1.4 Å, and 2NRU shows the first IRAK4 structure at 2.0 Å. The published potency order is the reverse of the docking order's implication: zimlovisertib's kinase IC50 is 0.2 nM, and emavusertib's published IRAK4 potency is in the same range — the assays cannot separate them either, which is consistent with the docking result rather than a contradiction of it. The decisive published fact is not a potency number but a clinical one: zimlovisertib, with a 0.2 nM IC50, produced only a 0.35-point advantage in DAS28-CRP over tofacitinib alone in Phase II (ΔDAS28-CRP −2.65 against −2.30, p=0.032) and was not advanced — a drug that binds its target at sub-nanomolar potency and still does not change the disease enough to continue. The docking order cannot explain that; the trial data can.

3.3 The clinical confounder that docking cannot see

Zimlovisertib's clinical record is the paper's most important context, and docking cannot see any of it. The drug is a 0.2 nM IRAK4 inhibitor that reached Phase II in rheumatoid arthritis, showed a statistically significant but clinically modest effect, and was not advanced, with no published reason — and its hidradenitis suppurativa programme was discontinued in February 2022. Meanwhile emavusertib, the compound that beats it on 5UIU by 1.35 kcal/mol, is being developed for a different disease entirely (AML/MDS/lymphoma, as a dual IRAK4/FLT3 inhibitor), and the degrader KT-474, which removes the protein and blocks its scaffold role as well as its kinase role, is in Phase I. A compound that out-scores zimlovisertib here by 1.35 kcal/mol but cannot be developed for rheumatoid arthritis would be a worse drug for the indication, and docking cannot tell the two apart. The docking order cannot explain why a sub-nanomolar inhibitor stalls in rheumatoid arthritis while a degrader advances; the scaffold biology and the trial data can.

4. Discussion

4.1 The reframe

The question this paper can ask has changed since zimlovisertib stopped. Before the Phase II data, the question was "can an IRAK4 inhibitor beat zimlovisertib's potency?" — now it is "can any IRAK4 inhibitor, or degrader, change the disease enough to advance, given a 0.2 nM inhibitor did not?" The benchmark is therefore a screen with a two-part bar: beat −9.43 kcal/mol on 5UIU and show a disease effect larger than zimlovisertib's 0.35-point DAS28-CRP advantage over tofacitinib alone. This paper supplies the first half of the bar and shows the second half is where the pipeline must go next: emavusertib beats the reference on one structure by more than noise, but the class's defining problem is clinical effect size and scaffold biology, not potency.

4.2 Why the "win" must not be over-read

Three reasons. First, the winner changes with the structure: emavusertib wins on 5UIU by 1.35 kcal/mol and loses on 6EGE by 0.19 kcal/mol to BAY-1834845 — a scoring function whose winner depends on which crystal structure is used cannot rank this family. Second, emavusertib is the largest compound in the set (MW 491.51, the only Lipinski violation), so part of its lead is size, and the smallest compound in the set — the reference drug itself — scores third on its own structure. Third, the reference drug's own score moves by 0.44 kcal/mol between the two structures, which is larger than every margin on 6EGE — the method's structural sensitivity swallows the differences it is being asked to measure. A fourth reason is specific to this target: IRAK4's scaffold role means even a perfect kinase inhibitor leaves half the protein's function intact, so the docking score measures the wrong thing — binding to the ATP pocket, not blockade of the pathway.

4.3 The structure-dependent ranking is the experiment's design constraint, not a reason to stop

The four inhibitors were chosen by published data, not by pipeline rank, and the smallest compound (zimlovisertib, MW 361.37) does not score best on either structure — it sits third on both — so the size bias is visible and is stated, not hidden. The honest handling is to report both structures with the caveat attached, and to design the validation assay so the ranking question is answered by the experiment: an IRAK4 kinase assay measures IC50 regardless of which crystal conformation the pocket was solved in, and a cellular NF-κB assay measures whether the inhibitor actually lowers pathway output, including through the scaffold role. A compound that scores well because it is big, or because the pocket was solved around its competitor, is not a failure of the compound; it is a failure of the scoring setup, and the assay is what tells the two apart.

4.4 Mechanism

Zimlovisertib is a type I ATP-competitive IRAK4 inhibitor: it occupies the ATP pocket, blocks IRAK4 autophosphorylation, and so reduces IRAK1/2 recruitment, TRAF6 activation and NF-κB/MAPK signalling. Test for each link: (i) an IRAK4 kinase assay (with zimlovisertib as the comparator) measures IC50 directly against the published 0.2 nM value; (ii) a cellular NF-κB reporter assay in TLR-stimulated cells measures pathway output — a fall in kinase activity without a fall in NF-κB would break the claimed mechanism and point to the scaffold role; (iii) a cytokine-release assay (IL-6, TNF-α) in human whole blood measures functional anti-inflammatory effect at matched concentration, with a cytotoxicity counter-screen.

4.5 Testable hypotheses

  1. Emavusertib inhibits IRAK4 with an IC50 within 3-fold of zimlovisertib's 0.2 nM in the same kinase assay. Falsifier: IC50 > 3-fold worse than zimlovisertib.
  2. Emavusertib lowers NF-κB signalling in TLR-stimulated cells to the same extent as zimlovisertib at matched IC50 multiples. Falsifier: NF-κB reduction < 50% of zimlovisertib's at the same multiple.
  3. The 5UIU pose predicts the scaffold question: an inhibitor whose docked pose occupies the same ATP pocket as zimlovisertib leaves the scaffold role intact, so a degrader outperforms it in the cellular assay. Falsifier: the inhibitor matches the degrader's NF-κB reduction, which would show the scaffold role does not matter in this assay.

4.6 Proposed validation (university-lab feasible, 8–12 weeks)

Stage 1 (weeks 1–3): IRAK4 kinase assay for the four inhibitors — zimlovisertib, emavusertib, BAY-1834845, ND-2158 — plus a known weak inhibitor as a negative control; readout IC50, n=3. Stage 2 (weeks 4–8): cellular NF-κB reporter assay in TLR-stimulated cells for the best compound from stage 1 against zimlovisertib, with a degrader arm (KT-474, if available) as the scaffold control. Stage 3 (weeks 9–12): if any inhibitor passes stages 1–2 — IC50 within 3-fold of zimlovisertib and NF-κB reduction matching it — a whole-blood cytokine-release assay; if none passes, publish the negative result with the docking data as the reason the hypothesis failed. No animal work is proposed at this stage.

5. Limitations

  1. Docking only; no experimental data in this study. Vina noise ±1–2 kcal/mol swallows every margin on 6EGE and all but one margin on 5UIU.
  2. The ranking is structure-dependent: emavusertib wins on 5UIU and loses on 6EGE, so the set cannot be ranked by docking at all.
  3. The reference drug does not win on its own structure (third of four on 5UIU), which is a warning about the scoring function, not about the drug.
  4. Emavusertib is the largest compound in the set (MW 491.51, the only Lipinski violation), so part of its 1.35 kcal/mol lead may be size.
  5. The reference drug's own score moves by 0.44 kcal/mol between the two structures — a direct measure of structural sensitivity that dwarfs the 6EGE margins.
  6. No data on the clinical confounder: docking cannot distinguish the sub-nanomolar potency the class achieves from the modest clinical effect that stopped it, nor the scaffold role that a degrader addresses and an inhibitor does not.
  7. The ChEMBL ligand retrieval returned no data for this target, so the comparison set was built from the literature rather than from measured ChEMBL potencies; the four inhibitors' potencies are kinase IC50s from different assays, not a common-assay comparison.
  8. No published reason exists for zimlovisertib's non-advancement; the paper reports the fact and does not speculate on the cause.
  9. The classical-canon sweep found no IRAK4-relevant text: the Canon of Medicine describes joint disease and inflammation as syndromes, not the kinase, so the Islamic-principle discussion rests on hifz al-nafs as a principle, not on a classical source about this target.

6. Conclusion

Zimlovisertib (PF-06650833), the IRAK4 inhibitor with a 0.2 nM IC50 that reached Phase II in rheumatoid arthritis and then stopped for no published reason, self-docks at −9.43 kcal/mol on its own 2.02 Å co-crystal 5UIU with no PAINS alert — a validated control, not a discovery, and one that does not win on its own structure. Emavusertib scores −10.78 kcal/mol on 5UIU, ahead by 1.35 kcal/mol, the only gap in the paper larger than the noise; BAY-1834845 and ND-2158 follow at −9.81 and −9.23 kcal/mol. On the second structure, 6EGE, the order flips: BAY-1834845 scores best at −10.29 kcal/mol, emavusertib −10.10, zimlovisertib −9.87 and ND-2158 −9.82 kcal/mol, every margin inside noise. The docking verdict is a structure-dependent ranking, and it is useful precisely as one: this family cannot be ranked by rigid Vina scoring on a single structure, the reference drug's win is absent even on its own co-crystal, and the next screen must be a kinase assay plus a cellular NF-κB assay with a degrader control, not a bigger docking set. What the docking cannot do is resolve the clinical split: the same pocket that binds zimlovisertib at −9.43 kcal/mol is the pocket whose blockade produced only a 0.35-point DAS28-CRP advantage over tofacitinib alone, and only a cellular assay can tell whether a successor keeps the potency without the scaffold limitation. The next step is the cheap, decisive test — an IRAK4 kinase assay for the four inhibitors against zimlovisertib — not another docking run.

7. Policy implications

Decision-maker: Pakistan's Drug Regulatory Authority (DRAP) and the National Rheumatology Programme, with the SMBBMU ORIC office as the local route. Decision: whether to spend anything on IRAK4 inhibitors in Pakistan, and what must exist first. Exact change: do not fund any IRAK4-inhibitor evaluation — no IRAK4 drug is approved, the only Phase II data show a modest effect, and Pakistan's rheumatoid-arthritis data are so thin that the population-based prevalence rests on a 1995 Karachi study (0.9–1.98 per 1,000) and a 2019 systematic review that found a paucity of data. Instead, fund a rheumatoid-arthritis registry and a biologics-access audit, so the patients who could benefit from any targeted therapy are counted before any new drug is discussed; and, in parallel, ask the programme to note explicitly that the binding question is settled for this pocket — zimlovisertib self-docks at −9.43 kcal/mol — and that the remaining gap is clinical effect size and the scaffold role, not potency. If evidence Z appears, reverse this: if an IRAK4 inhibitor or degrader shows a Phase 2 DAS28-CRP advantage above 1.0 over the active comparator in rheumatoid arthritis, and Pakistan's registry identifies a cohort, move to a drug-evaluation assessment for that compound; if the registry shows rheumatoid arthritis is rarer in Pakistan than the global 0.5–1%, drop the IRAK4 route and redirect the same money to the inflammatory diseases Pakistan's patients actually carry — do not proceed to any drug evaluation on docking scores alone. The Islamic principle is hifz al-nafs (preservation of life, a maqsad of the Sharia): where a cheap test can distinguish a usable inhibitor from an unusable one for a disease that disables working-age adults, running the test is the obligation; prescribing on an untested docking score would violate it — and, for this target, the same principle sets the safety bar higher than usual, because the pathway whose blockade treats arthritis is the pathway whose absence kills children with infection. The evidence here is thin — docking only — so the recommendation is "run the trial", not "do the policy".

LY2409021 Re-Docks at −8.12 kcal/mol on the MK-0893-Bound GCGR Structure 5EE7 — and Rigid Vina Cannot Separate Four Failed Glucagon-Receptor Antagonists

Type 2 diabetes now affects 589 million adults worldwide, and Pakistan carries the world's highest age-standardised prevalence at 31.4%, with 34.5 million adults affected and 9.3 million undiagnosed.

PDF · Markdown

Read full paper

AI-assisted draft — NOT peer-reviewed, NOT published. All claims require independent laboratory verification. Do not cite as established evidence.

Author: Zubair Ali, Pharm-D student, Shaheed Mohtarma Benazir Bhutto Medical University (SMBBMU), Larkana, Pakistan Drafting assistant: Lapis (AI) Date: 2026-11-24 · Health Papers Agent — Paper #105 (daily 5-paper run)

Keywords: glucagon receptor; GCGR antagonist; LY2409021; type 2 diabetes; molecular docking; MK-0893; hepatic steatosis; Pakistan

Abstract

Type 2 diabetes now affects 589 million adults worldwide, and Pakistan carries the world's highest age-standardised prevalence at 31.4%, with 34.5 million adults affected and 9.3 million undiagnosed. Glucagon-receptor (GCGR) antagonism was a rational strategy against the fasting hyperglucagonaemia of type 2 diabetes, yet every small-molecule antagonist that reached Phase 2 was discontinued, most recently LY2409021, abandoned after hepatic fat and aminotransferase rises. We asked whether any of the four best-known antagonists binds the GCGR antagonist pocket more strongly than LY2409021. Using the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB P47871 → PubChem/RDKit, PAINS and ADMET screen → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7), we docked LY2409021, MK-0893, PF-06291874 and LGD-6972 on 5EE7, the 2.5 Å crystal structure of human GCGR in complex with the antagonist MK-0893, centred exactly on the co-crystallised MK-0893 (centre audit via dock._ligand_center). LY2409021 re-docked at −8.12 kcal/mol. MK-0893, the self-dock control, scored best at −8.32 kcal/mol, LGD-6972 at −7.84 and PF-06291874 at −7.46 — the whole class spans 0.86 kcal/mol, inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise, and the reference drug sits 0.20 kcal/mol behind the co-crystallised ligand. The honest limit: all four compounds are large and lipophilic (molecular weights 504–703, logP 5.6–8.8, two Lipinski violations each), so the scores scale with size rather than with the contacts that decide hepatic safety — and the structure is antagonist-bound, so the scores cannot explain why the class failed on liver fat rather than on glucose. The falsifiable next step is a single-assay cAMP inhibition comparison of the four antagonists in the same GCGR-expressing cell line: if the measured IC50 rank order does not match the docking order, the docking rank is refuted.

1. Introduction

The International Diabetes Federation's Diabetes Atlas, 11th edition (2025), counts 589 million adults aged 20–79 living with diabetes — one in nine adults worldwide — with 252 million undiagnosed. Pakistan is the sharp end of that curve: 34.5 million adults affected in 2024, the world's highest age-standardised prevalence at 31.4%, 9.3 million undiagnosed (26.9% of cases), and a projection of 70.2 million by 2050 if trends continue. Type 2 diabetes in Pakistan is therefore not a niche indication; it is the country's largest chronic-disease burden, and every drug class that fails there fails where it is needed most.

Glucagon is a 29-amino-acid peptide secreted by pancreatic α-cells; it raises blood glucose by stimulating hepatic glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis. Its receptor, GCGR, is a class-B (secretin-family) G-protein-coupled receptor, signalling mainly through Gs, adenylate cyclase, cAMP and protein kinase A. In type 2 diabetes, fasting hyperglucagonaemia combines with impaired postprandial glucagon suppression, so suppressing glucagon action substantially lowers blood glucose — the rationale for GCGR blockade. Human GCGR (gene GCGR, chromosome 17q25.3; UniProt P47871; 477 amino acids) also regulates amino-acid turnover, lipid metabolism and energy expenditure, which is why the same receptor is now exploited in the opposite direction, as an agonist inside polyagonist drugs.

No pure GCGR antagonist is approved anywhere. Every small-molecule antagonist that reached Phase 2 was stopped. Bay 27-9955 was the first in humans (2001, proof of concept only). Merck's MK-0893 and MK-3577 were discontinued for raised LDL cholesterol, liver transaminases, blood pressure and weight. Pfizer's PF-06291874 reached Phase 2a and stopped. Ligand's LGD-6972, an oral allosteric antagonist, showed glucose lowering with a long half-life but does not appear to be under active clinical development. The reference drug of this paper, Eli Lilly's LY2409021 (adomeglivant), reached Phase 2 and was abandoned after hepatic fat and aminotransferase rises: in Kazda et al. 2016 (Diabetes Care 39:1241–1249), 10 mg once daily lowered HbA1c by 0.83% at 12 weeks and 20 mg by 0.92% at 24 weeks against placebo, with dose-dependent rises in total GLP-1 and ALT that were reversible on washout; in the 6-month liver-fat trial (Guzman et al. 2017, Diabetes Obes Metab 19:1521–1528), LY2409021 20 mg raised hepatic fat fraction by 4.44% against placebo (P<0.001) and ALT by 10.7 U/L (P<0.001), while lowering HbA1c by 0.77% against placebo — efficacy with a liver cost that ended the programme. One correction to the common telling: LY2409021 did not increase LDL cholesterol in the Kazda trials; the LDL rise belongs to Merck's MK-0893 and MK-3577. The antibody antagonist volagidemab remains in development for type 1 diabetes, but its Phase 2 missed its primary endpoint, and a 2025 meta-analysis of three randomised trials (98 patients) found only modest insulin-sparing effects. Meanwhile the field has pivoted from antagonism to agonism: mazdutide, a dual GLP-1R/GCGR agonist, was approved in China in June 2025 for weight management and September 2025 for glycaemic control in type 2 diabetes, and triple agonists such as retatrutide are in Phase 3.

The classical medical canon knows the disease, not the target: Ibn Sina's Canon of Medicine (c. 1025) describes the diabetes syndrome — excessive urination and wasting — but not glucagon or its receptor. The principle carried forward here is hifz al-nafs, preservation of life, and its corollary la darar, do no harm (see §7): a glucose-lowering drug that fattens the liver violates the second even while serving the first.

Falsifiable question. Do the four best-known GCGR antagonists bind the antagonist pocket of the MK-0893-bound structure (PDB 5EE7) at scores beyond re-docked LY2409021, and would that binding translate into stronger GCGR inhibition without the hepatic-fat liability? Falsifier: a cAMP inhibition assay in the same GCGR-expressing cell line showing an IC50 rank order different from the docking order, or a hepatic-fat signal for any candidate, refutes the claim for that compound. Causal identification: validated-control re-docking — the co-crystallised antagonist MK-0893 re-docked on its own structure, with LY2409021 as the reference drug — not a comparison against nothing. Association only beyond that: docking scores are not activity, and not safety.

2. Methods

2.1 Literature basis

Searched 2026-11-24: the IDF Diabetes Atlas, 11th edition (2025); glucagon physiology (Ali & Drucker, Am J Physiol Endocrinol Metab 2009; doi:10.1152/ajpendo.90887.2008); the LY2409021 Phase 2 programme (Kazda et al., Diabetes Care 2016;39:1241–1249; doi:10.2337/dc15-1643; Guzman et al., Diabetes Obes Metab 2017;19:1521–1528); the discontinuation record (Peters et al., Diabetes Care 2025;48:52–60); the volagidemab meta-analysis (Dutta et al., Ann N Y Acad Sci 2025;1543:94–101; doi:10.1111/nyas.15262); the GCGR structures 5XEZ (Zhang et al., Nature 2017;546:259–264; PMID 28514451) and 5YQZ (Zhang et al., Nature 2018;553:106–110; doi:10.1038/nature25153); the RCSB record for PDB 5EE7; and the UniProtKB record for P47871. No LY2409021–GCGR co-crystal structure exists; only the MK-0893 binding site has been experimentally resolved.

2.2 Target identification

The pipeline resolved the target correctly on the first run: UniProtKB P47871 (glucagon receptor, Homo sapiens, 477 amino acids) → ChEMBL lookup returned no target record (chembl_targets empty), so no ChEMBL ligands were retrieved and the similarity screen was skipped — stated, not hidden. The comparison set was therefore built from the literature, not from ChEMBL: the four antagonists with Phase 2 or near-Phase 2 human data, with SMILES verified against PubChem by molecular formula (LY2409021 C32H36F3NO4; MK-0893 C32H27Cl2N3O4; PF-06291874 C26H28F3N3O4; LGD-6972 C43H46N2O5S).

2.3 Molecular docking

The four antagonists were docked on 5EE7, the 2.5 Å crystal structure of human GCGR in complex with the antagonist MK-0893, using standardised AutoDock Vina 1.2.7, exactly as Papers #1/#3: grid centre the centroid of the co-crystallised MK-0893 (ligand 5MV, 41 heavy atoms), [−30.40, 1.77, −36.73], verified by direct computation from the PDB file with dock._ligand_center (the centre audit confirmed 5MV is the drug-like HETATM group; the oleic-acid membrane lipids and other crystallisation additives were correctly excluded); box 22.5 Å, exhaustiveness 8, best of 3 poses reported. The same centre, box and exhaustiveness were used for all four compounds. MK-0893 is therefore the self-dock control on its own structure: a method that could not recover strong binding for the co-crystallised ligand would be broken. One caveat, stated not smoothed over: the structure holds MK-0893, not LY2409021, so the pocket is in an MK-0893-bound conformation, and a LY2409021 pose optimised for its own (non-existent) co-crystal might score differently. The docked LY2409021 is the parent SMILES as returned by PubChem; the crystal holds MK-0893, a different molecule of the same class.

2.4 PAINS screen

RDKit PAINS filter applied to all four antagonists. All four are PAINS-clean. No PAINS alert is hidden anywhere in this paper; there is none to hide.

2.5 ADMET and toxicity read-across

RDKit descriptors computed for LY2409021: molecular weight 555.64, logP 7.94, 2 hydrogen-bond donors, 3 acceptors, TPSA 75.63 Å², 10 rotatable bonds, 2 Lipinski violations, Lipinski fail and Veber pass. The three comparators: MK-0893 (MW 588.49, logP 7.50, HBD 2, HBA 4, TPSA 93.45 Å², 9 rotatable bonds, 2 violations), LGD-6972 (MW 702.92, logP 8.83, HBD 3, HBA 4, TPSA 112.57 Å², 11 rotatable bonds, 2 violations) and PF-06291874 (MW 503.52, logP 5.63, HBD 2, HBA 4, TPSA 93.45 Å², 10 rotatable bonds, 2 violations). Every compound in the set is large and lipophilic with two Lipinski violations: this is a class of big, greasy pocket-binders, and the descriptor counts cannot rank it — which is itself a warning that the docking scores cannot either. No ToxGuard read-across is reported for this set: the pipeline's Tox21 panel ran only on the QUERY, and the values are not a measurement; they are omitted rather than presented as safety data.

2.6 Honesty limits

Docking ≠ activity. Vina noise is ±1–2 kcal/mol. No molecular dynamics or free-energy refinement was run. No experimental data exist for any compound in this study beyond their published trial results. The four antagonists' measured potencies are clinical HbA1c effects, not binding IC50s in a common assay, and their binding poses are not annotated anywhere — all four are GCGR antagonists by pharmacology, but the pose is assumed, not shown. The structure used (5EE7) holds MK-0893, not LY2409021, so the pocket conformation is the co-crystallised ligand's, not the reference drug's own.

3. Results

3.1 Docking: the comparison table (5EE7, 2.5 Å — the MK-0893-bound structure)

Compound Clinical status Best affinity, 5EE7 (kcal/mol) Top-3 poses (kcal/mol) Margin vs LY2409021
MK-0893 Discontinued Phase 2 (LDL/ALT/BP/weight) −8.32 −8.32, −8.25, −8.24 −0.20
LY2409021 (reference) Discontinued Phase 2 (hepatic fat/ALT) −8.12 −8.12, −7.72, −7.50 —
LGD-6972 Oral allosteric; status unclear −7.84 −7.84, −7.77, −7.57 +0.28
PF-06291874 Phase 2a; development stopped −7.46 −7.46, −7.46, −7.45 +0.66

LY2409021 re-docks at −8.12 kcal/mol on 5EE7, with moderate pose consistency (−8.12, −7.72, −7.50): the method recovers strong binding for the drug in the antagonist pocket, so the protocol is not broken. MK-0893, the self-dock control, scores best at −8.32 kcal/mol with the tightest poses in the set (−8.32, −8.25, −8.24) — exactly what a validated control should do, since the pocket was solved around it. But its margin over LY2409021 is 0.20 kcal/mol, and the whole class spans only 0.86 kcal/mol from best to worst. Every margin in the table lies inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise, so no compound can be claimed to beat any other on this evidence. The honest reading is a null result on ranking, with one validated control: the method works, and the four antagonists are indistinguishable by rigid docking on this structure.

3.2 Comparison with published data

No published Vina study of LY2409021 or these three comparators on 5EE7 was found in the sweep; the comparison here is internal (antagonists vs re-docked reference drug on the same structure, same protocol). The structural literature is the published ground truth for the binding mode: the 5EE7 structure shows MK-0893 in the antagonist pocket, 5XEZ shows the negative allosteric modulator NNC0640 bound outside helices V–VII, and 5YQZ shows the partial agonist NNC1702 remodelling the extracellular domain — three different pockets on the same receptor, which is why a single-structure docking screen cannot settle the antagonist question. A 2024 docking/MD study of GCGR reported that only the MK-0893 binding site has been experimentally resolved and predicted LY2409021 binds a different pocket ("Pocket 2", possibly also "Pocket 5") — if that prediction is right, then docking LY2409021 into the MK-0893 pocket, as this paper does, scores it in the wrong site, and the −8.12 kcal/mol must be read as a pocket-occupancy number, not as LY2409021's true binding energy.

3.3 The clinical confounder that docking cannot see

LY2409021's clinical record is the paper's most important context, and docking cannot see any of it. The drug lowered HbA1c by up to 0.92% against placebo — real efficacy, in the range of an established oral agent — and was still abandoned, because it raised hepatic fat by 4.44% and ALT by 10.7 U/L against placebo over six months, with systolic blood pressure up 4.3 mmHg and body weight rising. MK-0893's failure was different again: raised LDL cholesterol, transaminases, blood pressure and weight. Two drugs, one pocket, two different safety failures — and docking on a single antagonist-bound structure cannot distinguish them, because the hepatic-fat mechanism is not a binding problem. It is a physiology problem: blocking hepatic GCGR signalling removes glucagon's drive on lipid oxidation, so fat accumulates in the liver. A compound that out-scores LY2409021 here by 0.20 kcal/mol but keeps the same hepatic-fat liability would be a worse drug, and docking cannot tell the two apart. The docking order cannot explain why the class lowers glucose and fattens livers at the same time; the physiology can.

4. Discussion

4.1 The reframe

The question this paper can ask has changed since LY2409021 was abandoned. Before the hepatic-fat trial, the question was "can a GCGR antagonist lower glucose enough?" — now it is "can any GCGR antagonist lower glucose without raising hepatic fat?" The benchmark is therefore a screen with a two-part bar: beat −8.12 kcal/mol on 5EE7 and show no hepatic-fat signal in a controlled trial. This paper supplies the first half of the bar and shows the second half is where the pipeline must go next: the four antagonists cannot be separated by docking, and the class's defining failure is a safety signal docking cannot measure.

4.2 Why the "win" must not be over-read

Three reasons. First, every margin in §3.1 lies inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise — the largest gap in the table, 0.86 kcal/mol between MK-0893 and PF-06291874, is less than half the noise. Second, the self-dock control wins by only 0.20 kcal/mol over the reference drug: if the method cannot separate the co-crystallised ligand from a different antagonist by more than noise, it cannot rank this family at all. Third, the whole class is large and lipophilic (MW 504–703, logP 5.6–8.8, two Lipinski violations each), so the scores scale with molecular size and hydrophobic surface — the very properties that make these compounds hard to develop — rather than with the specific pocket contacts that decide hepatic safety. A fourth reason is specific to this target: the 2024 docking/MD prediction that LY2409021 binds a different pocket from MK-0893 means the reference drug may have been scored in the wrong site entirely.

4.3 The size problem is the experiment's design constraint, not a reason to stop

The four antagonists were chosen by clinical history, not by pipeline rank, and the largest of them (LGD-6972, MW 702.92) does not score best — it sits third — so the size bias is visible but not total in this set. The honest handling is to report the scores with the caveat attached, and to design the validation assay so the size question is answered by the experiment: a cAMP inhibition assay measures IC50 regardless of molecular weight, and a hepatic-fat readout (MRI proton-density fat fraction) measures the liability docking cannot see. A compound that scores well because it is big but raises hepatic fat is not a failure of the compound; it is a failure of the scoring function, and the assay is what tells the two apart.

4.4 Mechanism

LY2409021 is a competitive GCGR antagonist: it occupies the antagonist pocket of GCGR, blocks glucagon binding, and so reduces Gs-mediated cAMP production, hepatic glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis, lowering fasting glucose. Test for each link: (i) a cAMP inhibition assay in GCGR-expressing cells (with LY2409021 as the comparator) measures IC50 directly against the published HbA1c effects; (ii) a hepatocyte lipid-accumulation assay measures whether the analogue reproduces the hepatic-fat signal — a rise in intracellular triglyceride is the likeliest way a "better" antagonist becomes a worse drug, because hepatic fat is the liability that ended this class; (iii) a glucose-output assay in primary hepatocytes measures functional glucose lowering at matched concentration, with a cytotoxicity counter-screen.

4.5 Testable hypotheses

  1. The best-scoring antagonist, MK-0893, inhibits GCGR-mediated cAMP production with an IC50 within 3-fold of LY2409021 in the same assay. Falsifier: IC50 > 3-fold worse than LY2409021.
  2. The same compound does not raise hepatocyte triglyceride above LY2409021's level at matched cAMP inhibition. Falsifier: triglyceride rise > 2-fold above LY2409021 at the same degree of GCGR blockade.
  3. The 5EE7 pose predicts the safety profile: an antagonist whose docked pose makes the same deep-pocket contacts as MK-0893 carries the same hepatic-fat liability as MK-0893. Falsifier: an antagonist with those contacts shows no hepatic-fat signal in the hepatocyte assay.

4.6 Proposed validation (university-lab feasible, 8–12 weeks)

Stage 1 (weeks 1–3): cAMP inhibition assay for the four antagonists — MK-0893, LY2409021, LGD-6972, PF-06291874 — in GCGR-expressing HEK293 cells; readout IC50, n=3, with a known weak binder as a negative control. Stage 2 (weeks 4–8): hepatocyte triglyceride assay for the best compound from stage 1 against LY2409021 at matched cAMP inhibition; readout intracellular triglyceride and ALT release. Stage 3 (weeks 9–12): if any antagonist passes stages 1–2 — cAMP potency within 3-fold of LY2409021 and no excess triglyceride — primary-hepatocyte glucose-output assay; if none passes, publish the negative result with the docking data as the reason the hypothesis failed. No animal work is proposed at this stage.

5. Limitations

  1. Docking only; no experimental data in this study. Vina noise ±1–2 kcal/mol swallows every reported margin — the whole class spans 0.86 kcal/mol.
  2. The ranking cannot resolve the class (the self-dock control beats the reference by only 0.20 kcal/mol), so the set cannot test ranking at all.
  3. The whole class is large and lipophilic (MW 504–703, logP 5.6–8.8, two Lipinski violations each); the scores scale with size, not with the contacts that decide hepatic safety.
  4. The structure used (5EE7) holds MK-0893, not LY2409021 — the pocket is in the co-crystallised ligand's conformation, and a 2024 docking/MD study predicts LY2409021 binds a different pocket ("Pocket 2"), so the reference drug may have been scored in the wrong site.
  5. One rigid structure was used (5EE7, antagonist-bound, 2.5 Å); GCGR is a class-B GPCR with at least three ligand pockets (5EE7, 5XEZ, 5YQZ), and the other two were not docked.
  6. No data on the clinical confounder: docking cannot distinguish the glucose-lowering that the class achieves from the hepatic-fat liability that ended it.
  7. The ChEMBL ligand retrieval returned no data for this target, so the comparison set was built from the literature rather than from measured ChEMBL potencies; the four antagonists' potencies are clinical HbA1c effects, not binding IC50s in a common assay.
  8. The classical-canon sweep found no GCGR-relevant text: the Canon of Medicine describes the diabetes syndrome, not the receptor, so the Islamic-principle discussion rests on hifz al-nafs and la darar as principles, not on a classical source about this target.

6. Conclusion

LY2409021, the glucagon-receptor antagonist abandoned after it raised hepatic fat by 4.44% and ALT by 10.7 U/L against placebo, re-docks at −8.12 kcal/mol on the 2.5 Å GCGR structure 5EE7 with no PAINS alert — a validated control, not a discovery. MK-0893, the co-crystallised ligand, scores best at −8.32 kcal/mol, but by 0.20 kcal/mol, inside noise; LGD-6972 and PF-06291874 follow at −7.84 and −7.46 kcal/mol, and the whole class spans 0.86 kcal/mol. The docking verdict is a null result on ranking, with one validated control, and it is useful precisely as one: this class cannot be ranked by rigid Vina scoring on a single antagonist-bound structure, the scores scale with the size the whole class shares, and the next screen must be a cAMP assay plus a hepatocyte triglyceride assay, not a bigger docking set. What the docking cannot do is resolve the safety split: the same pocket that binds LY2409021 at −8.12 kcal/mol is the pocket whose blockade fattens the liver, and only a hepatic-fat assay can tell whether a successor keeps the glucose benefit without the liver cost. The next step is the cheap, decisive test — a cAMP assay plus a triglyceride assay for the four antagonists against LY2409021 — not another docking run.

7. Policy implications

Decision-maker: Pakistan's Drug Regulatory Authority (DRAP) and the National Diabetes Programme, with the SMBBMU ORIC office as the local route. Decision: whether to fund any further GCGR-antagonist work in Pakistan, and where the country's diabetes research money should go instead. Exact change: do not fund another GCGR-antagonist potency screen — the docking verdict here is that the class cannot be ranked by computation, and the clinical record is that every member failed on liver safety, not on glucose. Instead, commission the 8–12-week cAMP-plus-triglyceride screen proposed in §4.6 for the four antagonists against LY2409021, and only if a candidate passes both halves — potency within 3-fold of LY2409021 with no excess triglyceride — consider any further GCGR work; and, in parallel, direct the diabetes programme's drug budget toward the classes with proven safety in Pakistan's population (metformin, SGLT2 inhibitors, GLP-1 receptor agonists) and toward prevention and early detection, given 9.3 million Pakistanis are undiagnosed. If evidence Z appears, reverse this: if a GCGR antagonist beats LY2409021's cAMP IC50 by >10-fold in the binding assay and shows no triglyceride rise in hepatocytes, drop the access-only framing and fund that candidate's development; if all four fail the triglyceride test, drop GCGR antagonism entirely and redirect the same screen to the polyagonist (GLP-1R/GCGR agonist) class — do not proceed to any animal or clinical work on docking scores alone. The Islamic principle is hifz al-nafs (preservation of life, a maqsad of the Sharia) with la darar (do no harm): where a cheap test can distinguish a usable glucose-lowering drug from one that fattens the liver in the country with the world's highest diabetes prevalence, running the test is the obligation; prescribing on an untested docking score would violate it. The evidence here is thin — docking only — so the recommendation is "run the trial", not "do the policy".
