AI-assisted draft — NOT peer-reviewed, NOT published. All claims require independent laboratory verification. Do not cite as established evidence.

Author: Zubair Ali, Pharm-D student, Shaheed Mohtarma Benazir Bhutto Medical University (SMBBMU), Larkana, Pakistan Drafting assistant: Lapis (AI) Date: 2026-11-23 · Health Papers Agent — Paper #100 (daily 5-paper run)

Keywords: HIV-1; reverse transcriptase; doravirine; NNRTI; molecular docking; ChEMBL; drug resistance; K103N; Y181C

Abstract

About 40 million people were living with HIV in 2023, and the non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs) remain a backbone of antiretroviral therapy — yet the class's history is a history of resistance: K103N alone defeats efavirenz and nevirapine. Doravirine, a pyridinone NNRTI approved in 2018, was designed to keep activity against those mutants, with published IC50 values of 12 nM (wild-type), 21 nM (K103N), 31 nM (Y181C) and 33 nM (K103N/Y181C), and no viral breakthrough in resistance selections at clinically relevant concentrations where rilpivirine and efavirenz both broke through. We asked whether any measured RT ligand binds the NNRTI pocket more strongly than doravirine. The LeadForge pipeline resolved the target to UniProtKB P03366 (Gag-Pol polyprotein) and ChEMBL CHEMBL5823 — and then failed twice: ChEMBL returned zero bioactivities for CHEMBL5823, so no comparison set exists, and the pipeline's PDB picker selected 2HS1, verified live as the 0.84 Å structure of HIV-1 protease (V32I mutant) with darunavir, not reverse transcriptase — its −9.3 kcal/mol "doravirine" score is a docking into the protease active site and is discarded here as meaningless. On the correct structure, the 3.65 Å cryo-EM wild-type RT/DNA complex with doravirine (PDB 7Z2G), doravirine re-docked at −11.85 kcal/mol (poses −11.85, −11.68, −8.16) centred exactly on the co-crystallised ligand 2KW (centre audit via dock._ligand_center). The paper's finding is therefore a validated control plus two honest negatives: the method recovers strong binding for the drug in its own pocket, but the "does any analogue beat doravirine" question cannot be answered from ChEMBL as queried, and the pipeline's structure picker cannot be trusted on polyprotein targets. The falsifiable next step is a wild-type and K103N/Y181C RT polymerase assay of doravirine against its own published IC50s, with the 7Z2G pose as the structural hypothesis — not another docking run.

1. Introduction

HIV-1 reverse transcriptase (RT) is the enzyme that copies the viral RNA genome into DNA, and it has been a drug target since the first antiretroviral, zidovudine, in 1987. The NNRTIs bind an allosteric hydrophobic pocket — the NNRTI-binding pocket (NNIBP) — about 10 Å from the polymerase active site, and lock the enzyme in a non-productive conformation. The class's weakness is its low genetic barrier: a single substitution, K103N, raises the EC50 of efavirenz more than 50-fold and of nevirapine beyond measurement, and K103N, Y181C and G190A together account for more than 90% of transmitted NNRTI resistance in the United States. Doravirine (formerly MK-1439), a pyridinone NNRTI approved by the FDA in 2018, was designed around that failure: its flexible binding mode keeps hydrogen bonding to Lys101 and hydrophobic contacts to Tyr181, Tyr188, Phe227 and Leu234 even when the pocket mutates. In biochemical assays it inhibits wild-type RT at 4.5 nM and the K103N and Y181C mutants at 5.5 and 6.1 nM; in cell culture with 100% normal human serum its IC50 is 12 nM against wild-type virus, 21 nM against K103N, 31 nM against Y181C and 33 nM against the K103N/Y181C double mutant — and its inhibitory quotients (clinical trough over IC50) of 39, 27 and 25 against those three mutants dwarf rilpivirine's 4.6, 1.4 and 0.8 and efavirenz's 2.5, 60 and 1.9. In resistance selections at clinically relevant concentrations, no viral breakthrough was observed with doravirine against K103N, Y181C, G190A or K103N/Y181C, while breakthrough viruses were readily detected with rilpivirine and efavirenz.

The clinical record since approval supports that design. Through week 192 of the DRIVE-FORWARD and DRIVE-AHEAD phase 3 trials, resistance to doravirine was uncommon — genotypic 1.3%, phenotypic 1.0% — and the mutations that did emerge (most commonly V106A/I/M and F227C) were distinct from the classic NNRTI mutations: K103N, Y181C, K101E, E138K and G190A were not detected in any participant who met resistance-testing criteria. A 2025 real-world study of 102 virologically suppressed patients with past NNRTI resistance-associated mutations switched to doravirine-containing regimens found no virological failure at week 48 (0/87) or week 96 (0/86), even though 25% had documented historical doravirine resistance-associated mutations. The question this paper asks is the standard one for this series: among compounds with measured RT potency already in ChEMBL, does any bind the NNRTI pocket more strongly than doravirine — and can the pipeline even ask that question correctly?

The classical medical canon predates HIV by nine centuries and offers no target for it; the Canon of Medicine (c. 1025) knows no virus. The principle carried forward here is hifz al-nafs, preservation of life (see §7): where a cheap assay can distinguish a usable NNRTI from a useless one, running the assay is the obligation.

Falsifiable question. Do ChEMBL ligands with measured HIV-1 RT potency bind the NNRTI pocket of the doravirine-bound structure (PDB 7Z2G) at scores beyond re-docked doravirine, and would that binding translate into stronger RT inhibition, including against K103N/Y181C? Falsifier: an RT polymerase assay showing an IC50 worse than the analogue's published value, or loss of activity against the K103N/Y181C double mutant, refutes the claim for that compound. Causal identification: validated-control re-docking — the approved drug re-docked on a co-crystal structure of its own target, with the co-crystallised drug as the centre — not a comparison against nothing. Association only beyond that: docking scores are not activity.

2. Methods

2.1 Literature basis

Searched 2026-11-23: the doravirine resistance-suppression study (Lai et al., Antimicrob Agents Chemother 2016; doi:10.1128/AAC.02650-15); the DRIVE-FORWARD/DRIVE-AHEAD week-192 resistance analysis (J Acquir Immune Defic Syndr 2026;101(3):308–315; PMID 41129125); the real-world switch study in patients with past NNRTI mutations (J Antimicrob Chemother 2025;80:810–816; doi:10.1093/jac/dkae481); the doravirine cryo-EM structures (Singh et al., Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 2022;119:e2203660119; PMID 35858448; doi:10.1073/pnas.2203660119); the 2HS1 protease structure paper (Kovalevsky et al., J Mol Biol 2006;363:161–173; PMID 16962136); the RCSB records for PDB 7Z2G and 2HS1; and the UNAIDS 2024 global HIV estimates.

2.2 Target identification

The pipeline resolved the target to UniProtKB P03366 (Gag-Pol polyprotein, HIV-1 group M subtype B, isolate BH10) → ChEMBL CHEMBL5823, "Gag-Pol polyprotein", SINGLE PROTEIN, verified live 2026-11-23. This is the correct protein family but the wrong granularity: Gag-Pol is a 1,447-residue polyprotein that is cleaved into protease, reverse transcriptase and integrase, and the pipeline's downstream steps treated it as one target. That is the root cause of both failures in §2.3–2.4, and the standing fix for this series is now to query viral polyprotein targets by accession of the mature enzyme (for RT, the p66 subunit) rather than by the polyprotein name.

2.3 The pipeline's two failures, stated not smoothed over

First, ChEMBL bioactivity retrieval for CHEMBL5823 returned zero records (step 2: no_data, count 0). No known ligands with measured potency were retrieved, so the similarity screen was skipped and the only "lead" ranked was the query compound itself, doravirine (score 97.5). There is therefore no comparison set in this run, and the question "does any analogue beat doravirine" has no computational answer here. That is a data-retrieval failure, not a finding about doravirine.

Second, the pipeline's PDB picker selected 2HS1 and docked doravirine on it at −9.3 kcal/mol. Verified live 2026-11-23, 2HS1 is the ultra-high-resolution (0.84 Å) crystal structure of the HIV-1 protease V32I mutant in complex with the protease inhibitor darunavir (TMC114) — a different enzyme, a different pocket, a different drug class. A −9.3 kcal/mol score for an NNRTI in a protease active site is a property of the wrong protein and is discarded in full: it appears in this paper only as the artefact it is, with its file reference, so that no reader mistakes it for a result. The same polyprotein-granularity error has bitten this series before (Paper #95, HBV polymerase resolved to a human helicase), and the lesson is the same: the pipeline's structure pick must be verified against the target enzyme by hand, every run.

2.4 Molecular docking — the redock on the correct structure

The benchmark structure is 7Z2G: the cryo-EM structure of wild-type HIV-1 RT with a DNA aptamer in complex with doravirine, 3.65 Å (Singh et al., PNAS 2022). A targeted redock script (health-papers-agent/redock_hp088_7z2g.py) docked doravirine on 7Z2G using standardised AutoDock Vina 1.2.7, exactly as Papers #1/#3: grid centre the centroid of the co-crystallised doravirine (ligand 2KW, 29 heavy atoms — C17H11ClF3N5O3, matching doravirine), [72.10, 82.05, 65.58], verified by direct computation from the PDB file with dock._ligand_center (the centre audit confirmed 2KW is the largest drug-like HETATM group in the file; the two 21-atom OMC groups are modified nucleotides of the DNA aptamer, correctly excluded); box 22.5 Å, exhaustiveness 8, best of 3 poses reported. The receptor preparation keeps the DNA aptamer ATOM records, so the NNRTI pocket is realistic — the primer grip and the YMDD motif sit in their doravirine-bound, non-productive conformation, and removing the DNA would have left a hole where the pocket actually sits. Doravirine is therefore the self-dock control on its own structure: a method that could not recover strong binding for the drug in the pocket it was crystallised in would be broken. The docked doravirine is the parent SMILES as returned by PubChem (CID 58460047); the crystal holds the same molecule, so no prodrug/metabolite caveat applies here (unlike Paper #96, sofosbuvir).

2.5 PAINS screen

RDKit PAINS filter applied to doravirine. PAINS-clean: no alerts. No PAINS alert is hidden anywhere in this paper; there is none to hide.

2.6 ADMET and toxicity read-across

RDKit descriptors computed for doravirine: molecular weight 425.75, logP 2.65, 1 hydrogen-bond donor, 5 acceptors, TPSA 105.7 Å², 4 rotatable bonds, 0 Lipinski violations, Lipinski pass and Veber pass. ToxGuard Tox21 kNN read-across (12 assays) for doravirine: maximum predicted probability 0.328 (SR-ARE), a weak read-across (maximum neighbour similarity 0.241), not a measurement, and it does not clear the compound for development — it is the profile of an already-approved drug, reported for completeness.

2.7 Honesty limits

Docking ≠ activity. Vina noise is ±1–2 kcal/mol. No molecular dynamics or free-energy refinement was run. No experimental data exist for any compound in this study beyond doravirine's published IC50s. There is no comparison set: ChEMBL returned zero bioactivities for CHEMBL5823, so the benchmark question is unanswered, not answered in the negative. One rigid cryo-EM structure was used (7Z2G, 3.65 Å); the NNRTI pocket is flexible and adapts to different chemotypes, so one structure under-samples the binding landscape. The third pose (−8.16 kcal/mol) sits 3.7 kcal/mol above the best pose, so the pose ensemble is not tight.

3. Results

3.1 Docking: the comparison table (7Z2G, 3.65 Å — the drug's own structure)

Compound Measured RT potency (published) Best affinity, 7Z2G (kcal/mol) Top-3 poses (kcal/mol) Median pose
Doravirine (reference) IC50 12 nM (WT); 21 nM (K103N); 31 nM (Y181C); 33 nM (K103N/Y181C) −11.85 −11.85, −11.68, −8.16 −11.68
(no comparison ligands — ChEMBL returned 0 bioactivities for CHEMBL5823) — — — —

Doravirine re-docks at −11.85 kcal/mol on its own structure, with the top two poses tight (−11.85, −11.68): the method recovers strong binding for the drug in the pocket it was crystallised in, so the protocol is not broken. There is no analogue to compare it against, so no "beats doravirine" claim can be made in either direction. The discarded pipeline score (−9.3 kcal/mol on 2HS1, HIV-1 protease + darunavir) is not in the table, because it is not a measurement of this target.

3.2 Comparison with published data

No published Vina study of doravirine on 7Z2G was found in the sweep; the comparison here is internal (the drug re-docked on its own structure, same protocol as Papers #1/#3). The structural literature is the published ground truth for the binding mode: the 7Z2G cryo-EM structure shows doravirine in the NNIBP with its triazole hydrogen-bonded to Lys101 and its chlorobenzonitrile and trifluoromethyl groups in hydrophobic contact with Tyr181, Tyr188, Phe227 and Leu234, and shows the DNA primer 3′-end positioned at the active site in a non-productive state — the structural basis for the drug's retained activity against K103N and Y181C, whose side chains do not contact the drug's flexible core. The mutant structure 7Z2H (E138K/M184I RT/DNA + doravirine, 3.58 Å, same paper) shows the E138K mutation opening the pocket entrance, which the authors link to faster dissociation of rilpivirine — a mechanism doravirine's binding mode partly avoids.

3.3 The clinical confounder that docking cannot see

Doravirine's clinical record is the paper's most important context, and docking cannot see any of it. The drug's value is not that it binds RT more tightly than its predecessors — it is that it keeps binding when the pocket mutates, and that through 192 weeks of phase 3 follow-up only 1.3% of treated patients developed genotypic resistance, with the classic K103N/Y181C/G190A mutations never appearing. The real-world switch study makes the same point from the other side: patients whose viruses already carried NNRTI mutations, switched to doravirine while suppressed, did not fail. A compound that out-scores doravirine here by 1 kcal/mol but loses activity against K103N/Y181C would be a worse drug, and docking on a wild-type structure cannot tell the two apart. The docking order cannot explain why the drug's resistance barrier is high; the structure and the trial data together can.

4. Discussion

4.1 The reframe

The question this paper can ask has changed since doravirine was approved. Before approval, the question was "can an NNRTI keep activity against K103N and Y181C?" — now it is "which molecule, if any, beats doravirine on the wild-type pocket and keeps its mutant profile?" The benchmark is therefore a screen for successors with a two-part bar: beat −11.85 kcal/mol on 7Z2G and keep activity against K103N/Y181C. This paper supplies the first half of the bar and shows the second half is where the pipeline must be fixed before it can supply the first: the comparison set does not exist in ChEMBL as queried, and the structure picker chose a protease.

4.2 Why the "win" must not be over-read

There is no win to over-read. Three reasons the paper is a control plus two negatives, not a discovery. First, there is no comparison set — ChEMBL returned zero bioactivities for CHEMBL5823. Second, the pipeline's first structure was the wrong enzyme entirely, and the −9.3 kcal/mol it produced must be discarded, not averaged in. Third, even the valid re-dock is a single rigid structure at 3.65 Å cryo-EM resolution, and the third pose sits 3.7 kcal/mol above the best, so the pose ensemble is not tight.

4.3 The pipeline failure is the experiment's design constraint, not a reason to stop

The two failures have the same root cause and the same fix. The polyprotein granularity (P03366 → CHEMBL5823) broke both the ligand retrieval and the structure pick. The fix, now standing practice for this series: query viral polyprotein targets by the mature enzyme's accession (RT p66), verify the ChEMBL target's bioactivity count before docking, and verify the picked PDB entry's title against the target enzyme by hand before any score is reported. A pipeline that docks the right drug into the wrong enzyme and reports the number is worse than a pipeline that reports nothing — this paper reports the nothing, with the artefact named.

4.4 Mechanism

Doravirine binds the NNIBP ~10 Å from the polymerase active site, hydrogen-bonded to Lys101, and locks RT in a non-productive conformation with the DNA primer 3′-end mispositioned at the active site. Test for each link: (i) an RT polymerase assay (primer-extension, with doravirine as the comparator) measures IC50 directly against the published 12 nM wild-type value; (ii) the same assay on K103N, Y181C and K103N/Y181C mutant RT measures whether a candidate kept the resistance barrier that defines the class — loss of activity against the double mutant is the likeliest way a "better" NNRTI becomes a worse drug; (iii) a cell-based antiviral assay in the presence of human serum measures EC50 against doravirine at matched concentration, with a cytotoxicity counter-screen.

4.5 Testable hypotheses

  1. Doravirine inhibits wild-type HIV-1 RT in a polymerase assay with an IC50 within 3-fold of its published 12 nM value. Falsifier: IC50 > 3-fold worse than published.
  2. A candidate NNRTI that out-scores doravirine on 7Z2G keeps activity against K103N/Y181C mutant RT within 5-fold of wild-type. Falsifier: >10-fold loss against the double mutant.
  3. The 7Z2G pose predicts the resistance profile: a candidate whose docked pose loses the Lys101 hydrogen bond loses activity against K103N first. Falsifier: a candidate without the Lys101 contact keeps wild-type potency against K103N.

4.6 Proposed validation (university-lab feasible, 8–12 weeks)

Stage 1 (weeks 1–3): fix the pipeline query (mature-enzyme accession, verified ChEMBL bioactivity count, hand-verified PDB title) and re-run the ligand retrieval for HIV-1 RT to build the comparison set this paper could not — five ChEMBL RT ligands with measured potency, docked on 7Z2G at the audited centre. Stage 2 (weeks 4–8): RT polymerase primer-extension assay for doravirine against its published IC50s, plus the best-scoring candidate from stage 1, on wild-type and K103N/Y181C mutant RT. Stage 3 (weeks 9–12): if any candidate passes stages 1–2, cell-based antiviral assay in human serum plus a cytotoxicity counter-screen; if none passes, publish the negative result with the docking data as the reason the hypothesis failed. No animal work is proposed at this stage.

5. Limitations

  1. Docking only; no experimental data in this study. Vina noise ±1–2 kcal/mol swallows any margin under ~2 kcal/mol.
  2. There is no comparison set: ChEMBL returned zero bioactivities for CHEMBL5823, so the benchmark question is unanswered.
  3. The pipeline's first structure (2HS1) was HIV-1 protease, not RT; the −9.3 kcal/mol score on it is discarded, and the pipeline's structure picker needs independent verification every run.
  4. One rigid cryo-EM structure was used (7Z2G, 3.65 Å); the NNRTI pocket is flexible, and the third pose sits 3.7 kcal/mol above the best, so the pose ensemble is not tight.
  5. Docking was on the wild-type structure only; the K103N/Y181C resistance question — the one that matters clinically — was not docked, because no mutant RT structure with a candidate ligand was in the comparison set.
  6. No data on the clinical confounder: docking cannot distinguish the 1.3% genotypic resistance rate from the >90% transmitted-resistance share of K103N/Y181C/G190A.
  7. The classical-canon sweep found no HIV-relevant text: the Canon of Medicine predates the virus by nine centuries, so the Islamic-principle discussion rests on hifz al-nafs as a principle, not on a classical source about this disease.

6. Conclusion

Doravirine, the pyridinone NNRTI designed to survive K103N and Y181C, re-docks at −11.85 kcal/mol on its own 3.65 Å cryo-EM structure 7Z2G with tight top-two pose consistency and no PAINS alert — a validated control, not a discovery. No analogue can be claimed to beat it or lose to it: ChEMBL returned zero bioactivities for the pipeline's target CHEMBL5823, so there is no comparison set, and the pipeline's first structure was HIV-1 protease with darunavir, whose −9.3 kcal/mol score is discarded as a measurement of the wrong enzyme. The paper's useful result is therefore the control plus the two named failures: the method works on the right structure, the query path does not, and the fix — mature-enzyme accession, verified bioactivity count, hand-verified PDB title — is specified so the next run can ask the question this one could not. What the docking cannot do is resolve the resistance question that defines this drug: the same NNRTI pocket that binds doravirine at −11.85 kcal/mol is the pocket whose K103N and Y181C mutations defeat the older drugs, and only a mutant-RT assay can tell whether a successor keeps doravirine's barrier. The next step is the cheap, decisive test — fix the query, build the comparison set, and run a wild-type plus K103N/Y181C polymerase assay — not another docking run on an unverified structure.

7. Policy implications

Decision-maker: Pakistan's National AIDS Control Programme and the DRAP registration office, with the SMBBMU ORIC office as the local route. Decision: whether to fund a small, targeted validation of NNRTI benchmarking as an academic drug-discovery exercise, and whether to prioritise doravirine-containing regimens in procurement for patients with prior NNRTI exposure. Exact change: commission the 8–12-week pipeline-fix plus polymerase screen proposed in §4.6 for the five best ChEMBL RT ligands against doravirine, instead of funding another purely computational screen of the same target on unverified structures; and, in parallel, ask the AIDS programme to note explicitly that the binding question is settled for the wild-type pocket — doravirine re-docks at −11.85 kcal/mol — and that the remaining gap is the mutant pocket and the comparison set, not the drug's potency: every rupee spent re-docking doravirine into the wrong enzyme is a rupee not spent testing candidates against K103N/Y181C. If evidence Z appears, reverse this: if a candidate beats doravirine's re-dock by >2 kcal/mol on 7Z2G and keeps activity against K103N/Y181C within 5-fold, drop the access-only framing and fund the candidate's development; if the fixed query returns no candidate within noise of doravirine, drop this ligand set and redirect the same screen to the next NNRTI chemotypes — do not proceed to any animal or clinical work on docking scores alone. The Islamic principle is hifz al-nafs (preservation of life, a maqsad of the Sharia): where a cheap test can distinguish a usable NNRTI from a useless one for a disease affecting about 40 million people, running the test is the obligation; prescribing on an untested docking score would violate it. The evidence here is thin — docking only, and a single-compound control at that — so the recommendation is "run the trial", not "do the policy".

PC190723 Re-Docks at −9.43 kcal/mol on Its Own FtsZ Structure 4DXD — but the Pipeline Docked It into the GDP Pocket, and ChEMBL Resolved FtsZ to a Human Enzyme

Staphylococcus aureus was associated with more than a million deaths in 2019, and methicillin-resistant strains with more than 100,000 deaths directly attributable to resistance — yet no FtsZ inhibitor has reached the clinic.

PDF · Markdown

Read full paper

AI-assisted draft — NOT peer-reviewed, NOT published. All claims require independent laboratory verification. Do not cite as established evidence.

Author: Zubair Ali, Pharm-D student, Shaheed Mohtarma Benazir Bhutto Medical University (SMBBMU), Larkana, Pakistan Drafting assistant: Lapis (AI) Date: 2026-11-23 · Health Papers Agent — Paper #101 (daily 5-paper run)

Keywords: Staphylococcus aureus; FtsZ; PC190723; MRSA; molecular docking; ChEMBL; cell division; antimicrobial resistance

Abstract

Staphylococcus aureus was associated with more than a million deaths in 2019, and methicillin-resistant strains with more than 100,000 deaths directly attributable to resistance — yet no FtsZ inhibitor has reached the clinic. FtsZ, the essential bacterial GTPase that builds the Z-ring at the division site, is the target of PC190723, a 2,6-difluorobenzamide that stabilises FtsZ polymers, suppresses its GTPase activity, and kills staphylococci at a minimum inhibitory concentration of 1 µg/mL against both methicillin-sensitive and methicillin-resistant strains. We asked whether any measured FtsZ ligand binds the interdomain cleft more strongly than PC190723. The LeadForge pipeline resolved the target correctly to UniProtKB P0A029 (S. aureus FtsZ) — and then failed twice: ChEMBL resolved to CHEMBL2074, verified live as human maltase-glucoamylase, so zero bioactivities were returned and no comparison set exists; and the pipeline's PDB picker selected 3VOA, the GDP-form of FtsZ, whose centre is the nucleotide site, not the PC190723 cleft — its −8.83 kcal/mol score is a docking into the GDP pocket and is discarded here as a measurement of the wrong site. On the correct structure, the 2.0 Å crystal structure of S. aureus FtsZ in complex with PC190723 (PDB 4DXD), PC190723 re-docked at −9.43 kcal/mol (poses −9.43, −9.37, −9.16) centred exactly on the co-crystallised ligand 9PC (centre audit via dock._ligand_center, which correctly excluded the 28-atom GDP cofactor in favour of the 23-atom inhibitor). The paper's finding is therefore a validated control plus two honest negatives: the method recovers strong, tight binding for the drug in its own cleft, but the "does any analogue beat PC190723" question cannot be answered from ChEMBL as queried, and the pipeline's structure picker cannot be trusted when a structure holds both a nucleotide and an inhibitor. The falsifiable next step is a GTPase-plus-polymerisation assay of PC190723 against its own published MIC, with the 4DXD pose as the structural hypothesis — not another docking run.

1. Introduction

FtsZ is the most conserved protein in bacteria and archaea, and the first protein to arrive at the future division site, where it polymerises in a GTP-dependent manner into the Z-ring that recruits the divisome and guides septum synthesis. It is a structural homologue of eukaryotic tubulin, and its inhibitors work by the same logic as taxol: not by blocking assembly, but by stabilising polymers against disassembly. PC190723 — 3-[(6-chloro[1,3]thiazolo[5,4-b]pyridin-2-yl)methoxy]-2,6-difluorobenzamide — was built from the weak fragment 3-methoxybenzamide through 2,6-difluoro-3-alkyloxybenzamide optimisation, gaining roughly 8,000-fold in potency over the parent fragment, and it inhibits S. aureus at a minimum inhibitory concentration of 1 µg/mL against both methicillin-sensitive and methicillin-resistant strains. It binds the cleft between the N-terminal GTP-binding subdomain and the C-terminal subdomain — the pocket mapped by resistance mutations, the taxol-site equivalent in tubulin — where it stabilises single-stranded filaments into bundles, coils and toroids, reduces GTPase activity, and suppresses the polymer dynamics that division requires. It does not affect Escherichia coli, whose FtsZ is not susceptible, which is the Gram-positive selectivity question that has followed the class ever since.

The clinical case for the target is the synergy, not the single agent. PC190723 acts synergistically with β-lactam antibiotics in vitro and in vivo: in a murine model of MRSA infection the combination was efficacious, fluorescence microscopy showed the concomitant delocalisation of FtsZ and its β-lactam target PBP2, and combining PC190723 with imipenem markedly reduced the spontaneous frequency of PC190723-resistant mutants — while the resistant mutants that did arise showed attenuated virulence and restored β-lactam susceptibility. That is the design logic for a combination agent: the inhibitor's own resistance problem is mitigated by the partner drug. Despite that, no FtsZ inhibitor has reached the clinic: the benzamide class has struggled with pharmacological properties and a relatively high frequency of resistance mutations, and only one prodrug analogue, TXA709, was designated a Qualified Infectious Disease Product for S. aureus infections and has completed a phase I clinical trial. The question this paper asks is the standard one for this series: among compounds with measured FtsZ potency already in ChEMBL, does any bind the interdomain cleft more strongly than PC190723 — and can the pipeline even ask that question correctly?

The classical medical canon knows the wound, not the bacterium: Ibn Sina's Canon of Medicine (c. 1025) treats wounds, abscesses and putrefaction with drainage and dressings — the syndrome, not the target. The principle carried forward here is hifz al-nafs, preservation of life (see §7).

Falsifiable question. Do ChEMBL ligands with measured S. aureus FtsZ potency bind the interdomain cleft of the PC190723-bound structure (PDB 4DXD) at scores beyond re-docked PC190723, and would that binding translate into stronger FtsZ inhibition and antistaphylococcal activity? Falsifier: a GTPase or polymerisation assay showing an IC50 worse than the analogue's published value, or a whole-cell MIC above 4 µg/mL against MRSA, refutes the claim for that compound. Causal identification: validated-control re-docking — the reference inhibitor re-docked on a co-crystal structure of its own target, with the co-crystallised inhibitor as the centre — not a comparison against nothing. Association only beyond that: docking scores are not activity.

2. Methods

2.1 Literature basis

Searched 2026-11-23: the PC190723 discovery paper (Haydon et al., Science 2008;321:1673–1675; doi:10.1126/science.1159961); the FtsZ polymer-stabilisation mechanism (J Biol Chem 2010); the MRSA synergy and 4DXD structure paper (Tan et al., Sci Transl Med 2012;4:126ra35; PMID 22440737; doi:10.1126/scitranslmed.3003592); the SaFtsZ conformational-change structures (Matsui et al., Acta Crystallogr D Biol Crystallogr 2012;68:1175–1188; PMID 22948918); the allosteric-site fluorescence-polarisation screen and TXA709 phase I status (J Med Chem 2021; doi:10.1021/acs.jmedchem.0c02207); the 2,6-difluorobenzamide structure–activity review (ChemMedChem 2017;12:1303–1318); the global antimicrobial-resistance burden analysis (Antimicrobial Resistance Collaborators, Lancet 2022;399:629–655); and the RCSB records for PDB 4DXD and 3VOA.

2.2 Target identification

The pipeline resolved the target to UniProtKB P0A029 (cell division protein FtsZ, Staphylococcus aureus strain Mu50 / ATCC 700699), verified live 2026-11-23. This is the correct target. What failed was the ChEMBL resolution: the pipeline selected CHEMBL2074, verified live as "Maltase-glucoamylase", SINGLE PROTEIN, Homo sapiens — a human digestive enzyme with nothing to do with bacterial cell division. The standing fix for this series is now to verify the ChEMBL target's name and organism before any ligand retrieval is trusted.

2.3 The pipeline's two failures, stated not smoothed over

First, ChEMBL bioactivity retrieval for the wrong target CHEMBL2074 returned zero records (step 2: no_data, count 0). No known ligands with measured potency were retrieved, so the similarity screen was skipped and the only "lead" ranked was the query compound itself, PC190723 (score 99.2). There is therefore no comparison set in this run, and the question "does any analogue beat PC190723" has no computational answer here. That is a data-retrieval failure, not a finding about PC190723.

Second, the pipeline's PDB picker selected 3VOA and docked PC190723 on it at −8.83 kcal/mol. Verified live 2026-11-23, 3VOA is the GDP-form of SaFtsZ (residues 12–316), 1.73 Å — the structure that shows the straight, GDP-bound conformation, with no inhibitor bound. The centre the pipeline used is the GDP nucleotide site: PC190723 was docked into the GTP/GDP pocket, ~25 Å from the interdomain cleft where it actually binds. A −8.83 kcal/mol score for a cleft binder in the nucleotide pocket is a property of the wrong site and is discarded in full: it appears in this paper only as the artefact it is, with its file reference, so that no reader mistakes it for a result. The same structure-picker error has now bitten this series three times in two days (Papers #95, #100, #101), and the lesson is the same: the picked PDB entry's title and bound ligands must be verified by hand, every run.

2.4 Molecular docking — the redock on the correct structure

The benchmark structure is 4DXD: the 2.0 Å crystal structure of S. aureus FtsZ in complex with PC190723 (Tan et al., Sci Transl Med 2012). A targeted redock script (health-papers-agent/redock_hp090_4dxd.py) docked PC190723 on 4DXD using standardised AutoDock Vina 1.2.7, exactly as Papers #1/#3: grid centre the centroid of the co-crystallised PC190723 (ligand 9PC, 23 heavy atoms — C14H8ClF2N3O2S, matching PC190723), [−13.76, 41.85, 18.24], verified by direct computation from the PDB file with dock._ligand_center. The centre audit is the decisive check here: the file also holds a 28-atom GDP cofactor, and a naive largest-group pick would have centred on GDP ([5.03, 20.08, 21.23]) — the nucleotide site again. dock._ligand_center correctly excluded the GDP cofactor and returned the 9PC centroid, which is why this redock measures the cleft and the pipeline's 3VOA run did not. Box 22.5 Å, exhaustiveness 8, best of 3 poses reported. The receptor preparation keeps the GDP ATOM records, so the nucleotide pocket stays occupied and the cleft geometry is realistic. PC190723 is therefore the self-dock control on its own structure: a method that could not recover strong binding for the drug in the cleft it was crystallised in would be broken. The docked PC190723 is the parent SMILES as returned by PubChem (CID 25016417); the crystal holds the same molecule, so no prodrug/metabolite caveat applies here.

2.5 PAINS screen

RDKit PAINS filter applied to PC190723. PAINS-clean: no alerts. No PAINS alert is hidden anywhere in this paper; there is none to hide.

2.6 ADMET and toxicity read-across

RDKit descriptors computed for PC190723: molecular weight 355.75, logP 3.3, 1 hydrogen-bond donor, 5 acceptors, TPSA 78.1 Å², 4 rotatable bonds, 0 Lipinski violations, Lipinski pass and Veber pass. ToxGuard Tox21 kNN read-across (12 assays) for PC190723: maximum predicted probability 0.168 (NR-AhR), a weak read-across (maximum neighbour similarity 0.279), not a measurement, and it does not clear the compound for development — it is the profile of an investigational compound, reported for completeness.

2.7 Honesty limits

Docking ≠ activity. Vina noise is ±1–2 kcal/mol. No molecular dynamics or free-energy refinement was run. No experimental data exist for any compound in this study beyond PC190723's published MIC. There is no comparison set: ChEMBL returned zero bioactivities for the wrongly resolved target, so the benchmark question is unanswered, not answered in the negative. One rigid structure was used (4DXD, 2.0 Å); FtsZ undergoes marked conformational change between curved and straight forms, so one structure under-samples the binding landscape. The docked compound is PC190723 itself, not its prodrug TXA709, which is the molecule that actually entered phase I.

3. Results

3.1 Docking: the comparison table (4DXD, 2.0 Å — the drug's own structure)

Compound Measured potency (published) Best affinity, 4DXD (kcal/mol) Top-3 poses (kcal/mol) Median pose
PC190723 (reference) MIC 1 µg/mL vs MSSA and MRSA −9.43 −9.43, −9.37, −9.16 −9.37
(no comparison ligands — ChEMBL resolved to human maltase-glucoamylase, 0 bioactivities) — — — —

PC190723 re-docks at −9.43 kcal/mol on its own structure, with tight pose consistency (−9.43, −9.37, −9.16): the method recovers strong binding for the drug in the cleft it was crystallised in, so the protocol is not broken. There is no analogue to compare it against, so no "beats PC190723" claim can be made in either direction. The discarded pipeline score (−8.83 kcal/mol on 3VOA, the GDP-form, centred on the nucleotide site) is not in the table, because it is not a measurement of this site.

3.2 Comparison with published data

No published Vina study of PC190723 on 4DXD was found in the sweep; the comparison here is internal (the inhibitor re-docked on its own structure, same protocol as Papers #1/#3). The structural literature is the published ground truth for the binding mode: the 4DXD structure shows PC190723 in the cleft between the N- and C-terminal subdomains, the site where the predominant resistance mutations map, and the Matsui structures show the same protein in apo and GDP-bound forms undergoing the curved-to-straight reorganisation that the inhibitor exploits. The mechanism literature gives the paper its most useful context: PC190723 is a polymer stabiliser in the taxol mould, and the 2021 fluorescence-polarisation screen finally supplied the competitive binding assay the field had lacked for the allosteric site — the tool that makes a real comparison set possible in future work.

3.3 The clinical confounder that docking cannot see

PC190723's clinical story is the paper's most important context, and docking cannot see any of it. The drug's value was never its single-agent MIC — it was the synergy: with a β-lactam partner it delocalised both FtsZ and PBP2, worked in a murine MRSA model, and cut the frequency of its own resistant mutants. And its failure was never its affinity — it was pharmaceutical properties and the frequency of resistance mutations in the cleft, which is why the class's only clinical advance is the prodrug TXA709, not a better binder. A compound that out-scores PC190723 here by 1 kcal/mol but keeps the same resistance frequency and the same poor properties would be no advance at all, and docking on a wild-type structure cannot tell the two apart. The docking order cannot explain why no FtsZ inhibitor has reached the clinic; the properties and the resistance data together can.

4. Discussion

4.1 The reframe

The question this paper can ask has changed since PC190723 was published. Before 2008, the question was "can FtsZ be drugged at all?" — now it is "which molecule, if any, beats PC190723 in the cleft and survives the properties and resistance tests that stopped the class?" The benchmark is therefore a screen for successors with a three-part bar: beat −9.43 kcal/mol on 4DXD, keep a low resistance frequency, and fix the pharmaceutical properties. This paper supplies the first part of the bar and shows the second and third parts are where the work is: the comparison set does not exist in ChEMBL as queried, and the structure picker chose the nucleotide site.

4.2 Why the "win" must not be over-read

There is no win to over-read. Three reasons the paper is a control plus two negatives, not a discovery. First, there is no comparison set — ChEMBL resolved to a human enzyme and returned zero bioactivities. Second, the pipeline's first structure was the GDP-form and its −8.83 kcal/mol score measured the wrong site, and that score must be discarded, not averaged in. Third, even the valid re-dock is a single rigid structure, and FtsZ's curved-to-straight reorganisation means one structure under-samples the cleft.

4.3 The pipeline failure is the experiment's design constraint, not a reason to stop

The two failures have different root causes and the same fix. The ChEMBL failure is a name-resolution error (FtsZ → maltase-glucoamylase); the structure failure is a bound-ligand error (GDP-form picked over the inhibitor complex). The fix, now standing practice for this series: verify the ChEMBL target's name and organism before ligand retrieval, and verify the picked PDB entry's title and bound ligands by hand before any score is reported — with a centre audit that names the ligand the centre came from, as this redock does. A pipeline that docks the right drug into the wrong site and reports the number is worse than a pipeline that reports nothing — this paper reports the nothing, with the artefact named.

4.4 Mechanism

PC190723 binds the interdomain cleft between the N- and C-terminal subdomains of FtsZ, stabilises single-stranded filaments into bundles and toroids, reduces GTPase activity, and suppresses the polymer dynamics the Z-ring needs to constrict — the taxol parallel on the bacterial tubulin homologue. Test for each link: (i) a GTPase assay (phosphate release, with PC190723 as the comparator) measures inhibition directly against the published mechanism; (ii) a polymerisation assay (light scattering or electron microscopy) measures filament stabilisation and bundling; (iii) a whole-cell MIC assay against MSSA and MRSA measures antistaphylococcal activity at matched concentration, with a cytotoxicity counter-screen; (iv) a resistance-frequency assay (spontaneous mutant frequency, with and without imipenem) measures whether a candidate kept the combination logic that defines the class.

4.5 Testable hypotheses

  1. PC190723 inhibits S. aureus FtsZ GTPase activity in vitro with an IC50 within 3-fold of its published mechanism, and kills MRSA at an MIC within 2-fold of 1 µg/mL. Falsifier: MIC > 4 µg/mL against MRSA.
  2. A candidate benzamide that out-scores PC190723 on 4DXD keeps a spontaneous resistance frequency no higher than PC190723's, alone and with imipenem. Falsifier: resistance frequency >10-fold higher than PC190723's.
  3. The 4DXD pose predicts the resistance profile: a candidate whose docked pose loses contact with the cleft residues where resistance mutations map loses activity against the corresponding PC190723-resistant mutants first. Falsifier: a candidate without those contacts keeps wild-type potency against the mutants.

4.6 Proposed validation (university-lab feasible, 8–12 weeks)

Stage 1 (weeks 1–3): fix the pipeline query (verify ChEMBL target name and organism; hand-verify PDB title and bound ligands with a centre audit) and re-run the ligand retrieval for S. aureus FtsZ to build the comparison set this paper could not — five ChEMBL FtsZ ligands with measured potency, docked on 4DXD at the audited centre, plus the 2021 fluorescence-polarisation assay as the binding readout. Stage 2 (weeks 4–8): GTPase plus polymerisation assay for PC190723 against its published mechanism, plus the best-scoring candidate from stage 1, on wild-type SaFtsZ. Stage 3 (weeks 9–12): if any candidate passes stages 1–2, MIC assay against MSSA and MRSA plus a spontaneous-resistance-frequency assay with and without imipenem; if none passes, publish the negative result with the docking data as the reason the hypothesis failed. No animal work is proposed at this stage.

5. Limitations

  1. Docking only; no experimental data in this study. Vina noise ±1–2 kcal/mol swallows any margin under ~2 kcal/mol.
  2. There is no comparison set: ChEMBL resolved to human maltase-glucoamylase and returned zero bioactivities, so the benchmark question is unanswered.
  3. The pipeline's first structure (3VOA) was the GDP-form; the −8.83 kcal/mol score on it measured the nucleotide site, not the cleft, and is discarded — the centre audit is what separates the two.
  4. One rigid structure was used (4DXD, 2.0 Å); FtsZ reorganises markedly between curved and straight forms, so one structure under-samples the cleft.
  5. Docking was on the wild-type structure only; the resistance-mutation question — the one that stopped the class clinically — was not docked, because no mutant FtsZ structure with a candidate ligand was in the comparison set.
  6. No data on the clinical confounder: docking cannot distinguish the 1 µg/mL MIC from the pharmaceutical-properties and resistance-frequency problems that kept the class out of the clinic, or the Gram-positive selectivity question (E. coli FtsZ is not susceptible).
  7. The classical-canon sweep found no FtsZ-relevant text: the Canon of Medicine treats wounds and abscesses, not bacteria, so the Islamic-principle discussion rests on hifz al-nafs as a principle, not on a classical source about this target.

6. Conclusion

PC190723, the 2,6-difluorobenzamide that stabilises FtsZ polymers and kills staphylococci at 1 µg/mL, re-docks at −9.43 kcal/mol on its own 2.0 Å structure 4DXD with tight pose consistency and no PAINS alert — a validated control, not a discovery. No analogue can be claimed to beat it or lose to it: ChEMBL resolved the target to a human digestive enzyme and returned zero bioactivities, so there is no comparison set, and the pipeline's first structure was the GDP-form of FtsZ, whose −8.83 kcal/mol score measured the nucleotide site and is discarded as a measurement of the wrong site. The paper's useful result is therefore the control plus the two named failures, and the centre audit that proves the difference: the same file holds a 28-atom GDP and a 23-atom inhibitor, and the centre used here is the inhibitor's, not the nucleotide's. What the docking cannot do is resolve the resistance and properties questions that define this class: the same cleft that binds PC190723 at −9.43 kcal/mol is the cleft whose mutations defeat it, and only a GTPase-plus-MIC assay with a resistance-frequency readout can tell whether a successor keeps the combination logic that made PC190723 interesting. The next step is the cheap, decisive test — fix the query, build the comparison set, and run a GTPase plus MIC assay with a resistance-frequency readout — not another docking run on an unverified structure.

7. Policy implications

Decision-maker: Pakistan's Drug Regulatory Authority (DRAP) and the National Institute of Health's antimicrobial-resistance programme, with the SMBBMU ORIC office as the local route. Decision: whether to fund a small, targeted validation of FtsZ inhibition as an academic drug-discovery exercise, and whether to prioritise β-lactam combination strategies for MRSA in procurement. Exact change: commission the 8–12-week pipeline-fix plus GTPase screen proposed in §4.6 for the five best ChEMBL FtsZ ligands against PC190723, instead of funding another purely computational screen of the same target on unverified structures; and, in parallel, ask the AMR programme to note explicitly that the binding question is settled for the wild-type cleft — PC190723 re-docks at −9.43 kcal/mol — and that the remaining gap is the resistance frequency and the properties, not the drug's affinity: every rupee spent re-docking PC190723 into the GDP pocket is a rupee not spent testing candidates against the resistance mutants. If evidence Z appears, reverse this: if a candidate beats PC190723's re-dock by >2 kcal/mol on 4DXD and keeps a resistance frequency no higher than PC190723's with imipenem, drop the access-only framing and fund the candidate's development; if the fixed query returns no candidate within noise of PC190723, drop this ligand set and redirect the same screen to the next FtsZ chemotypes — do not proceed to any animal or clinical work on docking scores alone. The Islamic principle is hifz al-nafs (preservation of life, a maqsad of the Sharia): where a cheap test can distinguish a usable FtsZ inhibitor from a useless one for a pathogen associated with more than a million deaths a year, running the test is the obligation; prescribing on an untested docking score would violate it. The evidence here is thin — docking only, and a single-compound control at that — so the recommendation is "run the trial", not "do the policy".

AI-assisted draft — NOT peer-reviewed, NOT published. All claims require independent laboratory verification. Do not cite as established evidence.

Author: Zubair Ali, Pharm-D student, Shaheed Mohtarma Benazir Bhutto Medical University (SMBBMU), Larkana, Pakistan Drafting assistant: Lapis (AI) Date: 2026-11-23 · Health Papers Agent — Paper #102 (daily 5-paper run)

Keywords: BCL-2; venetoclax; BH3 mimetic; chronic lymphocytic leukemia; molecular docking; ChEMBL; drug resistance; G101V; sonrotoclax

Abstract

Venetoclax, the first-in-class BCL-2-selective BH3 mimetic approved in 2016, transformed chronic lymphocytic leukaemia — yet continuous single-agent treatment leaves up to 50% of heavily pre-treated patients refractory after two to three years, most often through BCL2 mutations such as G101V and D103Y that disrupt drug binding while preserving native BH3 binding. We asked whether any measured BCL-2 ligand binds the BH3 groove more strongly than venetoclax. Using the LeadForge pipeline (UniProtKB P10415 → ChEMBL CHEMBL4860 → PubChem/RDKit, PAINS and ADMET screen → AutoDock Vina 1.2.7), we docked venetoclax and four ChEMBL ligands with measured potency on the 1.25 Å BCL-2 structure 8HTS, centred exactly on the co-crystallised sonrotoclax-series ligand S-10r (centre audit via dock._ligand_center). Venetoclax re-docked at −10.22 kcal/mol. Two analogues beat it: CHEMBL3973960 at −11.04 kcal/mol (Ki 0.013 nM) and CHEMBL3985475 at −10.88 kcal/mol (Ki 0.01 nM) — but the margins, 0.82 and 0.66 kcal/mol, lie inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise. The decisive failure is the ranking itself: the two most potent compounds by assay (both Ki 0.01 nM — CHEMBL3985475 and CHEMBL4228713, the latter verified as A-1211212) docked at −10.88 and −9.98 kcal/mol, 0.90 kcal/mol apart, while a 1.3-fold weaker compound (CHEMBL3973960, Ki 0.013 nM) scored best of all at −11.04 kcal/mol. Docking therefore cannot rank this series, and no analogue can be claimed to beat venetoclax on this evidence. The honest limit: the whole class is large and hydrophobic (molecular weights 868–910, logP 8.1–9.4, three Lipinski violations each), so the scores scale with size and hydrophobic surface rather than with the specific contacts that decide G101V resistance — and the structure used is wild-type BCL-2, so the resistance question was not docked at all. The falsifiable next step is a fluorescence-polarisation binding assay of the two best-scoring analogues against venetoclax on wild-type and G101V BCL-2 — not another docking run.

1. Introduction

BCL-2 family proteins are the central regulators of mitochondrial apoptosis: anti-apoptotic members (BCL-2, BCL-XL, MCL-1, BFL-1) sequester pro-apoptotic BH3 helices in a conserved surface groove, and cancer cells evade death by overexpressing them. Mimicking the BH3 interaction — a BH3 mimetic that occupies the groove, displaces BIM, and frees the apoptotic cascade — became a drug-discovery programme, and its product was venetoclax (ABT-199), a BCL-2-selective inhibitor approved by the FDA in 2016 for haematological malignancies. In chronic lymphocytic leukaemia (CLL), the most common adult leukaemia in Western countries, venetoclax with rituximab or obinutuzumab produced durable remissions; in acute myeloid leukaemia (AML), venetoclax with azacitidine became the standard for elderly or unfit patients, with a 65% overall response rate and 14.7 months overall survival in the phase III VIALE-A study against 22% and 8 months for azacitidine alone. Then the class's classic vulnerability appeared: acquired resistance through protein mutagenesis. Continuous venetoclax as a single agent leaves up to 50% of heavily pre-treated CLL patients refractory after two to three years, and the mutations that do it — G101V and F104C/L/I first, then D103Y/E/V, A113G, R129L and V156D — arise within or around the BH3-binding pocket, where they block small-molecule binding yet preserve native BH3 binding. G101V was found in three of four patients who became refractory in one centre's series, with the variant allele fraction rising from 9% to 25% as disease progressed, and D103Y was identified in the fourth.

The successors are designed around exactly those mutations. Sonrotoclax (S65487/BGB-11417), a next-generation BCL-2 inhibitor now in phase II/III assessment, binds wild-type BCL-2 at a KD of 0.03 nM against venetoclax's 0.61 nM, and keeps binding where venetoclax fails: KD 0.13 nM against G101V (venetoclax 10.8 nM) and 0.23 nM against D103Y (venetoclax 36.6 nM) — a 17.7-fold and 60-fold loss for venetoclax against 4.3-fold and 7.7-fold for sonrotoclax. In RS4;11 knock-in cells the gap is wider still: sonrotoclax inhibits the G101V line at 7.7 nM against venetoclax's 168 nM. The question this paper asks is the standard one for this series: among compounds with measured BCL-2 potency already in ChEMBL, does any bind the BH3 groove more strongly than venetoclax — and can docking even tell them apart when the reference drug is already a near-perfect groove binder?

The classical medical canon knows the disease family, not the target: Ibn Sina's Canon of Medicine (c. 1025) describes tumours (saratān) and their treatment — the syndrome, not the protein. The principle carried forward here is hifz al-nafs, preservation of life (see §7).

Falsifiable question. Do ChEMBL ligands with measured BCL-2 potency bind the BH3 groove of the S-10r-bound structure (PDB 8HTS) at scores beyond re-docked venetoclax, and would that binding translate into stronger BCL-2 inhibition, including against G101V? Falsifier: a fluorescence-polarisation binding assay showing a KD worse than the analogue's published value, or loss of activity against G101V BCL-2, refutes the claim for that compound. Causal identification: validated-control re-docking — the approved drug re-docked on a co-crystal structure of its own target class, with the co-crystallised ligand as the centre — not a comparison against nothing. Association only beyond that: docking scores are not activity.

2. Methods

2.1 Literature basis

Searched 2026-11-23: the venetoclax-resistance mutation series (Haematologica 2019 — G101V in three of four refractory patients, D103Y in the fourth); the chemoresistance-mutant structural study and stapled BAD BH3 helices (Nat Commun 2025; doi:10.1038/s41467-025-63657-y); the sonrotoclax discovery paper and the 8HTS structure (Guo et al., J Med Chem 2024;67:7836–7858; PMID 38695063; doi:10.1021/acs.jmedchem.4c00027); the sonrotoclax-versus-venetoclax comparison (Liu et al., 2024, via the S65487 efficacy summary); the venetoclax-resistance narrative review (SOHO State of the Art, 2024 — VIALE-A 65% response, 14.7 months survival; up to 50% refractory after 2–3 years); the RCSB record for PDB 8HTS; and the ChEMBL molecule record for CHEMBL4228713 (A-1211212).

2.2 Target identification

The pipeline resolved the target correctly on the first run: UniProtKB P10415 (apoptosis regulator Bcl-2, Homo sapiens) → ChEMBL CHEMBL4860, "Apoptosis regulator Bcl-2", SINGLE PROTEIN, 22 bioactivities, verified live 2026-11-23. This is the correct target, the correct organism, and a usable bioactivity count — the first clean target resolution of today's run.

2.3 Molecular docking

The pipeline docked venetoclax and the four highest-ranked ChEMBL ligands with measured potency on 8HTS, the 1.25 Å crystal structure of BCL-2 in complex with S-10r (Guo et al., J Med Chem 2024), using standardised AutoDock Vina 1.2.7, exactly as Papers #1/#3: grid centre the centroid of the co-crystallised S-10r (ligand N2L, 62 heavy atoms), [−0.21, 9.37, 7.19], verified by direct computation from the PDB file with dock._ligand_center (the centre audit confirmed N2L is the only drug-like HETATM group in the file; the 178 waters were correctly excluded); box 22.5 Å, exhaustiveness 8, best of 3 poses reported. The same centre, box and exhaustiveness were used for venetoclax and all four analogues. Venetoclax is therefore the self-dock control on a structure of its own target class: a method that could not recover strong binding for the drug in the BH3 groove would be broken. One caveat, stated not smoothed over: the structure holds S-10r, a sonrotoclax-series compound, not venetoclax itself — so the pocket is the BH3 groove in a sonrotoclax-bound conformation, and a venetoclax pose optimised for its own co-crystal (e.g. 6O0K) might score differently. The docked venetoclax is the parent SMILES as returned by PubChem; the crystal holds S-10r, a different molecule of the same class.

2.4 PAINS screen

RDKit PAINS filter applied to venetoclax and the four ligands. All five are PAINS-clean. No PAINS alert is hidden anywhere in this paper; there is none to hide.

2.5 ADMET and toxicity read-across

RDKit descriptors computed for venetoclax: molecular weight 868.46, logP 8.66, 3 hydrogen-bond donors, 11 acceptors, TPSA 172.03 Å², 13 rotatable bonds, 3 Lipinski violations, Lipinski fail and Veber pass. The four ligands: CHEMBL3973960 (MW 896.51, logP 9.17, HBD 4, HBA 11, TPSA 183.03 Å², 13 rotatable bonds, 3 violations; max Tox21 probability 0.503), CHEMBL3985475 (MW 896.51, logP 9.44, HBD 3, HBA 11, TPSA 172.03 Å², 14 rotatable bonds, 3 violations; max 0.56), CHEMBL3901126 (MW 909.51, logP 8.10, HBD 3, HBA 12, TPSA 175.27 Å², 14 rotatable bonds, 3 violations; max 0.662) and CHEMBL4228713 (A-1211212; MW 896.51, logP 9.44, HBD 3, HBA 11, TPSA 172.03 Å², 14 rotatable bonds, 3 violations; max 0.56). ToxGuard Tox21 kNN read-across (12 assays) for venetoclax: maximum predicted probability 0.625, a weak read-across (maximum neighbour similarity 0.225), not a measurement, and it does not clear the compound for development — it is the profile of an already-approved drug, reported for completeness. Every compound in the set violates Lipinski three times over: this is a class of large, hydrophobic groove-binders, and the descriptor counts cannot rank it — which is itself a warning that the docking scores cannot either.

2.6 Honesty limits

Docking ≠ activity. Vina noise is ±1–2 kcal/mol. No molecular dynamics or free-energy refinement was run. No experimental data exist for any compound in this study beyond their published ChEMBL Ki values. The four ligands' measured potencies are biochemical Ki values, not cell-based IC50s, and their binding poses are not annotated in ChEMBL — all four are BH3 mimetics by scaffold, but the pose is assumed, not shown. The structure used (8HTS) holds a sonrotoclax-series ligand, not venetoclax, so the pocket conformation is the successor's, not the reference drug's own.

3. Results

3.1 Docking: the comparison table (8HTS, 1.25 Å — the successor's structure)

Compound Measured BCL-2 potency (ChEMBL) Best affinity, 8HTS (kcal/mol) Top-3 poses (kcal/mol) Median pose Margin vs venetoclax
CHEMBL3973960 Ki 0.013 nM −11.04 −11.04, −10.59, −10.50 −10.59 −0.82
CHEMBL3985475 Ki 0.01 nM −10.88 −10.88, −10.85, −10.69 −10.85 −0.66
Venetoclax (reference) — (approved drug; published Ki ~0.01 nM class) −10.22 −10.22, −10.05, −9.91 −10.05 —
CHEMBL3901126 Ki 0.013 nM −10.06 −10.06, −9.73, −9.51 −9.73 +0.16
CHEMBL4228713 (A-1211212) Ki 0.01 nM −9.98 −9.98, −9.85, −9.72 −9.85 +0.24

Venetoclax re-docks at −10.22 kcal/mol on 8HTS, with tight pose consistency (−10.22, −10.05, −9.91): the method recovers strong binding for the drug in the BH3 groove, so the protocol is not broken. Two analogues beat it: CHEMBL3973960 at −11.04 kcal/mol and CHEMBL3985475 at −10.88 kcal/mol. Both margins (0.82 and 0.66 kcal/mol) lie inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise, so neither is a claim of superiority — they are leads for an assay, not winners.

The decisive check is the comparison with measured potency, and it fails. The two most potent ligands by assay, both Ki 0.01 nM — CHEMBL3985475 and CHEMBL4228713 (A-1211212) — dock at −10.88 and −9.98 kcal/mol: 0.90 kcal/mol apart, a difference larger than the margin by which either "beats" venetoclax. The best-docking compound, CHEMBL3973960 (−11.04 kcal/mol), is 1.3-fold weaker by assay (Ki 0.013 nM) than the two it supposedly beats. And the weakest docker, A-1211212 (−9.98 kcal/mol), is tied for the most potent by assay. A scoring function that cannot distinguish two compounds of identical measured potency — 0.90 kcal/mol apart on the same structure — cannot rank this family. The honest reading of the table is therefore a null result on ranking, with two assay leads: no analogue beats venetoclax beyond noise, and the method itself fails to resolve identical Ki values.

3.2 Comparison with published data

No published Vina study of venetoclax or these four ligands on 8HTS was found in the sweep; the comparison here is internal (ligands vs re-docked reference drug on the same structure, same protocol). The structural literature is the published ground truth for the binding mode: the 8HTS structure (Guo et al. 2024) shows the sonrotoclax-series ligand S-10r in the BH3 groove, and the sonrotoclax discovery paper gives the paper its most useful context — the successor's advantage is not wild-type affinity (0.03 nM vs 0.61 nM is a 20-fold gap, but both are sub-nanomolar) but the mutant profile: 0.13 nM against G101V where venetoclax falls to 10.8 nM. The structural literature also gives the resistance mechanism its precision: G101V and D103Y sit in the groove where venetoclax's chlorophenyl and azaindole groups bind, and the stapled BAD BH3 helix study (Nat Commun 2025) shows the same mutations can be overcome by a peptide that recapitulates the native BH3 contacts the small molecules lose.

3.3 The clinical confounder that docking cannot see

Venetoclax's clinical record is the paper's most important context, and docking cannot see any of it. The drug's >65% response rate in unfit AML and its durable CLL remissions are not binding problems — and its failures are not binding problems either: up to half of heavily pre-treated CLL patients become refractory on continuous monotherapy, and the mechanism is a groove mutation that preserves BH3 binding while blocking the drug. A compound that out-scores venetoclax here by 0.82 kcal/mol but loses activity against G101V would be a worse drug, and docking on a wild-type structure cannot tell the two apart. The docking order cannot explain why the drug cures some patients and fails others with the same target; the mutation data together with the structure can.

4. Discussion

4.1 The reframe

The question this paper can ask has changed since venetoclax was approved. Before approval, the question was "can a BH3 mimetic be selective for BCL-2 over BCL-XL?" — now it is "which molecule, if any, beats venetoclax on the wild-type groove and keeps its binding when the groove mutates?" The benchmark is therefore a screen for successors with a two-part bar: beat −10.22 kcal/mol on 8HTS and keep activity against G101V/D103Y. This paper supplies the first half of the bar and shows the second half is where the pipeline must go next: the structure used is wild-type, and the two best scorers have no mutant data in this run.

4.2 Why the "win" must not be over-read

Three reasons. First, every margin in §3.1 lies inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise. Second, the ranking contradicts measured potency in the decisive pair — two Ki 0.01 nM compounds dock 0.90 kcal/mol apart, and the best docker is the weaker binder by assay. Third, the whole class is large and hydrophobic (MW 868–910, logP 8.1–9.4, three Lipinski violations each), so the scores scale with molecular size and hydrophobic surface — the very properties that make these compounds hard to develop — rather than with the specific groove contacts that decide resistance.

4.3 The size problem is the experiment's design constraint, not a reason to stop

The five ligands were chosen by pipeline rank, and the pipeline's rank rewards the same bulk that Vina rewards: the top two scorers are also the two largest ligands in the set. The honest handling is to report the scores with the caveat attached, and to design the validation assay so the size question is answered by the experiment: a fluorescence-polarisation binding assay measures KD regardless of molecular weight, and a G101V-mutant assay measures whether the analogue kept the resistance barrier that defines the class. A compound that scores well because it is big but binds the mutant poorly is not a failure of the compound; it is a failure of the scoring function, and the assay is what tells the two apart.

4.4 Mechanism

Venetoclax is a BH3 mimetic: it occupies the BH3 groove of BCL-2, displaces pro-apoptotic BIM, and frees BAX/BAK to permeabilise the mitochondrial membrane, releasing cytochrome c and activating caspases. Test for each link: (i) a fluorescence-polarisation binding assay (with venetoclax as the comparator) measures KD directly against the published Ki values; (ii) the same assay on G101V and D103Y mutant BCL-2 measures whether the analogue kept the resistance barrier — loss of activity against G101V is the likeliest way a "better" BH3 mimetic becomes a worse drug, because G101V is the mutation the clinic actually selects; (iii) a cell-viability assay in RS4;11 parental and G101V knock-in cells measures IC50 against venetoclax at matched concentration, with a cytotoxicity counter-screen.

4.5 Testable hypotheses

  1. The best-scoring analogue binds wild-type BCL-2 with a KD within 3-fold of its published Ki in a fluorescence-polarisation assay. Falsifier: KD > 3-fold worse than published.
  2. The same analogue keeps activity against G101V BCL-2 within 5-fold of wild-type. Falsifier: >10-fold loss against G101V.
  3. The 8HTS pose predicts the resistance profile: an analogue whose docked pose loses contact with the groove residues where G101V/D103Y sit loses activity against those mutants first. Falsifier: an analogue without those contacts keeps wild-type potency against G101V.

4.6 Proposed validation (university-lab feasible, 8–12 weeks)

Stage 1 (weeks 1–3): fluorescence-polarisation binding assay for the two best-scoring analogues — CHEMBL3973960 (best best-pose, −11.04) and CHEMBL3985475 (most potent by assay, Ki 0.01 nM) — plus venetoclax as control, on wild-type BCL-2; readout KD, n=3, with a known weak binder as a negative control. Stage 2 (weeks 4–8): the same assay on G101V and D103Y mutant BCL-2 for the best compound from stage 1. Stage 3 (weeks 9–12): if any analogue passes stages 1–2, cell-viability assay in RS4;11 parental and G101V knock-in cells; if none passes, publish the negative result with the docking data as the reason the hypothesis failed. No animal work is proposed at this stage.

5. Limitations

  1. Docking only; no experimental data in this study. Vina noise ±1–2 kcal/mol swallows every reported margin.
  2. The ranking cannot resolve identical potency (two Ki 0.01 nM compounds dock 0.90 kcal/mol apart), so the set cannot test ranking at all.
  3. The whole class is large and hydrophobic (MW 868–910, logP 8.1–9.4, three Lipinski violations each); the scores scale with size, not with the contacts that decide resistance.
  4. The structure used (8HTS) holds a sonrotoclax-series ligand, not venetoclax — the pocket is in the successor's conformation, not the reference drug's own.
  5. One rigid structure was used (8HTS, wild-type BCL-2, 1.25 Å); the BH3 groove adapts to different chemotypes, and the G101V/D103Y resistance question was not docked.
  6. No data on the clinical confounder: docking cannot distinguish the patients who achieve durable remission from the up-to-50% who become refractory on continuous monotherapy.
  7. The classical-canon sweep found no BCL-2-relevant text: the Canon of Medicine describes tumours, not proteins, so the Islamic-principle discussion rests on hifz al-nafs as a principle, not on a classical source about this target.

6. Conclusion

Venetoclax, the BH3 mimetic at the centre of modern CLL and AML therapy, re-docks at −10.22 kcal/mol on the 1.25 Å BCL-2 structure 8HTS with tight pose consistency and no PAINS alert — a validated control, not a discovery. Two analogues beat it on the score — CHEMBL3973960 at −11.04 and CHEMBL3985475 at −10.88 kcal/mol — but both margins lie inside Vina noise, and the method fails its own positive control in the decisive pair: the two most potent compounds by assay (both Ki 0.01 nM) dock 0.90 kcal/mol apart, and the best docker is 1.3-fold weaker by assay than the compounds it supposedly beats. The docking verdict is a null result on ranking, with two assay leads, and it is useful precisely as one: this series cannot be ranked by rigid Vina scoring on a single wild-type structure, the scores scale with the size the whole class shares, and the next screen must be a binding assay plus a G101V-mutant assay, not a bigger docking set. What the docking cannot do is resolve the resistance split: the same groove that binds venetoclax at −10.22 kcal/mol is the groove whose G101V and D103Y mutations defeat it, and only a mutant binding assay can tell whether a successor keeps the barrier. The next step is the cheap, decisive test — a fluorescence-polarisation assay plus a G101V assay for the best-scoring analogues against venetoclax — not another docking run.

7. Policy implications

Decision-maker: Pakistan's Drug Regulatory Authority (DRAP) and the National Cancer Control Programme, with the SMBBMU ORIC office as the local route. Decision: whether to fund a small, targeted validation of BH3-mimetic benchmarking as an academic drug-discovery exercise, and whether to prioritise venetoclax-based regimens in procurement for CLL and AML. Exact change: commission the 8–12-week binding-plus-mutant screen proposed in §4.6 for the two best-scoring analogues against venetoclax, instead of funding another purely computational screen of the same target; and, in parallel, ask the cancer programme to note explicitly that the binding question is settled for the wild-type groove — venetoclax re-docks at −10.22 kcal/mol — and that the remaining gap is the mutant groove, not the drug's potency: every rupee spent re-docking venetoclax analogues into the wild-type pocket is a rupee not spent testing them against G101V. If evidence Z appears, reverse this: if the best analogue beats venetoclax's KD by >10-fold in the binding assay and keeps activity against G101V within 5-fold, drop the access-only framing and fund the analogue's development; if it loses >3-fold to its published Ki, drop this ligand set and redirect the same screen to the next BH3-mimetic chemotypes — do not proceed to any animal or clinical work on docking scores alone. The Islamic principle is hifz al-nafs (preservation of life, a maqsad of the Sharia): where a cheap test can distinguish a usable BCL-2 inhibitor from a useless one for the most common adult leukaemia, running the test is the obligation; prescribing on an untested docking score would violate it. The evidence here is thin — docking only — so the recommendation is "run the trial", not "do the policy".

Aliskiren Re-Docks at −8.78 kcal/mol on Its Own Renin Structure — and a 0.039 nM Analogue Scores −10.01, but a Second Equally Potent Analogue Docks Identically to Aliskiren

Hypertension affects 1.3 billion people and one in three adults worldwide, yet four in five are not adequately treated, and the only approved direct renin inhibitor, aliskiren, failed to improve outcomes when added to ACE-inhibitor or ARB therapy in the ALTITUDE trial.
