3.3 The 6JED replication reproduces the pattern exactly — and the EPE-centred run is discarded

Re-centred on the MCR ligand, 6JED gives the same result: 3AP-DPA best (−7.13), DPA second (−6.08), the four stereoisomers in a 0.34 kcal/mol band (−5.54 to −5.88), epi-l again best of the four, overall ρ = −0.66 — identical to 4C1G to two decimal places. The finding is not structure-dependent: two structures, two resolutions, same collapse. The first 6JED run, centred on the HEPES buffer molecule EPE by the pipeline's automatic picker, is discarded as evidence (its scores were nearly identical — −7.12, −6.05, −5.93, −5.68, −5.67, −5.66 — because the 22.5 Å box still covered the active site, which is precisely why the error was dangerous: a wrong centre that still returns plausible numbers). It is recorded here so the failure mode is visible: a centre picker that requires ≥6 atoms will centre on a buffer molecule whenever the true ligand is a 5-atom fragment.

3.4 Mechanism: the score cannot see the bond that does the work

The mechanism was stated before the results and the data confirm it. Captopril's potency differences come from how its thiolate and carboxylate engage the two Zn(II) ions and Arg228 — interactions that do not exist in the scored system, because the receptor preparation removed the zinc and Vina has no metal term. Four stereoisomers of one molecule present the same atoms, the same descriptors and nearly the same shape to a metal-free pocket, so they receive nearly the same score; the 0.08 kcal/mol spread is the residue of shape differences after the chemistry has been deleted. The dicarboxylates escape the collapse only partially: they are larger, more polar molecules whose shape and hydrogen-bonding differ enough for Vina to order them, and their measured gap is partly a size/polarity effect — but their true mechanism (metal chelation and metal stripping, Zhang et al. 2021) is equally invisible to the score, which is why even their correct ordering is compressed (0.92 vs 1.50 kcal/mol). The sibling benchmark on VIM-2 in this series found the same failure with the same four stereoisomers: a 0.07 kcal/mol span for a 76-fold measured range (ρ = 0.15, n = 4). Two B1 enzymes, two independent structure sets, the same number: ~0.1 kcal/mol of docking score for ~60–76-fold of metal-dependent potency.

Discussion

Two findings, one encouraging and one limiting — and the limiting one is the paper.

First, rigid docking can shortlist dicarboxylate scaffolds for IMP-1. 3AP-DPA out-scores DPA on both structures, by 0.92 and 1.05 kcal/mol, in the correct direction for a 12.6-fold measured gap, and both dicarboxylates clear the thiols by ~0.5–1.5 kcal/mol. A screen that ranks 3AP-DPA analogues first would spend its assay budget in the right place. The 3AP-DPA scaffold — a dipicolinic acid core with an aryl substituent at the 4-position — is the lead to optimise, and the honest next step is synthesis of 4-substituted analogues, not more docking of the same two compounds.

Second, rigid metal-free docking is blind to the stereochemistry that defines thiol MBL inhibition, and the blindness is quantitative, reproducible and now replicated across two enzymes. A 60-fold potency range collapses into 0.08 kcal/mol on IMP-1 and a 76-fold range into 0.07 kcal/mol on VIM-2. No re-ranking, no consensus scoring and no bigger box will fix this: the information that separates d- from epi-l-captopril is the geometry of thiolate–Zn(II) coordination, and that information is deleted before scoring starts. The falsifier stands open — a metal-aware method that orders the four stereoisomers with a spread ≥1 kcal/mol would refute the claim — but until such a method is run, any IMP-1 or VIM-2 screen that reports Vina scores for thiol inhibitors as a ranking is reporting noise with two decimal places. The practical consequence is a screening rule: metal-chelating chemotypes (thiols, dicarboxylates, boronates) must not be ranked by metal-free rigid docking; use it only to shortlist non-chelating scaffolds, and rank chelators by assay or by a metal-aware method (Zn retained, coordination-aware scoring, or QM/MM estimates of metal binding).

Association only. This is a retrospective docking benchmark, not a causal experiment: it shows that Vina scores do not track measured IMP-1 potency within the captopril series, under the stated protocol. It does not show that no docking method can rank these compounds — the falsifier names the method that could.

Limitations

  1. No lab data. All results are computational; no IMP-1 assay was run, and the measured IC50s are taken from two published sources (Brem et al. 2016; Chen et al. 2017 via ChEMBL).
  2. Metal stripped, by design of the pipeline. The receptor preparation removes Zn(II); the paper tests metal-free docking deliberately, but a metal-aware comparison was not run — that is the named falsifier, not a result.
  3. Small n. Six compounds; the within-series correlation uses four. A single additional stereoisomer series could change ρ, though it cannot change the 0.08 kcal/mol spread, which is the paper's central number.
  4. Assay heterogeneity. The dicarboxylate IC50s (Chen et al. 2017) and the captopril IC50s (Brem et al. 2016) come from different assays and years; the 60-fold and 12.6-fold gaps are within-assay comparisons, but cross-class comparisons assume assay comparability.
  5. No RMSD for the re-dock. The d-captopril re-dock control is a tight score, not an atom-by-atom pose comparison.
  6. RDKit valence warnings during receptor preparation. The preparation step emitted "explicit valence greater than permitted" warnings for metal-adjacent atoms; all twelve docks completed and returned poses, but the preparation is triage-grade and the warnings are recorded here rather than hidden.
  7. Islamic canon gaps (named, per the programme's rule). Ibn Sina's Canon, Book II materia medica, was not screened against IMP-1 — no Canon-listed plant was docked in this run. The full 23-volume Kitab al-Hawi of Al-Razi exists in English only in selections, so it was used through verified summaries, not read in full. Most classical Arabic manuscripts on medicine remain undigitised in library collections (Süleymaniye, Dar al-Kutub, the British Library) with no online copy; this paper claims no more than the named works above.

Policy implications

Decision-maker: the Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan (DRAP) and the National Institute of Health, Pakistan — antimicrobial resistance programme; and hospital antimicrobial stewardship committees. Three exact changes, each with its falsifier:

  1. Any computational MBL-inhibitor screen submitted for public research funding in Pakistan must state whether its docking retained the catalytic Zn(II) ions, and metal-chelating chemotypes must be ranked by assay or a metal-aware method — not by metal-free Vina scores. If a metal-aware method is shown not to beat Vina's ranking on a blinded set, reverse this requirement. This is the direct operational consequence of the 0.08 kcal/mol result: public money currently risks being spent ranking noise.
  2. Prioritise the 3AP-DPA dicarboxylate scaffold over thiol repurposing in the national IMP-1 research agenda. 3AP-DPA (240 nM) is the most potent measured IMP-1 inhibitor in the ChEMBL record for this target and the only chemotype this benchmark could rank correctly; captopril repurposing for IMP-1 should be deprioritised (best stereoisomer 7.2 µM, and its ranking cannot be trusted computationally).
  3. Fund a Pakistan IMP-1 assay panel. IMP-1 is 2.7% of carbapenemase genes today (Gondal et al. 2023) but plasmid-borne and rising wherever carbapenems are overused; the country has no domestic IC50 pipeline for MBL inhibitors, so every ranking decision is imported. A single national panel (IMP-1, NDM-1, VIM-2) at one reference laboratory would convert this paper's falsifier into a routine check.

Islamic principle behind the recommendations. Preservation of life (hifz al-nafs, one of the five objectives of the law, Al-Ghazali, Al-Mustasfa; systematised by Al-Shatibi, Al-Muwafaqat): "whoever saves a life, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely" (Qur'an 5:32). Antimicrobial resistance is a direct threat to life — in Pakistan 42.1% of clinical isolates in the Lahore study were carbapenem-resistant — so a screening method that mis-ranks inhibitors is not a technical footnote but a failure to protect life, and public interest (maslaha) requires the method to be fixed before it is funded. Stewardship (khilafah, Qur'an 2:30): antibiotics are a trust held for future generations, and a steward does not spend a trust on a tool known to mislead. Justice ('adl, Qur'an 4:135): the burden of carbapenem resistance falls hardest on the poorest patients, who cannot afford polymyxins or imported combinations — so the research agenda must prioritise the scaffolds with the best measured potency per rupee, not the most familiar repurposed drug. Where the Islamic sources and the modern evidence point the same way — protect life, spend the trust honestly, favour the poor — this paper says so; they do here.

Conclusion

Rigid AutoDock Vina docking into the d-captopril-bound IMP-1 structure 4C1G ranks the dicarboxylates correctly — 3AP-DPA (−7.42 kcal/mol) ahead of dipicolinic acid (−6.50) for a 12.6-fold measured gap — with an overall Spearman ρ = −0.66 (n = 6). But the four captopril stereoisomers collapse into 0.08 kcal/mol for a 60-fold measured potency range, the weakest scoring joint-best, and the 6JED replication reproduces the pattern exactly. The mechanism is the deleted metal: the pipeline strips the two catalytic Zn(II) ions and Vina has no metal-coordination term, so inhibitors whose binding is Zn chelation are scored on shape alone. Two B1 enzymes now show the same failure (VIM-2: 0.07 kcal/mol for 76-fold). The memorable number is 0.08 kcal/mol — that is what 60-fold of metal-dependent potency is worth to a metal-free docking score. Do not rank thiol MBL inhibitors with it.

Pemigatinib Re-Docks at −8.83 kcal/mol on FGFR2 2PVF, but the Most Potent Measured Inhibitor Scores Worst and the Most Potent Lead Was Never Docked

FGFR2 fusions drive 10–15% of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, and pemigatinib, the first approved FGFR inhibitor for this disease, produced a 35.5% objective response rate in FIGHT-202.

PDF · Markdown

Read full paper

AI-assisted draft — NOT peer-reviewed, NOT published. All claims require independent laboratory verification. Do not cite as established evidence.

Author: Zubair Ali, Pharm-D student, Shaheed Mohtarma Benazir Bhutto Medical University (SMBBMU), Larkana, Pakistan Drafting assistant: Lapis (AI) Date: 2026-11-17 · Health Papers Agent — Paper #71 (daily 5-paper run) Topic ID: HP-080

Keywords: FGFR2; pemigatinib; cholangiocarcinoma; molecular docking; AutoDock Vina; futibatinib; hyperphosphataemia; drug discovery

Abstract

FGFR2 fusions drive 10–15% of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, and pemigatinib, the first approved FGFR inhibitor for this disease, produced a 35.5% objective response rate in FIGHT-202. We benchmarked rigid AutoDock Vina docking (v1.2.7) against measured FGFR2 inhibition for four sub-nanomolar compounds on the activated FGFR2 kinase structure 2PVF (1.8 Å), with the grid centre audited to exactly 0.00 Å from the ATP-analogue centroid. Pemigatinib re-docked at −8.83 kcal/mol, reproduced to −8.90 by its own ChEMBL record, a 0.07 kcal/mol duplicate. But the ranking fails: the most potent measured inhibitor, CHEMBL4870179 (IC50 0.15 nM), scored worst at −8.01, and the most potent compound in the whole 26-lead set (CHEMBL5173892, 0.11 nM) was never docked, because the pipeline's similarity-dominated ranking placed it 20th. Spearman rho is +0.40 (n = 4). ChEMBL mutant records add the clinically decisive number: pemigatinib loses about 6,000-fold potency against the gatekeeper mutant FGFR2 V564F (IC50 1,460.5 nM), a loss no wild-type docking score can see. The honest limit cuts deeper than the ranking: the two leads' sub-nanomolar values come from a single document, while a patent document reports 100 nM for both. Falsifiable claim: rigid docking on the activated FGFR2 structure cannot rank sub-nanomolar FGFR2 inhibitors. A re-dock on an inhibitor-bound, inactive-conformation FGFR2 structure that recovers the measured order with rho at or below −0.5 would refute it; so would a prospective enzyme assay showing CHEMBL5171314, the best-docked compound, underperforming pemigatinib in cells.

1. Introduction

Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) is a rare, aggressive cancer of the bile ducts with few effective systemic options after first-line chemotherapy. FGFR2 fusions and rearrangements — chromosomal rearrangements that fuse the FGFR2 kinase domain to a partner gene, producing ligand-independent dimerisation and constitutive signalling — occur in approximately 10–15% of iCCA and almost nowhere else, making them one of the most actionable alterations in oncology. Pemigatinib, a selective oral inhibitor of FGFR1, 2 and 3, became the first approved drug for this population on the FIGHT-202 trial (Abou-Alfa et al. 2020): among 107 previously treated patients with FGFR2 fusions or rearrangements, 38 (35.5%, 95% CI 26.5–45.4) achieved an objective response, three of them complete, on 13.5 mg daily (two weeks on, one week off). Hyperphosphataemia — the on-target class effect of FGFR inhibition, which blocks FGF23 signalling and raises serum phosphate — was the most common adverse event at 60% (88/146). The covalent next-generation inhibitor futibatinib followed in FOENIX-CCA2 (Goyal et al. 2023): 43 of 103 patients (42%, 95% CI 32–52) responded, median duration of response 9.7 months, median progression-free survival 9.0 months and overall survival 21.7 months, with grade 3 hyperphosphataemia in 30%.

The clinical question this paper attacks is narrower than "does pemigatinib work" — that is settled. It is whether a standard computational benchmark can rank FGFR2 inhibitors at all, in a target where every known inhibitor is already sub-nanomolar. When the whole measured range spans 0.11–0.5 nM — a 4.5-fold window, or 0.89 kcal/mol of binding free energy — the differences a screen must resolve are smaller than Vina's documented ±1–2 kcal/mol noise. The falsifiable hypothesis, stated before the results: under one standardised protocol on the activated FGFR2 structure 2PVF, Vina will reproduce pemigatinib's own docking within 0.1 kcal/mol (the duplicate control) but will not recover the measured potency order of four sub-nanomolar inhibitors (Spearman rho above −0.5), because the potency differences are below the method's resolution.

2. Methods

2.1 Literature basis

PubMed (E-utilities, accessed 17 November 2026) for FIGHT-202, FOENIX-CCA2 and FGFR2 fusion prevalence; ChEMBL (live API, accessed 17 November 2026) for target, potency and resistance-mutant records. Every number traces to a PMID-verified source, a ChEMBL record named in the text, or a computation in the raw JSON. The Islamic canon check is in §2.5.

2.2 Molecular docking

Standardised AutoDock Vina protocol, exactly as Papers #1/#3: Vina v1.2.7, exhaustiveness 8, box 22.5 Å, best of three poses reported, same binding site, grid centre and box for the reference drug and every test compound. Target: FGFR2, UniProt P21802, resolved by accession to ChEMBL target CHEMBL4142 (Fibroblast growth factor receptor 2, Homo sapiens, SINGLE PROTEIN, component P21802 — verified live; the pipeline's text-search list offered maltase-glucoamylase CHEMBL2074 first, as usual, and it was not used). Structure: PDB 2PVF, 1.8 Å, the tyrosine-phosphorylated activated FGFR2 kinase domain in complex with the ATP analogue ACP (adenosine 5′-(β,γ-methylene)triphosphate) and a substrate peptide. Centre audit: the docking centre [23.11, −5.95, −2.14] is exactly the centroid of the 31-atom ACP ligand, computed directly from the 2PVF HETATM records (distance 0.00 Å) — the ATP-binding pocket, the correct site for an ATP-competitive inhibitor. The phosphotyrosine residue PTR 586 (substrate peptide) sits 17.3 Å from the centre and was not used. Ligands: the top five leads by the pipeline's composite score (similarity × 40 + Lipinski × 20 + Veber × 10 + PAINS × 10 + tox × 20) plus the reference query itself, from 40 ChEMBL bioactivities at pChEMBL ≥ 5 for CHEMBL4142. PAINS screen (RDKit) and ToxGuard Tox21 kNN panel for every compound. Spearman rank correlation between best Vina affinity and measured pChEMBL, computed on the four distinct docked compounds (the duplicate pemigatinib dock excluded); negative rho is the correct direction (better dock, more potent).

2.3 The duplicate control, stated in advance

The pipeline returns the reference drug twice: once as the QUERY (PubChem CID 86705695, pemigatinib) and once as ChEMBL4297522, which ChEMBL identifies as PEMIGATINIB (max phase 4, first approval 2020), same formula C24H27F2N5O4. Both were docked. Their score difference is a built-in reproducibility control for the whole protocol: two independent ligand preparations of the same molecule, same site, same box.

2.4 Honesty limits

Docking ≠ activity; Vina noise is ±1–2 kcal/mol; no experimental data were generated; no molecular dynamics or free-energy refinement was run; the structure is the activated (phosphorylated) kinase, not an inhibitor-bound inactive conformation. Measured potencies are ChEMBL top records and span assay formats (see §3.3).

2.5 Literature and the Islamic canon

The classical canon was checked alongside the modern literature, as the programme requires. Ibn Sina's Canon of Medicine (c. 1025) discusses diseases of the liver and bile in detail, and Al-Razi's Kitab al-Hawi (c. 900) records biliary disease; both predate the molecular diagnosis of cholangiocarcinoma by nine centuries, so neither names FGFR2, and no Canon-listed remedy was docked or screened in this run — the paper claims no traditional-medicine finding. The honest limit, named here: the full 23-volume Kitab al-Hawi exists in English only in selections, and most classical Arabic medical manuscripts remain undigitised.

3. Results

3.1 Docking: the comparison table

Compound Measured FGFR2 IC50 (ChEMBL top record) pChEMBL Best affinity (kcal/mol) Poses (kcal/mol) PAINS
CHEMBL5171314 0.27 nM 9.57 −9.25 −9.25, −9.24, −8.94 none
Pemigatinib (CHEMBL4297522) 0.24 nM 9.62 −8.90 −8.90, −8.84, −8.77 none
Pemigatinib (QUERY, duplicate) — (same molecule) — −8.83 −8.83, −8.71, −8.69 none
CHEMBL4862823 0.30 nM 9.52 −8.12 −8.12, −8.11, −8.09 none
CHEMBL4870179 0.15 nM 9.82 −8.01 −8.01, −8.00, −7.49 none

All five docks completed with tight poses (best-to-third spread ≤ 0.52 kcal/mol). The duplicate control passed: pemigatinib docked twice at −8.83 and −8.90, a 0.07 kcal/mol difference — the protocol reproduces itself. The ranking did not: the most potent measured inhibitor, CHEMBL4870179 (0.15 nM), scored worst (−8.01), 1.24 kcal/mol behind the best-docked compound, while the best-docked compound, CHEMBL5171314 (−9.25), is only the third most potent by measurement (0.27 nM). Spearman rho is +0.40 (n = 4) — a weak positive correlation carried by the middle of the table, while the most potent compound still scores worst. The spread of the whole docking table (1.24 kcal/mol) is inside Vina's noise band, and the spread of the whole measured range (0.15–0.30 nM) is 0.41 kcal/mol of binding free energy — the signal is smaller than the noise, and the result is what that arithmetic predicts.

3.2 Potency is solved; the ranking problem is the selection problem

All 26 leads retrieved for FGFR2 are sub-nanomolar: IC50 0.11–0.50 nM, pChEMBL 9.30–9.96. The most potent compound in the set, CHEMBL5173892 (IC50 0.11 nM, pChEMBL 9.96), was never docked: the pipeline docks the top five by a similarity-dominated composite score, and CHEMBL5173892 ranks 20th by that score (similarity 0.178 to pemigatinib). The same failure appeared in this series' DPP-4 paper, where the most potent compound in the set was never docked for the same reason. A screen that ranks by similarity to the reference drug systematically undocks the most potent compounds when they are the least similar to the reference — which is exactly the property a novel scaffold should have. One PAINS alert exists in the 26-lead set (CHEMBL1852688, rank 26); all docked compounds are PAINS-clean. Pemigatinib itself computes as drug-like: MW 487.51, logP 3.66, 1 donor, 6 acceptors, TPSA 83.16 Å², 6 rotatable bonds, zero Lipinski violations; ToxGuard kNN read-across is weak (maximum neighbour similarity 0.271) with all twelve Tox21 assay scores ≤ 0.239.

3.3 The measured order is less certain than the single numbers suggest

The two leads' sub-nanomolar values come from a single document each: CHEMBL4870179 (0.15 nM) and CHEMBL4862823 (0.30 nM) were both measured in one assay series (biotinylated-peptide substrate, human FGFR2, document CHEMBL4808209), and their relative order rests on that one series. A patent document (CHEMBL5726086) reports IC50 100 nM for both compounds under different conditions — a 300- to 600-fold conflict with the paper values. Pemigatinib's own record shows the same assay-to-assay spread: 0.24 nM (the pipeline's top record), 0.4 nM, 0.5 nM in three further records, and 1.0 nM by ELISA — a four-fold range for one drug. The honest reading is that the measured order among these four compounds is itself uncertain at the 0.4–0.9 kcal/mol level, before docking adds its own ±1–2 kcal/mol. The rho of +0.40 is therefore a statement about two uncertain orderings, not a precise measurement of docking failure — it is weakly positive only because the middle of the table lines up, while the most potent compound scores worst, and no re-analysis of the same four numbers can make it a ranking claim without new data.

3.4 The resistance data the docking cannot see

ChEMBL's mutant records for pemigatinib (document CHEMBL5131515, radiometric kinase assay) quantify the resistance problem that defines this target's future: against the gatekeeper mutant FGFR2 V564F, pemigatinib's IC50 is 1,460.5 nM — roughly 6,000-fold worse than wild type (0.24 nM) — and against N549H it is 3.37 nM, about 14-fold worse. Rigid docking on a wild-type structure cannot price either mutation: the V564F change is a single side chain in the ATP pocket, and the 6,000-fold loss is a steric and energetic effect that a rigid, metal-free, wild-type score has no way to represent. This is the same lesson as the series' covalent papers (DprE1, BTK): the clinically decisive number for an FGFR2 inhibitor is not its wild-type IC50, which is sub-nanomolar for every compound in the set, but its mutant coverage — and that number is not a docking number. Futibatinib's advantage in FOENIX-CCA2 is precisely that it is covalent and retains activity against acquired resistance mutations; the NEJM abstract states this directly.

3.5 Comparison with published docking

No published Vina benchmark of pemigatinib against these three ChEMBL leads on 2PVF was found in the literature sweep; the comparison is therefore internal (duplicate control, §2.3) and clinical (FIGHT-202 and FOENIX-CCA2 response rates). The paper does not claim its scores contradict any published docking result.

4. Discussion

4.1 The reframe: the target is solved, the screen is not

FGFR2 inhibition is a solved problem at the potency level: 26 compounds below 0.5 nM, two approved drugs, response rates of 35–42%. The unsolved problems are selectivity against FGFR1 (the hyperphosphataemia driver), mutant coverage (V564F costs pemigatinib 6,000-fold), and access (see §7). A docking screen that ranks sub-nanomolar compounds against each other on a wild-type structure answers none of these. It also actively misleads: it promotes CHEMBL5171314, an unnamed research compound, above the two approved drugs' class, on a 0.42 kcal/mol margin that is noise, while the compound that most needs docking — the most potent, least similar one — never gets docked at all.

4.2 Why the "win" must not be over-read

CHEMBL5171314's −9.25 is the best score in the table and means nothing on its own: it is 0.35 kcal/mol ahead of pemigatinib, inside noise; its measured potency is worse than pemigatinib's; and it is an unnamed compound with no clinical record. The duplicate control (Δ0.07) proves the protocol is reproducible, which makes the ranking failure more informative, not less: a reproducible method returning a reversed ranking is a method whose resolution is below the signal, not a method with a bug to fix by re-running.

4.3 Association only

This is a retrospective docking benchmark, not a causal experiment: it shows that Vina scores on 2PVF do not track measured FGFR2 potency within four sub-nanomolar compounds, under the stated protocol. It does not show that no docking method can rank these compounds — the falsifier names the method that could — and it does not show that CHEMBL5171314 is a worse drug than pemigatinib.

4.4 Testable hypotheses

  1. CHEMBL5171314 does not outperform pemigatinib in cells. Falsifier: paired FGFR2-driven cell viability assays (e.g. FGFR2-fusion iCCA lines); an IC50 for CHEMBL5171314 below pemigatinib's would refute the docking-implied order in the other direction.
  2. A re-dock on an inhibitor-bound inactive FGFR2 structure recovers the measured order (rho ≤ −0.5). Falsifier: the re-dock itself; if rho stays above −0.5, the failure is the scoring function, not the conformation.
  3. CHEMBL5173892 (0.11 nM, never docked) docks within 0.5 kcal/mol of pemigatinib. Falsifier: dock it on 2PVF under the same protocol; a score worse than −8.3 would show the selection problem is also a scoring problem.
  4. The V564F resistance gap is invisible to wild-type docking. Falsifier: a V564F-mutant structure dock showing pemigatinib losing ≥ 2 kcal/mol relative to wild type; a smaller loss would suggest the mutant effect is partly assay artefact.

4.5 Proposed validation (university-lab feasible, 8–12 weeks)

Stage 1 (weeks 1–2): dock CHEMBL5173892 on 2PVF under the identical protocol, and re-dock all five compounds on an inhibitor-bound FGFR2 structure (DFG-out if available) to test hypothesis 2. Stage 2 (weeks 3–6): obtain CHEMBL5171314 and CHEMBL4870179 commercially and run paired FGFR2 enzyme assays (wild type, V564F, N549H) with pemigatinib and futibatinib as controls. Stage 3 (weeks 7–10): cell viability in an FGFR2-fusion iCCA line for the two leads versus pemigatinib. Stage 4 (weeks 11–12): report all results including the negatives — a reversed ranking confirmed in cells is a publishable result.

5. Limitations

  1. No lab data. All results are computational; no FGFR2 assay was run, and the measured IC50s are ChEMBL records.
  2. Small n. Four distinct docked compounds; rho = +0.40 on n = 4 is a descriptive check, not a validated ranking failure.
  3. Assay heterogeneity. The four potencies span documents and formats, and a patent document conflicts with the paper values for the two leads (§3.3).
  4. Single structure, activated conformation. 2PVF is the phosphorylated, activated kinase with an ATP analogue bound; an inhibitor-bound inactive conformation might rank differently — that is the named falsifier, not a result.
  5. Selection bias. Only the top five by a similarity-dominated composite were docked; the most potent compound in the set was excluded by that rule.
  6. No mutant docking. V564F and N549H effects are reported from ChEMBL records, not computed.
  7. Islamic canon gaps (named, per the programme's rule). The Canon and Kitab al-Hawi were checked through named works, not read in full; the full 23-volume Hawi exists in English only in selections, and most classical Arabic medical manuscripts remain undigitised.

6. Policy implications

Decision-maker: the Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan (DRAP), the Ministry of National Health Services, and the national cancer programme — with the provincial health departments that run the public cancer hospitals. Three exact changes, each with its falsifier:

  1. Make FGFR2 fusion testing available in the public system before buying the drug. Pemigatinib helps only the 10–15% of iCCA patients with an FGFR2 fusion, and the test (RNA-based NGS or FISH) is the gate. A public laboratory that cannot test for the fusion cannot use the drug rationally, and will either treat unselected patients (wasting a costly drug on the 85–90% it cannot help) or treat nobody. Fund one reference NGS panel for FGFR2 fusions at a national laboratory, with a published turnaround time. If a validated, cheaper test (e.g. immunohistochemistry surrogate) is shown to match NGS for FGFR2 fusions, reverse this and fund that instead.
  2. Negotiate access, do not import at list price. Pemigatinib and futibatinib are priced for high-income markets; at list price they are unreachable for a Pakistani public hospital. The state should seek a pooled-procurement or voluntary-licence route for FGFR inhibitors, as it has done for other oncology drugs, and publish the price it pays. If the manufacturers refuse, the fallback is the covalent-compound route in (3), not silent non-availability.
  3. Fund mutant-coverage testing, not more wild-type docking. The clinically decisive number is V564F coverage (pemigatinib loses 6,000-fold), and no Pakistani laboratory currently runs an FGFR2 mutant panel. A single national panel (wild type, V564F, N549H) at one reference laboratory would convert this paper's falsifier into a routine check for any future FGFR2 inhibitor. Islamic principle behind the recommendations: preservation of life (hifz al-nafs, Al-Ghazali, Al-Mustasfa; Al-Shatibi, Al-Muwafaqat) — cholangiocarcinoma is a fatal disease and the drug exists, so a test that is not offered is a life not saved; and justice ('adl, Qur'an 4:135) — the burden falls on patients who cannot pay list price, so the research and procurement agenda must favour the poor, not the most familiar drug. Where the Islamic sources and the modern evidence point the same way, this paper says so; they do here.

7. Conclusion

Rigid Vina docking on the activated FGFR2 structure 2PVF reproduces pemigatinib itself to 0.07 kcal/mol and then ranks four sub-nanomolar inhibitors poorly (rho = +0.40, n = 4): the most potent measured compound scores worst, and the most potent compound in the set was never docked because it was too dissimilar to the reference. The measured range (0.15–0.30 nM, 0.41 kcal/mol) is smaller than the method's noise, and the measured order is itself uncertain across documents. The memorable number is 6,000-fold: what the gatekeeper mutation V564F costs pemigatinib, a number no wild-type docking score can see. Do not rank FGFR2 inhibitors by wild-type docking; test mutant coverage instead.

2026-11-16 Health Draft ready

Dapagliflozin Re-Docks at −11.00 kcal/mol on Its Own Cryo-EM Structure — but the Screen Ranks the Most Potent Lead Last

Dapagliflozin blocks the kidney's sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) and has transformed diabetic kidney disease and heart failure, but finding a better SGLT2 inhibitor still relies on screens that must first prove they can rank the drugs we already have.

PDF · Markdown

Read full paper

AI-assisted draft — NOT peer-reviewed, NOT published. All claims require independent laboratory verification. Do not cite as established evidence.

Author: Zubair Ali, Pharm-D student, Shaheed Mohtarma Benazir Bhutto Medical University (SMBBMU), Larkana, Pakistan Drafting assistant: Lapis (AI) Date: 2026-11-16 · Health Papers Agent — Paper #68 (daily 5-paper run)

Keywords: SGLT2; dapagliflozin; empagliflozin; diabetic kidney disease; cryo-EM; molecular docking; AutoDock Vina; polyol pathway

Abstract

Dapagliflozin blocks the kidney's sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) and has transformed diabetic kidney disease and heart failure, but finding a better SGLT2 inhibitor still relies on screens that must first prove they can rank the drugs we already have. We asked whether a standard automated docking pipeline ranks SGLT2 inhibitors by their measured potency. The pipeline (UniProtKB → ChEMBL → PubChem → RDKit → Vina 1.2.7) found no X-ray structure for SGLT2 and skipped docking entirely, so we docked dapagliflozin, four ChEMBL leads and empagliflozin on 8HEZ, the 2.8 angstrom cryo-EM structure of human SGLT2 bound to dapagliflozin itself, with the grid centre verified as the bound dapagliflozin's centroid. Dapagliflozin re-docks at −11.00 kcal/mol; its duplicate ChEMBL record scores −11.61, a 0.61 kcal/mol gap between identical molecules that sets the run's noise floor. The lead CHEMBL3703792 leads at −12.34, empagliflozin scores −12.03, and the LeadForge star lead CHEMBL5288495 scores −11.48 — but the docking rank against the measured potencies is exactly inverted (Spearman rho −1.0, n = 4): the most potent lead (IC50 0.308 nM) scores worst (−9.76) and the least potent (0.551 nM) scores best. The measured band is only 1.8-fold wide, so the inversion is a property of a band too narrow to rank, not a real anti-correlation — and empagliflozin, six times less potent than dapagliflozin (3.1 versus 0.49 nM), still out-scores it by 1.03 kcal/mol. The screen cannot rank SGLT2 inhibitors within this potency band, and the star lead is indistinguishable from dapagliflozin itself (0.48 kcal/mol behind its duplicate record, inside the 0.61 noise floor). The falsifiable next step is a glucose-uptake assay: if the measured IC50 rank does not match the docking rank, docking is not a ranking tool for this target. And the polyol-escape caveat from Paper #3 stands: an SGLT2-only inhibitor, however potent, does not address the sorbitol pathway that damages retina, kidney and nerve.

1. Introduction

SGLT2 reabsorbs most of the glucose filtered by the kidney, and blocking it spills glucose into the urine, lowers blood glucose, and — through mechanisms that go beyond glucose lowering — protects the kidney and the heart. In Pakistan, where 34.5 million adults live with diabetes at the highest age-standardised prevalence in the world (IDF Diabetes Atlas, 11th edition, 2025), that protection matters: diabetic kidney disease is the leading cause of kidney failure, and the SGLT2 inhibitors are the first drug class in decades to change its course. Dapagliflozin's evidence is the strongest in the class. In DAPA-CKD (4,304 patients with CKD, with or without diabetes), it cut the primary composite — a sustained 50% fall in eGFR, end-stage kidney disease, or death from renal or cardiovascular causes — from 14.5% to 9.2% over a median 2.4 years (hazard ratio 0.61, 95% CI 0.51–0.72; number needed to treat 19), with the kidney composite at HR 0.56 and death at HR 0.69 (Heerspink et al., N Engl J Med 2020;383:1436–1446, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2024816). In DAPA-HF (4,744 patients with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction), it cut worsening heart failure or cardiovascular death from 21.2% to 16.3% (HR 0.74, 0.65–0.85) (McMurray et al., N Engl J Med 2019;381:1995–2008, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1911303). The benefit is independent of diabetes status in both trials.

The structural basis arrived only recently. There is no X-ray structure of human SGLT2; the structures are cryo-EM. Niu et al. resolved the human SGLT2–MAP17 complex bound to empagliflozin at 2.95 angstrom (7VSI, Nature 2022;601:280–284) and showed empagliflozin occupying both the sugar-binding site and the external vestibule, locking the transporter in an outward-open conformation. Hiraizumi et al. then resolved the complex with five inhibitors, including dapagliflozin (8HEZ, 2.8 angstrom, Nat Struct Mol Biol 2024;31:159–169), and showed the four synthetic inhibitors binding the outward-facing conformation while phlorizin binds inward-facing. That history creates a precise, testable problem for docking. A pipeline that only accepts X-ray structures finds no structure at all for SGLT2 and skips docking — the correct behaviour for its own rules, and a failure of the rules. And a screen that docks on the cryo-EM structure must first prove it can rank dapagliflozin against empagliflozin and against leads whose measured potencies span less than two-fold.

This paper is SGLT2-only by design (topic HP-006), and it carries the polyol-escape caveat stated in Paper #3 of this series. Blocking SGLT2 lowers blood glucose, but glucose that enters insulin-independent tissues — retina, kidney, nerve — still feeds the polyol pathway: aldose reductase reduces it to sorbitol, consuming NADPH and depleting the glutathione those cells need against oxidative stress, while sorbitol itself cannot cross membranes and draws water in. Paper #3's rationale for a dual aldose-reductase + SGLT2 inhibitor was exactly this escape: an SGLT2-only drug, however potent, does not address polyol-mediated damage. The screen below ranks SGLT2 fit; it says nothing about the polyol pathway, and the paper does not pretend otherwise.

Hypothesis (falsifiable): under one standardised Vina protocol on the dapagliflozin-bound cryo-EM structure (8HEZ), the docking rank of the SGLT2 inhibitors will track their measured potencies, and the LeadForge star lead CHEMBL5288495 (IC50 0.35 nM) will out-score dapagliflozin. Falsified if the rank correlation is below 0.5, or if the star lead does not out-score dapagliflozin by more than the duplicate-molecule noise floor.

2. Methods

2.1 Literature basis

Searches were run on 2026-11-16 (web search; PubMed; the daily digest of 2026-11-15, which contained no SGLT2 item). Key sources: Heerspink et al. 2020 (doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2024816) for DAPA-CKD; McMurray et al. 2019 (doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1911303) for DAPA-HF; Niu et al. 2022 (Nature 601:280–284) for 7VSI; Hiraizumi et al. 2024 (Nat Struct Mol Biol 31:159–169, doi:10.1038/s41594-023-01134-0) for 8HEZ; Michel et al. 2015 (Naunyn Schmiedebergs Arch Pharmacol 388:801–816, doi:10.1007/s00210-015-1134-1) for empagliflozin's IC50 of 3.1 nM and its selectivity; and the IDF Diabetes Atlas, 11th edition (2025), for the Pakistan diabetes burden. Every citation in the References section was verified (journal, year, PMID or DOI checked, not invented).

2.2 Computation

The standard LeadForge pipeline was run with target "Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2" and reference drug dapagliflozin (run_docking.py, RDKit venv). UniProtKB resolved SGLT2 to P31639 (human SLC5A2, 672 amino acids), ChEMBL to target CHEMBL3884 (Sodium/glucose cotransporter 2, single protein, human), which returned 22 bioactivities; the similarity screen kept 22 and the ranking produced 23 leads. The pipeline's structure picker found no experimental structure meeting its criteria (X-ray only, under 3.0 angstrom) and docking was SKIPPED — error no_pdb_found — which the task protocol requires the paper to state honestly rather than to work around silently. The pipeline output is hidden_files/dock-HP-006-2026-11-16.json.

Because no X-ray structure exists, a control docking was run on 8HEZ, the 2.8 angstrom cryo-EM structure of the human SGLT2–MAP17 complex bound to dapagliflozin (hidden_files/dock_hp006_8hez.py, same Vina defaults: AutoDock Vina 1.2.7, one box of 22.5 angstrom, exhaustiveness 8, best of three poses reported). The centre [66.86, 66.86, 76.15] is from D._ligand_center and was verified by computing the HETATM group centroids directly from the PDB file: it is exactly the centroid of the bound dapagliflozin (ligand code LE6, chain A, residue 802, 28 atoms). The other HETATM groups are water molecules, a sodium ion (centroid [76.29, 61.39, 69.96]) and an N-acetylglucosamine (NAG, chain A, residue 801, centroid [60.43, 63.11, 114.25]) — the glycosylation site, far from the inhibitor pocket, and not the centre. Six compounds were docked: the query plus the top four leads, and empagliflozin (SMILES fetched live from PubChem PUG REST by name) as an approved-drug comparison. The query (dapagliflozin, MW 408.88, logP 1.84, TPSA 99.38, zero Lipinski violations, PAINS-clean, highest Tox21 read-across 0.076) carries no ChEMBL activity value in the pipeline output; its ChEMBL record CHEMBL429910 carries IC50 0.49 nM, and other ChEMBL assays for the same target report EC50 1.1 nM and IC50 6.7 nM — the paper quotes the stored value and names the spread. The leads' potencies are the ChEMBL bioactivity values for target CHEMBL3884, quoted as stored (IC50 values; the pipeline output does not record assay conditions, and the paper does not invent them).

2.3 PAINS and safety panel

RDKit PAINS filter and the ToxGuard Tox21 kNN read-across panel (12 assays) were applied to every compound, exactly as in Papers #1/#3 and the 2026-11-15 run.

2.4 Analysis plan (stated before results)

The analysis plan was fixed before docking: (i) report the 8HEZ docking table with measured SGLT2 potencies from the ChEMBL record and the literature; (ii) treat CHEMBL429910, the ChEMBL record of dapagliflozin itself, as a duplicate-reproducibility check against the query, exactly as Paper #64 did for olaparib; (iii) compute Spearman rank correlation of docking score against measured potency; (iv) declare the screen unable to rank within the band if the correlation is below 0.5 or the duplicate gap exceeds the gaps between distinct compounds. No post-hoc re-ranking was performed; any exploratory observation is labelled as such.

2.5 Honesty limits

Docking is not activity. Vina noise is ±1–2 kcal/mol. The structure is cryo-EM at 2.8 angstrom, not X-ray, and the docking is rigid: SGLT2 is a transporter that cycles through outward-open, occluded and inward-open states, and a single rigid conformation cannot model that cycle or the sodium-coupled transport step. No compound was assayed. The polyol pathway, the paper's stated caveat, is not modelled here. No cure claims are made.

3. Results

3.1 The pipeline found no structure — docking was skipped

The pipeline's structure picker accepts X-ray structures under 3.0 angstrom only. Human SGLT2 has no X-ray structure; its experimental structures are cryo-EM (7VSI at 2.95 angstrom, 8HEZ at 2.8 angstrom). The pipeline therefore returned no_pdb_found and skipped docking. That is the correct behaviour under its own rules, and it is also a failure of the rules: a pipeline that cannot use cryo-EM structures cannot dock the target that defines the class, and a user who did not read the log would receive a lead ranking with no docking at all. The docking below is the manual control that the pipeline's rules excluded.

3.2 Docking on the dapagliflozin-bound cryo-EM structure (8HEZ, 2.8 angstrom)

Compound Measured SGLT2 potency Vina on 8HEZ (kcal/mol) PAINS
CHEMBL3703792 IC50 0.551 nM (ChEMBL) −12.34 (−12.34, −9.34, −8.78) clean
Empagliflozin IC50 3.1 nM (literature) −12.03 (−12.03, −9.74, −9.38) clean
CHEMBL429910 (= dapagliflozin) IC50 0.49 nM (ChEMBL) −11.61 (−11.61, −10.07, −8.40) clean
CHEMBL5288495 (star lead) IC50 0.35 nM (ChEMBL) −11.48 (−11.48, −9.45, −8.46) clean
Dapagliflozin (QUERY) IC50 0.49 nM (ChEMBL record); other assays EC50 1.1 nM, IC50 6.7 nM −11.00 (−11.00, −10.09, −8.42) clean
CHEMBL3703868 IC50 0.308 nM (ChEMBL) −9.76 (−9.76, −8.81, −8.49) clean

Scores in kcal/mol, best of three poses (all poses in parentheses). All six compounds are PAINS-clean, carry zero Lipinski violations each (MW 408–461, logP 1.13–3.28), and show no decisive Tox21 signal (highest single read-across 0.362 for the star lead, 0.076 for dapagliflozin). Pose spreads are 1.27–3.56 kcal/mol — wider than the converged 6L88 control in Paper #67, tighter than the unconverged 4PF3 run, and moderate enough that the best-pose numbers are usable but not precise.

Three findings matter. First, the duplicate check: dapagliflozin docked twice — once as the query, once as its ChEMBL record CHEMBL429910 — scores −11.00 and −11.61, a 0.61 kcal/mol gap between identical molecules. That is the run's noise floor, and it is larger than the 0.37 gap Paper #64 found for the olaparib duplicate. Any gap smaller than 0.61 between two compounds in this table is indistinguishable from re-docking the same molecule.

Second, the rank is exactly inverted against the measured potencies. The four ChEMBL leads' measured order is CHEMBL3703868 (0.308 nM) > CHEMBL5288495 (0.35) > CHEMBL429910 (0.49) > CHEMBL3703792 (0.551); the docking order is the precise reverse, Spearman rho −1.0 (n = 4). The most potent lead scores worst (−9.76) and the least potent scores best (−12.34), a 2.58 kcal/mol gap across a 1.8-fold potency band. The paper reports the −1.0 and declines to treat it as a real anti-correlation: a 1.8-fold band is narrower than any assay can resolve, and the inversion is what noise looks like when the signal is smaller than the noise. The honest statement is that the screen cannot rank within this band — not that it ranks backwards.

Third, the approved-drug comparison fails the same way Paper #67's did. Empagliflozin (IC50 3.1 nM) is about six times less potent than dapagliflozin (0.49 nM by the stored ChEMBL value), yet it out-scores dapagliflozin by 1.03 kcal/mol (−12.03 versus −11.00). And the star lead CHEMBL5288495 (IC50 0.35 nM) scores −11.48 — 0.48 kcal/mol behind dapagliflozin's duplicate record, inside the 0.61 noise floor, and 0.86 behind the leader. The star lead is indistinguishable from dapagliflozin itself by this screen. The hypothesis is falsified on both counts: the rank correlation is −1.0, not above 0.5, and the star lead does not out-score dapagliflozin by more than the duplicate noise floor.

3.3 Comparison with published docking

No published Vina docking score for dapagliflozin on 8HEZ was found to compare against, and the paper does not invent one. The reference point is the structural literature: Niu et al. 2022 showed empagliflozin occupying both the sugar-binding site and the external vestibule of the outward-open transporter (7VSI), and Hiraizumi et al. 2024 showed the four synthetic inhibitors, including dapagliflozin, binding the outward-facing conformation (8HEZ). Our re-dock places dapagliflozin at −11.00 kcal/mol in its own co-crystal pocket with poses of −11.00, −10.09 and −8.42, consistent with re-docking into its own cryo-EM structure. The earlier LeadForge figure for the star lead (−7.03 kcal/mol against dapagliflozin's −4.84) is NOT reproduced here: it came from a different structure and protocol whose grid centre was never verified after the centre-pick bug, and the two numbers are not comparable. The honest comparator is the clinical one: dapagliflozin's kidney and heart-failure benefits (DAPA-CKD HR 0.61; DAPA-HF HR 0.74) and its selectivity (about 1,200-fold over SGLT1; empagliflozin over 2,500-fold) are properties of the drugs in patients and in cells, and no docking score on 8HEZ predicts them.

4. Discussion

4.1 What the screen can and cannot say

The screen can say that dapagliflozin re-docks in its own pocket at −11.00 kcal/mol, that the duplicate-molecule noise floor is 0.61 kcal/mol, and that the lead CHEMBL3703792 tops the table at −12.34 — a candidate worth the glucose-uptake assay, not a verdict. It can say that the pipeline's X-ray-only rule excludes the only structures that exist for this target, and that a cryo-EM structure at 2.8 angstrom docks fine once the centre is verified against the bound ligand. It cannot rank SGLT2 inhibitors within a 1.8-fold potency band: the rank is inverted, the star lead is indistinguishable from dapagliflozin, and the weaker approved drug out-scores the stronger one. It cannot say anything about the polyol pathway, which is the paper's stated caveat and the reason Paper #3 proposed a dual inhibitor.

4.2 The cryo-EM lesson

The pipeline's structure picker is the finding, not a footnote. It accepts X-ray structures under 3.0 angstrom and nothing else, so for SGLT2 — a target whose structures are all cryo-EM — it silently returns no docking and a lead ranking built on similarity and ADMET alone. Paper #65 found the same pattern for GLP-1R, where the picker chose a 1.80 angstrom extracellular-domain crystal over the 3.1 angstrom cryo-EM structure of the full receptor with the drug bound, and the drug re-docked 3.14 kcal/mol stronger on the cryo-EM structure. The lesson generalises: the picker's resolution filter is a proxy for quality, and for membrane proteins — transporters, GPCRs — the best structure is often the cryo-EM one the filter excludes. The fix is to let the picker accept cryo-EM structures and to verify the centre against the bound ligand, as this paper did; the fix is stated here as a pipeline change, not implemented in this run.

4.3 The polyol-escape caveat, restated

An SGLT2-only inhibitor lowers blood glucose by spilling it into the urine, but the glucose that reaches insulin-independent tissues still enters the polyol pathway, where aldose reductase reduces it to sorbitol at the cost of NADPH, depleting glutathione and drawing water into cells that cannot export sorbitol. That is the damage mechanism in retina, kidney and nerve, and it is not addressed by a better SGLT2 score. Paper #3's dual aldose-reductase + SGLT2 rationale stands: the next screen in this series should dock against both targets and require a lead to score on both, or the programme should say plainly that it is optimising glucose lowering and kidney protection, not the polyol damage. This paper optimises the former and states the limit.

4.4 Testable hypotheses

  1. Potency hypothesis. In a glucose-uptake assay in SGLT2-expressing cells, the measured IC50 rank of the docked set reproduces the 8HEZ docking rank. Falsified if the rank correlation is below 0.5 — in which case docking is not a ranking tool for this target, and the programme should screen by uptake assay directly.
  2. Selectivity hypothesis. The best lead CHEMBL3703792 is at least 1,000-fold selective for SGLT2 over SGLT1 in the same assay, matching dapagliflozin's profile. Falsified if selectivity is below 100-fold — in which case the lead risks the gastrointestinal effects of SGLT1 blockade, whatever its SGLT2 score.
  3. Polyol hypothesis. In a diabetic rat model, the best lead plus an aldose-reductase inhibitor reduces retinal sorbitol more than the lead alone, at the same glucose lowering. Falsified if the combination adds nothing — in which case Paper #3's dual rationale does not hold in vivo, and the SGLT2-only path is sufficient for that endpoint.

4.5 Proposed validation (university-lab feasible, 8–12 weeks)

Stage 1 (weeks 1–3): glucose-uptake (AMG) assay in SGLT2- and SGLT1-expressing cells for the docked set plus dapagliflozin and empagliflozin as controls; report IC50 with 95% CI and the SGLT2/SGLT1 selectivity ratio. Stage 2 (weeks 4–6): aldose-reductase inhibition assay for the best lead, to test the dual-inhibition rationale directly. Stage 3 (weeks 7–10): urinary glucose excretion and kidney sorbitol in a diabetic rat model for the best lead versus dapagliflozin, with and without an aldose-reductase inhibitor. Stage 4 (weeks 11–12): hERG and CYP inhibition screen for the lead. Success criterion: the lead matches dapagliflozin's glucose lowering with at least 1,000-fold SGLT2 selectivity — not merely a better docking score.

5. Limitations

  1. Docking only; no experimental data in this paper. Vina noise (±1–2 kcal/mol) is larger than several of the gaps reported, and the duplicate-molecule gap (0.61 kcal/mol) is the measured noise floor for this run.
  2. A single rigid cryo-EM conformation: SGLT2 cycles through outward-open, occluded and inward-open states, and rigid docking cannot model that cycle or the sodium-coupled transport step; no MD or free-energy refinement was run.
  3. The measured potency band is 1.8-fold wide (0.308–0.551 nM), narrower than any assay can resolve; the −1.0 rank correlation is a property of that band, not evidence of anti-correlation.
  4. Measured potencies mix ChEMBL bioactivities and literature IC50 values from different assays; dapagliflozin itself is reported as 0.49 nM (stored ChEMBL IC50), 1.1 nM (EC50) and 6.7 nM (IC50) in different assays.
  5. The polyol pathway is stated as a caveat, not modelled; no aldose-reductase docking or assay is in this paper.
  6. The Islamic canon sweep covers the available digitised canon relevant to the question (Ibn Sina, Al-Qanun fi al-Tibb, c. 1025; Al-Razi, Kitab al-Hawi, c. 900); the full 23 volumes of Kitab al-Hawi exist in English only in selections, and many classical Arabic manuscripts remain undigitised — the sweep names this gap rather than claiming completeness.
  7. No Pakistan-specific data on SGLT2 inhibitor prices, availability, or kidney-monitoring capacity are reported here; the burden numbers are national diabetes estimates (IDF Diabetes Atlas 2025).

6. Conclusion

Dapagliflozin re-docks at −11.00 kcal/mol in its own cryo-EM pocket (8HEZ), but the screen cannot rank SGLT2 inhibitors: the docking rank against measured potency is exactly inverted (rho −1.0, n = 4) across a 1.8-fold band too narrow to rank, the star lead CHEMBL5288495 (−11.48) is indistinguishable from dapagliflozin itself (0.48 kcal/mol behind its duplicate record, inside the 0.61 noise floor), and empagliflozin — six times less potent — out-scores dapagliflozin by 1.03 kcal/mol. The pipeline's X-ray-only rule skipped docking entirely for this target, because the only SGLT2 structures are cryo-EM; the manual control on 8HEZ, with its centre verified against the bound dapagliflozin, is what produced the numbers. And the polyol-escape caveat from Paper #3 stands: an SGLT2-only inhibitor, however potent, does not address the sorbitol pathway that damages retina, kidney and nerve.

7. Policy implications

Decision-maker: the Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan (DRAP) and the provincial health departments, with the Pakistan Society of Nephrology and the Pakistan Endocrine Society as clinical advisers. Decision: whether to add an SGLT2 inhibitor to the public formulary for diabetic kidney disease and heart failure, and at what price. Recommendation: add dapagliflozin (or a generic equivalent when available) to the formulary for patients with diabetic kidney disease or heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, on the DAPA-CKD and DAPA-HF evidence — the kidney composite fell by 39% and the heart-failure composite by 26%, with benefits independent of diabetes status — and pair the listing with urine albumin-to-creatinine testing in diabetes clinics, since the indication cannot be applied where albuminuria is never measured. Falsifier / reversal: if the negotiated price exceeds the per-patient cost of the current standard pathway without a measured kidney- or heart-failure-outcome gain, or if albuminuria testing coverage cannot be demonstrated in the prescribing facilities, reverse the formulary recommendation and keep the drug in the private market only. The principle is hifz al-nafs (preservation of life) with maslaha (public benefit) as the weighing rule, in the tradition of Ibn Sina's Al-Qanun fi al-Tibb (c. 1025): a health system preserves life by buying the drug whose benefit is proven in the patients who need it, and by building the testing that finds those patients — treatment and diagnosis together, not one without the other.
