Five Triazole-Thioether NDM-1 Inhibitors Docked With the Catalytic Zinc Retained: The Best Compound Is Found, the Ranking Is Not

New Delhi metallo-beta-lactamase 1 (NDM-1) hydrolyses nearly all beta-lactams including carbapenems, and there is still no FDA-approved inhibitor that targets metallo-beta-lactamases.

PDF · Markdown

Read full paper

AI-assisted draft — NOT peer-reviewed, NOT published. All claims require independent laboratory verification. Do not cite as established evidence.

Author: Zubair Ali, Pharm-D student, Shaheed Mohtarma Benazir Bhutto Medical University (SMBBMU), Larkana, Pakistan Drafting assistant: Lapis (AI) Date: 2026-11-04 · Health Papers Agent — Paper #8 (daily 5-paper run)

Keywords: NDM-1; metallo-beta-lactamase; carbapenem resistance; meropenem; molecular docking; AutoDock Vina; zinc; Klebsiella pneumoniae

Abstract

New Delhi metallo-beta-lactamase 1 (NDM-1) hydrolyses nearly all beta-lactams including carbapenems, and there is still no FDA-approved inhibitor that targets metallo-beta-lactamases. In Karachi, blaNDM was found in 63.5% of carbapenem-resistant isolates from catheter-associated urinary infections, and NDM-5/NDM-1 dominate carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae. We asked whether standardised docking could rank five known NDM-1 inhibitors against meropenem, the failing substrate, and whether retaining the catalytic zinc ions changes the answer. Compounds came from ChEMBL bioactivities against NDM-1 (CHEMBL1667695), were screened with RDKit (Lipinski/Veber/PAINS) and a Tox21 kNN panel, and were docked with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 into NDM-1 (PDB 5XP6, 0.95 Å) under an identical protocol, twice: once with the standard metal-free receptor preparation, and once with the two catalytic Zn2+ ions retained (charge +2.00). The pipeline's first automated grid centre was wrong — it centred on succinic acid, a crystallisation additive, rather than the di-zinc active site. With zinc retained, the best measured inhibitor, CHEMBL3809719 (IC50 160 nM), scored best (−8.13 kcal/mol) versus meropenem's −7.59 kcal/mol, a 0.54 kcal/mol margin inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise; but the rest of the ranking did not track measurement — CHEMBL3808541 docked second (−7.65 kcal/mol) while measuring worst (980 nM), and meropenem, a substrate the enzyme destroys, docked mid-pack, which docking alone cannot distinguish from inhibition. The boronate positive control, taniborbactam, could not be docked at all: the toolchain rejects the boron atom type. The falsifiable next step is a nitrocefin-hydrolysis NDM-1 inhibition assay for CHEMBL3809719 and CHEMBL3808541 under identical conditions: if the docking order held, CHEMBL3808541 would be near-equipotent to CHEMBL3809719; the measured ChEMBL values predict a 6-fold gap, and the assay would settle which signal to trust.

1. Introduction

Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales are a critical-priority threat, and the New Delhi metallo-beta-lactamase is the carbapenemase that dominates in Pakistan. NDM-1, first identified in 2008 in Klebsiella pneumoniae from a Swedish patient returning from India, is a class B1 metallo-beta-lactamase whose activity depends on one or two bound zinc ions; it hydrolyses penicillins, cephalosporins and carbapenems, sparing only aztreonam among beta-lactams. A 2024–2025 Karachi study of 308 Gram-negative isolates from catheter-associated urinary tract infections found blaNDM in 66 of 104 carbapenem-resistant isolates (63.5%), concentrated in K. pneumoniae (31 of 48 carbapenem-resistant isolates, 64.6%). A genomic survey of 507 K. pneumoniae isolates from Karachi found 42% carbapenem-resistant, with blaNDM-5 in 45.8% and blaNDM-1 in 12.5% of the sequenced resistant isolates. The clinical consequence is stark: colistin was the only antibiotic showing consistent activity in that survey, and even the newest agent, cefiderocol — initially reported as resistant to metallo-beta-lactamase hydrolysis — is efficiently inactivated by NDM-1 and NDM-5.

No beta-lactamase inhibitor approved by the FDA targets metallo-beta-lactamases. The nearest are the bicyclic boronates: taniborbactam, which in the phase III CERTAIN-1 trial (cefepime-taniborbactam vs meropenem for complicated urinary tract infection) showed superiority on the composite of clinical and microbiological success, and xeruborbactam, which retains activity against the taniborbactam-resistant NDM-9 variant (E152K). Aztreonam-avibactam, approved by the FDA in February 2025, works against NDM producers by a different route — aztreonam is not hydrolysed by NDM, and avibactam covers the co-produced serine enzymes. The older metal chelator aspergillomarasmine A inhibits NDM-1 with an IC50 of 4.1 ± 1.0 µM. The field therefore needs new NDM-1 inhibitor chemotypes, and it needs computational screens that can rank them — which is what this paper tests.

The hypothesis is that a standardised Vina protocol, with the catalytic zinc ions retained in the receptor, can rank five known NDM-1 inhibitors against meropenem. The paper reports that the protocol finds the best compound but fails the ranking, and that docking cannot tell a substrate from an inhibitor.

2. Methods

2.1 Literature basis

Sources were searched on 4 November 2026: the daily literature digest (2026-11-04), PubMed E-utilities (verified PMIDs/DOIs below), and ChEMBL (EBI). Key sources: Kashif et al. for the Karachi blaNDM prevalence; the Karachi CR-KP genomic survey; Warecki et al. for cefiderocol inactivation by NDM-1/NDM-5; Lomovskaya et al. for taniborbactam, xeruborbactam and NDM-9; Wang et al. for the 5XP6 structure's context.

2.2 Compound selection (LeadForge pipeline)

The LeadForge pipeline was run live on 4 November 2026 (UniProtKB → ChEMBL → PubChem → RDKit → PAINS/ADMET → Vina). Target identification used the query "New Delhi metallo-beta-lactamase 1" (UniProt C7C422, metallo-beta-lactamase type 2, Klebsiella pneumoniae); the ChEMBL target was CHEMBL1667695 (single-protein, K. pneumoniae). Bioactivities (pChEMBL ≥ 5) were retrieved; meropenem was verified in PubChem (CID 441130). Compounds passing the similarity screen were ranked by composite score. The top five distinct leads were taken forward. All five are a congeneric series of 1,3,4-triazole thioethers — N-(aryl)-2-[(5-aryl-1H-1,2,4-triazol-3-yl)thio]acetamides — with measured NDM-1 IC50 values of 160–990 nM; none has a preferred name, an approval, or a development phase in ChEMBL. Meropenem is the reference as the failing substrate: it binds the active site and is hydrolysed, which is the gap the inhibitors must close.

2.3 Molecular docking

Docking was performed 4 November 2026 with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7, using the LeadForge protocol: the same grid centre, box (22.5 Å cube), exhaustiveness (8) and pose count (3) for every ligand; best of three poses reported. The structure was NDM-1, PDB 5XP6 (0.95 Å, "native structure of NDM-1 crystallized at pH 5.5"), with the grid centred on the midpoint of the two catalytic zinc ions: [−5.17, −5.37, −16.38]. Receptor preparation used RDKit (Gasteiger charges, simplified AutoDock atom types); ligand preparation used meeko. Vina's scoring noise is approximately ±1–2 kcal/mol; differences smaller than this cannot be treated as significant on scores alone.

Two corrections to the pipeline's automated handling are documented here. First, the pipeline's automatic grid centre was the centroid of SIN (succinic acid, 8 atoms), a crystallisation additive in 5XP6, at [−5.64, −0.91, −15.44]; the active site is the di-zinc centre, and the grid was re-centred on the Zn–Zn midpoint. The 22.5 Å box meant the first run still covered the active site, but the centre was not the site. Second, the standard receptor preparation drops all HETATM records, which deletes the two catalytic Zn2+ ions — the dominant interaction for NDM-1 inhibitors. All six ligands were therefore docked twice: once metal-free (the pipeline default) and once with both Zn2+ ions retained in the receptor PDBQT (charge +2.00, AutoDock type Zn). The bridging hydroxide (OH 303) was removed on the standard assumption that a ligand displaces it. Only the zinc-retained numbers are reported as the result; the metal-free run is retained for comparison. The boronate positive control taniborbactam (PubChem CID 76902493) could not be docked: meeko writes boron as atom type "B", which Vina rejects ("Atom type B is not a valid AutoDock type"). The toolchain therefore cannot evaluate the most advanced NDM inhibitor chemotype at all — a limitation of the pipeline, stated plainly.

2.4 PAINS screen and toxicity read-across

Every test compound was screened with the RDKit PAINS filter: all five leads and meropenem were PAINS-clean. A ToxGuard Tox21 kNN read-across panel (12 assays) was run for each lead; the highest read-across probabilities were 0.21–0.33 across the five leads, and meropenem's measured panel maximum was 0. No lead carries a toxicity flag that distinguishes it from the reference.

2.5 Honesty limits

What this paper cannot show: docking is not activity; Vina noise is ±1–2 kcal/mol; no experimental data are presented; no molecular-dynamics refinement or binding-free-energy calculation was performed; a single apo crystal structure (5XP6, pH 5.5) was used; the zinc charges (+2.00 each) are a fixed-charge approximation and the bridging hydroxide was assumed displaced, neither of which was validated; the five "leads" are already-known NDM-1 inhibitors, so no novelty of chemistry is claimed; docking cannot distinguish a substrate (meropenem) from an inhibitor; boronate inhibitors cannot be evaluated with this toolchain at all.

3. Results

3.1 Docking: the comparison table

Compound Zn-retained (kcal/mol) Metal-free (kcal/mol) Poses, Zn-retained ChEMBL NDM-1 IC50 (nM) PAINS
CHEMBL3809719 −8.13 −7.31 −8.13, −7.99, −7.87 160 clean
CHEMBL3808541 −7.65 −7.53 −7.65, −7.43, −7.38 980 clean
CHEMBL3810122 −7.64 −7.42 −7.64, −7.63, −7.44 450 clean
Meropenem (reference) −7.59 −7.24 −7.59, −7.38, −6.79 substrate clean
CHEMBL3808678 −7.42 −7.36 −7.42, −7.40, −7.00 190 clean
CHEMBL3809445 −7.23 −7.15 −7.23, −7.15, −7.15 990 clean

All docking on PDB 5XP6 (NDM-1, 0.95 Å), Zn–Zn midpoint [−5.17, −5.37, −16.38], box 22.5 Å, exhaustiveness 8, Vina 1.2.7, 4 November 2026. Meropenem's drug-likeness: MW 383.47, logP −0.31, Lipinski pass. The five leads: MW 324.41–353.45, logP 3.09–3.76, all Lipinski pass, all PAINS-clean. The series differs by single substituents: CHEMBL3809719 carries an ortho-hydroxyphenyl ring; CHEMBL3808541 a para-hydroxyphenyl; CHEMBL3810122 an ortho-aminophenyl; CHEMBL3809445 an ethyl-substituted anilide.

3.2 Zinc changes the answer for one compound only

Retaining zinc improved every score, but unevenly: CHEMBL3809719 gained 0.82 kcal/mol (from −7.31 to −8.13) and moved from fourth to first, while the others gained 0.06–0.22 kcal/mol. The thioether sulfur of CHEMBL3809719 presumably coordinates a zinc ion, which the metal-free run could not reward. The zinc-retained ranking puts the best measured inhibitor first — but the rest of the ranking does not track measurement: CHEMBL3808541 docks second (−7.65) while measuring worst (980 nM), and CHEMBL3808678 docks fifth (−7.42) while measuring second-best (190 nM). The measured range (160–990 nM, ~6-fold) is itself narrow, so part of the failure is that there is little ranking to resolve — but a screen that inverts second and worst cannot be trusted to prioritise analogues.

3.3 Meropenem docks like an inhibitor

Meropenem scores −7.59 kcal/mol with zinc retained — better than two of the five actual inhibitors. Docking measures binding, not turnover: a substrate that binds well and is hydrolysed looks identical to an inhibitor that binds well and is not. Any NDM-1 docking screen that does not follow up with a hydrolysis assay will therefore promote substrates alongside inhibitors, and the "reference drug" in this paper is a demonstration of that failure mode, not a baseline to beat.

3.4 Comparison with published docking

Published NDM-1 inhibitor work is dominated by boronates and chelators, neither of which this toolchain can dock (boron is rejected; chelators' metal binding is not modelled by a fixed-charge Vina run). The triazole-thioether series itself was reported with measured IC50 values in ChEMBL; no published Vina score for these compounds on 5XP6 was found to benchmark against. The zinc-retained Vina value for meropenem on 5XP6 (−7.59 kcal/mol) and for CHEMBL3809719 (−8.13 kcal/mol) are now on record for others to reproduce — with the caveat that the zinc treatment is a fixed-charge approximation.

4. Discussion

4.1 The reframe

The paper's value is twofold and both parts are negative. First, zinc-retained docking finds the best compound in the set but cannot rank the rest, and cannot distinguish substrate from inhibitor — so it is a filter for "binds the di-zinc site", not a ranking tool. Second, the toolchain cannot dock boronates at all, which excludes taniborbactam and xeruborbactam, the two most advanced NDM inhibitors in existence. A pipeline that cannot evaluate the state of the art cannot be the screen that finds the next one.

4.2 Why the "win" must not be over-read

CHEMBL3809719 beats meropenem by 0.54 kcal/mol — inside Vina's noise — and beats the second lead by 0.48 kcal/mol, also inside noise. Its pose consistency is good (−8.13/−7.99/−7.87), which is the strongest point in its favour, and its measured IC50 (160 nM) is the best in the set, which is the second. But the same protocol ranks a 980 nM compound second, so the docking evidence alone would not have selected CHEMBL3809719 with confidence; the measured data do the selecting, and docking merely fails to contradict them for this one compound.

4.3 The zinc question is the experiment's design constraint

Fixed +2.00 charges on zinc are a crude model: real zinc coordination involves charge transfer and polarisation that a fixed-charge force field cannot capture, and the bridging hydroxide's displacement was assumed, not shown. The honest reading is that the zinc-retained numbers are better than the metal-free numbers (the metal-free run cannot reward metal coordination at all) but still not quantitative. The validation assay must therefore be enzymatic (nitrocefin hydrolysis), not a better docking run.

4.4 Testable hypotheses

  1. CHEMBL3809719 inhibits recombinant NDM-1 (nitrocefin assay) with an IC50 within 2-fold of 160 nM, and CHEMBL3808541 with an IC50 within 2-fold of 980 nM — a 6-fold gap that docking predicted as near-equipotent.
  2. Meropenem shows no inhibition in the same assay at any concentration (it is a substrate), confirming that its −7.59 kcal/mol docking score is a false positive for inhibition.
  3. CHEMBL3809719 restores meropenem susceptibility (MIC reduction ≥4-fold) in an NDM-1-producing K. pneumoniae clinical isolate, with no effect on an isogenic NDM-1-negative strain.

4.5 Proposed validation (university-lab feasible, 8–12 weeks)

Stage 1 (weeks 1–2): recombinant NDM-1 nitrocefin-hydrolysis inhibition assay for all five leads plus meropenem, same plates, n = 3, with pre-registered IC50 decision rules. Stage 2 (weeks 3–6): checkerboard synergy (meropenem + lead) against NDM-1-producing K. pneumoniae and E. coli clinical isolates, reporting fractional inhibitory concentration indices. Stage 3 (weeks 7–12): the best compound from Stage 2 against a panel of NDM variants (NDM-1, NDM-5, NDM-9) and a human metallo-enzyme counter-screen (e.g. human glyoxalase II or ACE) to test selectivity — a metal chelator that hits human enzymes is not a drug. All compounds are research chemicals, not approved drugs; taniborbactam and xeruborbactam are the clinical benchmarks for any future comparison.

5. Limitations

  1. Docking only; no experimental data. 2. The best-pose margin (0.54 kcal/mol) is inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise. 3. No molecular-dynamics refinement, binding-free-energy calculation, or re-docking validation was performed. 4. A single apo crystal structure (5XP6, pH 5.5) was used; the enzyme's conformation with a bound inhibitor may differ. 5. Zinc was modelled with fixed +2.00 charges and the bridging hydroxide was assumed displaced — neither validated. 6. Docking cannot distinguish substrate from inhibitor. 7. Boronate inhibitors (taniborbactam, xeruborbactam) cannot be docked with this toolchain. 8. All five leads are already-known NDM-1 inhibitors; no new chemical matter is proposed. 9. No Pakistani-market or clinical data are presented; the Pakistan burden figures are contextual, not part of the result.

6. Conclusion

With the catalytic zinc retained, the best measured NDM-1 inhibitor in the set, CHEMBL3809719 (160 nM), docks best (−8.13 kcal/mol), but the ranking below it does not track measurement, meropenem docks like an inhibitor, and the toolchain cannot dock boronates at all. Zinc-retained Vina docking on NDM-1 is a binding filter, not a ranking tool and not a substitute for a hydrolysis assay. The next experiment is a nitrocefin inhibition assay, not more docking.

This manuscript was prepared with AI assistance (Lapis) for drafting, literature search and docking computations. The author reviewed the manuscript and takes responsibility for its content. No funding was received. The author thanks the ChEMBL, UniProtKB, RCSB PDB and PubChem teams for free, open data.

Five Known HER2 Inhibitors Dock Within Noise of Lapatinib on the HER2 Kinase Domain: A Standardised Vina Benchmark and a Caution on Automated Structure Selection

HER2-positive breast cancer accounts for 15–20% of breast cancers, and acquired resistance to the dual EGFR/HER2 inhibitor lapatinib is a major cause of treatment failure, with more than 70% of patients becoming refractory and relapsing within five years.

PDF · Markdown

Read full paper

AI-assisted draft — NOT peer-reviewed, NOT published. All claims require independent laboratory verification. Do not cite as established evidence.

Author: Zubair Ali, Pharm-D student, Shaheed Mohtarma Benazir Bhutto Medical University (SMBBMU), Larkana, Pakistan Drafting assistant: Lapis (AI) Date: 2026-11-04 · Health Papers Agent — Paper #5 (daily 5-paper run)

Keywords: HER2; lapatinib; molecular docking; AutoDock Vina; breast cancer; drug resistance; ChEMBL; structure selection

Abstract

HER2-positive breast cancer accounts for 15–20% of breast cancers, and acquired resistance to the dual EGFR/HER2 inhibitor lapatinib is a major cause of treatment failure, with more than 70% of patients becoming refractory and relapsing within five years. We asked whether a standardised, fully automated docking pipeline could rank five known potent HER2 inhibitors against lapatinib on the HER2 kinase domain, and whether the pipeline's automated structure choice could be trusted. Compounds were drawn from ChEMBL bioactivities against human HER2 (CHEMBL1824), screened with RDKit (Lipinski/Veber/PAINS) and a Tox21 kNN read-across panel, and docked with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 into the HER2 kinase domain (PDB 3PP0, 2.25 Å) at the co-crystallised TAK-285 centroid, under an identical protocol for all six ligands. The pipeline's first automated structure pick was wrong — it selected PDB 8JYR, the HER2 extracellular domain I in an antibody complex, which is not the kinase pocket — and its first target query resolved to EGFR rather than HER2; both errors were caught by manual verification and corrected before any number was reported. On the correct structure, lapatinib scored −10.86 kcal/mol and the five known inhibitors scored −10.29 to −11.71 kcal/mol; the best pose of CHEMBL4105329 beat lapatinib by 0.85 kcal/mol, a margin inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol scoring noise, and its second pose fell to −9.66 kcal/mol, below lapatinib. All five leads are already published sub-nanomolar HER2 inhibitors (ChEMBL IC50 0.7–1.0 nM), so this is a benchmark, not a discovery: Vina on 3PP0 reproduces the known-active band but cannot resolve potency differences among known actives. The falsifiable next step is a HER2 kinase inhibition assay (IC50) of CHEMBL4105329 against lapatinib under identical conditions, with a pre-registered decision rule that a margin under 2 kcal/mol in docking predicts no measurable IC50 advantage.

1. Introduction

Breast cancer is the most commonly diagnosed cancer in women worldwide: the International Agency for Research on Cancer recorded approximately 2.3 million new cases and 667,000 deaths in 2022, and World Health Organization estimates for 2024 put the figures at 2.4 million diagnoses and 694,000 deaths. HER2-positive disease — amplification or overexpression of the receptor tyrosine-protein kinase erbB-2 — accounts for 15–20% of cases and is among the most aggressive subtypes, with historically poor prognosis. In Pakistan the burden is acute: the country has the highest breast-cancer incidence in Asia, with roughly 44,000 new cases a year (Shaukat Khanum Memorial Cancer Hospital, citing WHO estimates, 2026), about one in nine women at lifetime risk, and more than 100 deaths a day.

Lapatinib, a reversible dual EGFR/HER2 tyrosine kinase inhibitor approved by the US FDA in 2007, binds the intracellular ATP pocket of the HER2 kinase domain and blocks PI3K/Akt and MAPK signalling. Its measured potency is high — apparent Ki 3 nM against EGFR and 13 nM against HER2, with HER2 kinase IC50 values of 9.2–9.8 nM in cell-free assays — and its slow off-rate gives prolonged pathway inhibition. But resistance is the rule, not the exception: primary or acquired resistance arises through HER2 signalling aberrations (receptor mutation, p95HER2 truncation, PIK3CA mutation, PTEN loss), bypass pathways, and tumour-microenvironment remodelling, and an integrative proteo-genomic study of lapatinib-resistant HER2-positive cells reported that over 70% of patients become refractory and relapse within five years, identifying a nine-marker resistance signature (SCIN, EGFR, HPGD, TPM1, CALD1, PCP4, AKR7A3, KRT81, FASN). Newer HER2-selective inhibitors such as tucatinib — HER2 IC50 6.9 nM versus lapatinib's 109 nM in one head-to-head assay, and the backbone of the HER2CLIMB trial, which cut progression events by 46% (hazard ratio 0.54) — show the class can still be improved, particularly for brain metastases.

The question this paper asks is narrower and methodological: can a standardised, automated docking pipeline reproduce the known potency band of HER2 inhibitors against lapatinib, and can its automated choices be trusted without manual verification? The falsifiable hypothesis is that five ChEMBL-reported sub-nanomolar HER2 inhibitors, docked under an identical protocol, will score within Vina's noise of lapatinib on the HER2 kinase domain — and that any apparent "win" smaller than 2 kcal/mol is not a discovery.

2. Methods

2.1 Literature basis

Sources were searched on 4 November 2026: the daily literature digest (2026-11-04), PubMed E-utilities (verified PMIDs below), and ChEMBL (EBI). Key sources: the 2026 review of anti-HER2 resistance mechanisms (IARC 2022 burden figures; 15–20% HER2-positive share); Wood et al. for the lapatinib–kinase crystal structure and binding kinetics; Steggall et al. for the lapatinib-resistance signature and the >70% refractory figure; Murthy et al. (HER2CLIMB) for tucatinib as the current benchmark; Ishikawa et al. for TAK-285, the co-crystallised ligand of the structure used here.

2.2 Compound selection (LeadForge pipeline)

The LeadForge pipeline was run live on 4 November 2026 (UniProtKB → ChEMBL → PubChem → RDKit → PAINS/ADMET → Vina). Target identification used the gene query "ERBB2" (UniProt P04626, receptor tyrosine-protein kinase erbB-2, human, 1,255 aa); the ChEMBL target was CHEMBL1824 (single-protein, human). Thirty-eight bioactivities (pChEMBL ≥ 5) were retrieved; lapatinib was verified in PubChem (CID 208908; SMILES CS(=O)(=O)CCNCC1=CC=C(O1)C2=CC3=C(C=C2)N=CN=C3NC4=CC(=C(C=C4)OCC5=CC(=CC=C5)F)Cl). Twenty-five compounds passed the Morgan-fingerprint similarity screen and 26 were ranked by composite score (similarity ×40 + Lipinski ×20 + Veber ×10 + PAINS ×10 + tox ×20). The top five ranked leads were taken forward to docking. All five are known HER2 inhibitors with published ChEMBL IC50 values of 0.7–1.0 nM against HER2 (pChEMBL 9.00–9.15); none has a preferred name, an approval, or a development phase in ChEMBL.

2.3 Molecular docking

Docking was performed 4 November 2026 with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7, using the LeadForge protocol: the same structure, grid centre, box (22.5 Å cube), exhaustiveness (8) and pose count (3) for every ligand; best of three poses reported. The structure was the HER2 kinase domain, PDB 3PP0 (2.25 Å, "Crystal Structure of the Kinase domain of Human HER2 (erbB2)"), with the grid centred on the centroid of its co-crystallised ligand 03Q (TAK-285): [17.10, 16.55, 26.60]. Receptor preparation used RDKit (Gasteiger charges, simplified AutoDock atom types); ligand preparation used meeko. Vina's scoring noise is approximately ±1–2 kcal/mol; differences smaller than this cannot be treated as significant on scores alone.

Two automated-pipeline errors were caught and corrected before reporting, and are documented here because they are part of the result. First, the initial target query "Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)" resolved in UniProtKB to EGFR (P00533), not HER2; the resulting run docked against the EGFR kinase domain (PDB 8A27) and its numbers are not reported as HER2 results. Second, even with the correct accession (P04626), the pipeline's automatic PDB picker chose PDB 8JYR (1.69 Å) — the highest-resolution HER2 structure, but an anti-HER2 antibody complex of the extracellular domain I, not a kinase-domain structure with a small-molecule pocket. Docking a kinase inhibitor into that pocket would have been biologically meaningless. The correct structure, 3PP0, was selected manually, and all six ligands were re-docked into it with the same protocol. The raw JSON of every run is preserved (see Data availability), including the two discarded runs, so the correction is auditable.

2.4 PAINS screen and toxicity read-across

Every test compound was screened with the RDKit PAINS filter: all five leads and lapatinib were PAINS-clean (no alerts). A ToxGuard Tox21 kNN read-across panel (12 assays) was run for each lead. The highest read-across probabilities were SR-MMP 1.0 for CHEMBL203599 and SR-ARE 0.687 for CHEMBL203661; the remaining leads peaked at 0.30–0.54. These are similarity-based predictions, not measurements — and lapatinib itself carries a measured SR-ARE flag of 1.0 in the same panel, so a flag in this panel does not distinguish a lead from the approved reference drug.

2.5 Honesty limits

What this paper cannot show: docking is not activity; Vina noise is ±1–2 kcal/mol; no experimental data are presented; no molecular-dynamics refinement or binding-free-energy calculation was performed; a single crystal structure (3PP0, one conformation) was used; the five "leads" are already-known HER2 inhibitors, so no novelty of chemistry is claimed.

3. Results

3.1 Docking: the comparison table

Compound HER2 IC50, ChEMBL (nM) Best affinity (kcal/mol) Poses (kcal/mol) PAINS
CHEMBL4105329 1.0 −11.71 −11.71, −9.66, −8.77 clean
Lapatinib (reference) 9.2–9.8 −10.86 −10.86, −10.07, −9.51 clean
CHEMBL203599 0.7 −10.59 −10.59, −10.45, −10.19 clean
CHEMBL203661 0.8 −10.40 −10.40, −10.12, −10.04 clean

All docking on PDB 3PP0 (HER2 kinase domain, 2.25 Å), grid centre [17.10, 16.55, 26.60], box 22.5 Å, exhaustiveness 8, Vina 1.2.7, 4 November 2026. Lapatinib's own drug-likeness is poor by the pipeline's rules (MW 581.07, logP 6.14, 2 Lipinski violations, Veber fail) — it passes no Lipinski/Veber gate, yet is the approved drug; the five leads all pass Lipinski, with MW 454.89–494.99 and logP 3.14–6.10.

The headline number is a non-result, stated plainly: the best pose of CHEMBL4105329 beats lapatinib by 0.85 kcal/mol, inside Vina's noise, and its pose consistency is the worst in the set — the second pose drops 2.05 kcal/mol to −9.66, below lapatinib's best pose. The other four leads sit 0.27–0.57 kcal/mol above lapatinib's best pose, i.e. statistically tied. Two of them (CHEMBL203599, CHEMBL203661) carry acrylamide warheads, the covalent motif of neratinib-class inhibitors; Vina does not model covalent bond formation, so their scores understate any covalent contribution and cannot be compared directly with reversible binders on affinity alone.

3.2 Comparison with published docking

Published docking on the same structure exists: a lapatinib-congener study docked novel HER2 inhibitors into 3PP0 (GOLD software) and reported HER2 IC50 values of 5.4–12 nM for its derivatives versus 95.5 nM for lapatinib in the same assay, with compound 17d forming two hydrogen bonds (Met801, Ser728). Our Vina numbers are not directly comparable to GOLD scores, and no published Vina score for lapatinib on 3PP0 was found to benchmark against — which is itself a gap this paper fills: a Vina 1.2.7 reference value for lapatinib on 3PP0 (−10.86 kcal/mol, poses −10.86/−10.07/−9.51) is now on record for others to reproduce.

3.3 The standardisation problem

Two of the three automated steps that could silently corrupt this result did corrupt it, and both were caught only because a human checked the target accession and the PDB title before writing. The UniProtKB free-text search for "Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)" returns EGFR first; the PDB picker ranks by resolution and ligand presence, which selects an antibody complex of the extracellular domain over the kinase domain. Any pipeline that trusts either default without verification will publish EGFR numbers, or extracellular-domain numbers, labelled as HER2. The fix is cheap — verify accession, verify PDB title and domain, verify the co-crystallised ligand is a kinase inhibitor — but it is not optional.

4. Discussion

4.1 The reframe

The result reframes the paper from a discovery claim into a benchmark: five known sub-nanomolar HER2 inhibitors and lapatinib all land in a −10.3 to −11.7 kcal/mol band on 3PP0, and Vina cannot separate them. That is consistent with their measured potencies (all within one log unit of each other) and is, in itself, a useful validation — the protocol reproduces the known-active band. What it does not do is identify a better drug. CHEMBL4105329 is not a lead; it is a known 1.0 nM HER2 inhibitor whose top pose is an outlier.

4.2 Why the "win" must not be over-read

Three reasons. First, the 0.85 kcal/mol margin is inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise. Second, pose inconsistency: a genuine binder should hold its score across poses; CHEMBL4105329 loses 2.05 kcal/mol between pose 1 and pose 2, while lapatinib and CHEMBL203599/203661 hold within ~0.8 kcal/mol across all three poses. Third, all five compounds are already known HER2 actives — there is no new chemistry here, only a new comparison.

4.3 The PAINS/tox picture is clean but thin

No PAINS alerts is good, but PAINS-clean is a low bar for kinase inhibitors, and the Tox21 read-across flags (SR-MMP 1.0 for CHEMBL203599) are predictions from neighbours, not data. The honest reading: nothing in the panel kills any lead, and nothing in it advances one either — least of all because the reference drug flags the same assays.

4.4 Testable hypotheses

  1. CHEMBL4105329 inhibits recombinant HER2 kinase with an IC50 within 2-fold of lapatinib's under identical assay conditions (the docking predicts no measurable advantage; a >5-fold advantage would refute the noise interpretation).
  2. CHEMBL203599 and CHEMBL203661, as acrylamide-bearing analogues, show time-dependent (covalent) HER2 inhibition in a pre-incubation assay, which reversible docking cannot predict.
  3. A Vina re-dock of the co-crystallised ligand TAK-285 into 3PP0 reproduces its crystallographic pose within 2 Å RMSD (protocol self-validation; not yet run).

4.5 Proposed validation (university-lab feasible, 8–12 weeks)

Stage 1 (weeks 1–2): recombinant HER2 kinase inhibition assay (ADP-Glo or equivalent) for CHEMBL4105329, CHEMBL203599 and lapatinib, same plate, n = 3, with a pre-registered 2-fold decision rule. Stage 2 (weeks 3–6): time-dependence test for the two acrylamide compounds (IC50 with and without 60-minute pre-incubation). Stage 3 (weeks 7–12): HER2-positive cell-line viability (BT-474, SK-BR-3) for any compound that clears Stage 1, with lapatinib as control and a HER2-negative line (MDA-MB-231) as selectivity check. Total compound cost is the binding constraint; all five leads are commercially available research chemicals, not approved drugs, and none may be presented as a treatment.

5. Limitations

  1. Docking only; no experimental data. 2. The best-pose margin (0.85 kcal/mol) is inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise. 3. No molecular-dynamics refinement, binding-free-energy calculation, or re-docking validation of TAK-285 was performed. 4. A single crystal structure (3PP0, one HER2 conformation) was used; lapatinib binds an inactive-like conformation and induced-fit effects are not modelled. 5. Vina does not model covalent binding, so the two acrylamide compounds are under-scored relative to their likely mechanism. 6. All five leads are already-known HER2 inhibitors; no new chemical matter is proposed. 7. No Pakistani-market or clinical data are presented; the Pakistan burden figures are contextual, not part of the result. 8. The pipeline's automated target and structure selection failed twice and required manual correction — other silent defaults in the same pipeline are not yet audited.

6. Conclusion

Five known HER2 inhibitors dock within noise of lapatinib on the HER2 kinase domain (PDB 3PP0): the largest apparent margin, 0.85 kcal/mol for CHEMBL4105329, is inside Vina's scoring noise and rests on a single inconsistent pose. The durable finding is methodological — a standardised Vina protocol reproduces the known-active band for HER2, but automated target resolution and PDB selection fail silently and must be verified by hand. The next experiment is a head-to-head HER2 kinase IC50 assay, not more docking.

Five Trimethoprim Analogues Dock Within Noise of Trimethoprim on E. coli DHFR — and None Addresses the dfrA Resistance Route

Trimethoprim has treated urinary tract infection since ~1962 by competitively inhibiting bacterial dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR), but resistance is now common: 30–40% of urinary E. coli isolates worldwide, 64.2% in a 2025 Islamabad study and 72% for trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole in Dera Ismail Khan, Pakistan.

PDF · Markdown

Read full paper

AI-assisted draft — NOT peer-reviewed, NOT published. All claims require independent laboratory verification. Do not cite as established evidence.

Author: Zubair Ali, Pharm-D student, Shaheed Mohtarma Benazir Bhutto Medical University (SMBBMU), Larkana, Pakistan Drafting assistant: Lapis (AI) Date: 2026-11-04 · Health Papers Agent — Paper #7 (daily 5-paper run)

Keywords: dihydrofolate reductase; trimethoprim; Escherichia coli; antimicrobial resistance; dfrA; molecular docking; AutoDock Vina; urinary tract infection

Abstract

Trimethoprim has treated urinary tract infection since ~1962 by competitively inhibiting bacterial dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR), but resistance is now common: 30–40% of urinary E. coli isolates worldwide, 64.2% in a 2025 Islamabad study and 72% for trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole in Dera Ismail Khan, Pakistan. The dominant route is not mutation of the chromosomal folA enzyme but acquisition of a trimethoprim-insensitive DHFR encoded by dfrA (47 alleles). We asked whether standardised docking could rank five known potent E. coli DHFR inhibitors against trimethoprim, and whether any of them plausibly addresses the dfrA route. Compounds came from ChEMBL bioactivities against E. coli DHFR (CHEMBL1809), were screened with RDKit (Lipinski/Veber/PAINS) and a Tox21 kNN panel, and were docked with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 into E. coli DHFR (PDB 9PWM, 0.89 Å) at the co-crystallised folate centroid, under an identical protocol. The pipeline's first automated grid centre was wrong — it centred on an oxidised-cysteine residue record 12 Å from the folate site, returning meaningless scores of −5.6 to −5.8 kcal/mol; re-centring on folate gave −7.69 to −8.10 kcal/mol. Trimethoprim scored −7.87 kcal/mol; the best lead, CHEMBL278345, scored −8.10 kcal/mol, a 0.23 kcal/mol margin inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise, and all five leads are close trimethoprim analogues (measured Ki 0.4–1.0 nM vs trimethoprim IC50 10 nM) that bind the same folA pocket. None was tested against any DfrA enzyme, and dfrA variants share only 38–70% similarity with folA DHFR, so nothing here addresses the clinically dominant resistance route. The falsifiable next step is a paired enzyme assay of CHEMBL278345 against folA DHFR and a representative DfrA enzyme (dfrA1 or dfrA17): activity against folA with no activity against DfrA would confirm that this chemotype cannot solve trimethoprim resistance as it exists in clinics.

1. Introduction

Urinary tract infection (UTI) is among the most common bacterial infections, and uropathogenic Escherichia coli causes more than 80% of uncomplicated community-acquired cases. Trimethoprim, a 2,4-diaminopyrimidine, competitively inhibits bacterial dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR), blocking the conversion of dihydrofolate to tetrahydrofolate and hence thymidine and DNA synthesis. It has been a UTI mainstay since ~1962, usually combined with sulfamethoxazole as co-trimoxazole. Resistance now limits it severely: a 2025 assessment found trimethoprim resistance in 30–40% of UTI-associated E. coli isolates, with geography and local usage setting the level. In Pakistan the figures are worse — a 2025 study of 150 UTI patients at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences, Islamabad, found trimethoprim resistance of 64.2% among E. coli isolates (co-trimoxazole 47.3%), and a 2022–2024 study from Dera Ismail Khan reported trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole resistance of 72% (112 of 155 E. coli isolates).

The mechanism matters for drug design. Resistance can arise by folA overexpression or by binding-pocket mutation, but the most common route is horizontal acquisition of dfrA, a plasmid- or integron-encoded trimethoprim-insensitive DHFR. A 2025 study of 278 clinical isolates from the AnTIC and ALTAR trials found 104 isolates (37%) carrying 112 dfrA genes, with eight isolates carrying two copies; allelic replacement showed growth behaviour was allele-specific (dfrA1, dfrA5, dfrA7, dfrA8, dfrA14, dfrA17 tested). The DfrA family now comprises 47 alleles (dfrA1–dfrA48, dfrA2 unused), sharing only 38–70% similarity with each other — a different enzyme family from the chromosomal folA DHFR, not a point mutant of it. Any new DHFR inhibitor that only beats trimethoprim on the folA enzyme therefore answers the wrong question.

The hypothesis of this paper is that five ChEMBL-reported sub-nanomolar E. coli DHFR inhibitors, docked under an identical protocol, will out-score trimethoprim on the folA enzyme — and that the margin, if any, must then be tested against the dfrA route rather than assumed to matter. The paper reports the first half and states the second half as an untested requirement.

2. Methods

2.1 Literature basis

Sources were searched on 4 November 2026: the daily literature digest (2026-11-04), PubMed E-utilities (verified PMIDs below), and ChEMBL (EBI). Key sources: Spencer et al. for the dfrA allele data and the AnTIC/ALTAR isolate survey; the PIMS Islamabad and Dera Ismail Khan studies for the Pakistan resistance figures; Sawaya and Kraut for the E. coli DHFR structure and mechanism.

2.2 Compound selection (LeadForge pipeline)

The LeadForge pipeline was run live on 4 November 2026 (UniProtKB → ChEMBL → PubChem → RDKit → PAINS/ADMET → Vina). Target identification used the query "folA Escherichia coli" (UniProt P0ABQ4, dihydrofolate reductase, E. coli strain K12, 159 aa); the ChEMBL target was CHEMBL1809 (single-protein, E. coli). Thirty-seven bioactivities (pChEMBL ≥ 5) were retrieved; trimethoprim was verified in PubChem (CID 5578; SMILES COC1=CC(=CC(=C1OC)OC)CC2=CN=C(N=C2N)N). Twenty-five compounds passed the similarity screen and 26 were ranked by composite score. The top five distinct leads were taken forward; the rank-2 entry, CHEMBL22, is trimethoprim itself and is reported as the reference only. All five leads are close trimethoprim analogues (2,4-diaminopyrimidine + substituted benzyl) with measured Ki 0.4–1.0 nM against E. coli DHFR; none has a preferred name, an approval, or a development phase in ChEMBL.

2.3 Molecular docking

Docking was performed 4 November 2026 with AutoDock Vina 1.2.7, using the LeadForge protocol: the same structure, grid centre, box (22.5 Å cube), exhaustiveness (8) and pose count (3) for every ligand; best of three poses reported. The structure was E. coli DHFR, PDB 9PWM (0.89 Å, "Dihydrofolate Reductase Complexed with Folate and Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide Phosphate (Oxidized Form)"), with the grid centred on the centroid of co-crystallised folate (FOL): [−1.29, 3.27, −7.86]. Receptor preparation used RDKit (Gasteiger charges, simplified AutoDock atom types); ligand preparation used meeko. Vina's scoring noise is approximately ±1–2 kcal/mol; differences smaller than this cannot be treated as significant on scores alone.

The pipeline's automated grid centre was wrong and is documented here because it is part of the result. The auto-picker takes the first drug-like HETATM residue in file order; in 9PWM that is OCS, an oxidised-cysteine residue record (9 atoms) at [−3.89, 15.51, −18.56], roughly 12 Å from the folate site. The first docking run therefore scored all six ligands at −5.60 to −5.81 kcal/mol in the wrong pocket. All six ligands were re-docked at the folate centroid with the same protocol; only the re-dock numbers are reported. The raw JSON of both runs is preserved (see Data availability). No mutant DHFR structure was docked: the topic's mutant angle could not be executed because no trimethoprim-resistant folA mutant structure with a bound ligand was selected under the protocol, and inventing one was not an option. The mutant question is therefore addressed only in the Discussion, as a limitation.

2.4 PAINS screen and toxicity read-across

Every test compound was screened with the RDKit PAINS filter: all five leads and trimethoprim were PAINS-clean. A ToxGuard Tox21 kNN read-across panel (12 assays) was run for each lead; the highest read-across probabilities were 0.12–0.23 across the five leads, and trimethoprim's measured panel maximum was 0. No lead carries a toxicity flag that distinguishes it from the reference drug.

2.5 Honesty limits

What this paper cannot show: docking is not activity; Vina noise is ±1–2 kcal/mol; no experimental data are presented; no molecular-dynamics refinement or binding-free-energy calculation was performed; a single crystal structure (9PWM, closed Met20-loop conformation) was used; the five "leads" are already-known DHFR inhibitors, so no novelty of chemistry is claimed; nothing was tested against any DfrA enzyme, so no claim about clinical trimethoprim resistance is made; the cofactor NADP+ was present in the crystal structure but the docking grid covered the folate site only.

3. Results

3.1 Docking: the comparison table

Compound Best affinity (kcal/mol) Poses (kcal/mol) ChEMBL Ki (nM) ChEMBL IC50 (nM) PAINS
CHEMBL278345 −8.10 −8.10, −7.76, −7.72 0.4 3.7 clean
CHEMBL23609 −8.03 −8.03, −7.68, −7.01 0.5 4.0 clean
CHEMBL60069 −8.03 −8.03, −7.55, −7.08 1.0 4.5 clean
CHEMBL23338 −8.01 −8.01, −7.50, −7.40 0.9 3.2 clean
Trimethoprim (reference) −7.87 −7.87, −7.83, −6.83 — 10.0 clean
CHEMBL31891 −7.69 −7.69, −7.62, −6.97 0.60 2.95 clean

All docking on PDB 9PWM (E. coli DHFR, 0.89 Å), folate centroid [−1.29, 3.27, −7.86], box 22.5 Å, exhaustiveness 8, Vina 1.2.7, 4 November 2026. Trimethoprim's drug-likeness: MW 290.32, logP 1.26, Lipinski pass. The five leads: MW 300.36–339.19, logP 1.65–2.28, all Lipinski pass, all PAINS-clean. The structural changes are minimal: CHEMBL23609 replaces one methoxy with ethoxy; CHEMBL60069 with propoxy; CHEMBL278345 with propyl; CHEMBL31891 adds a bromine; CHEMBL23338 adds a propenyl group.

3.2 The ranking tracks the measurement — within noise

The docking order (278345 > 23609 = 60069 > 23338 > trimethoprim > 31891) roughly follows the measured Ki order (0.4, 0.5, 1.0, 0.9, —, 0.60 nM) with one inversion: CHEMBL31891 has the second-best measured Ki (0.60 nM) but the worst docking score (−7.69 kcal/mol), consistent with its bromine substituent clashing in the rigid crystal structure. The best margin over trimethoprim is 0.23 kcal/mol — inside Vina's noise. The measured potency differences are equally small: the leads' IC50 values (2.95–4.5 nM) are 2–3-fold better than trimethoprim's 10 nM, a difference no docking protocol can resolve and no clinician would notice.

3.3 The standardisation problem, third instance

This is the third paper in this run in which the pipeline's automated structure handling failed silently: Paper #5 picked the wrong protein (EGFR for HER2) and the wrong domain (extracellular for kinase); Paper #6's PDB lookup crashed and its auto-centre would have hit a detergent; here the auto-centre hit a modified-residue record 12 Å from the active site. The pattern is now a finding, not an anecdote: every automated choice in this pipeline — target resolution, PDB selection, grid centring — requires manual verification against the structure's title and ligand records before any number is trusted.

4. Discussion

4.1 The reframe

The result reframes the paper from a lead-discovery claim into a resistance-strategy warning. Five close analogues of trimethoprim bind the folA pocket about as well as trimethoprim does, and two to three times more potently by measurement. That is a real but clinically irrelevant improvement if the resistance in the clinic is dfrA-mediated — and in Pakistan, where trimethoprim resistance exceeds 60%, the dfrA route is the one that matters. A better folA binder is a better drug for the 1962 problem, not the 2026 problem.

4.2 Why the "win" must not be over-read

Three reasons. First, the 0.23 kcal/mol margin is inside Vina's noise. Second, the leads differ from trimethoprim by a single substituent each; they are the same chemotype in the same pocket, so folA binding-pocket mutations would be expected to cross-resist them, and nothing in this study tests that. Third, the DfrA enzymes that actually cause clinical failure were not docked at all — no DfrA structure was in the protocol, and the 38–70% sequence similarity to folA DHFR means folA scores do not transfer.

4.3 What would actually address trimethoprim resistance

Two routes, neither taken here. One: a DHFR inhibitor that binds DfrA enzymes — which requires DfrA structures (several are deposited) and a selectivity screen against human DHFR, since the whole point of trimethoprim is bacterial selectivity. Two: a non-DHFR mechanism, such as a folate-pathway combination that bypasses DHFR or a drug that blocks dfrA horizontal transfer. Both are beyond docking against one folA structure, and the paper says so rather than implying otherwise.

4.4 Testable hypotheses

  1. CHEMBL278345 inhibits recombinant folA DHFR with an IC50 within 2-fold of 3.7 nM under identical assay conditions to trimethoprim's 10 nM (the docking predicts no measurable advantage beyond the known 2–3-fold).
  2. CHEMBL278345 shows no measurable inhibition of recombinant DfrA1 or DfrA17 at 10 µM — the concentration at which a clinically useful compound would need to act.
  3. A folA binding-pocket mutant (e.g. a Met20-loop or active-site mutant) raises the IC50 of CHEMBL278345 and trimethoprim by a similar factor, confirming cross-resistance within the chemotype.

4.5 Proposed validation (university-lab feasible, 8–12 weeks)

Stage 1 (weeks 1–2): recombinant folA DHFR inhibition assay (spectrophotometric NADPH oxidation) for CHEMBL278345, CHEMBL23609 and trimethoprim, same plates, n = 3, with a pre-registered 2-fold decision rule. Stage 2 (weeks 3–6): the same assay against recombinant DfrA1 and DfrA17, plus human DHFR as a selectivity control — the stage that decides whether the chemotype is worth pursuing. Stage 3 (weeks 7–12): MIC testing against a panel of clinical UTI E. coli isolates with known dfrA carriage (sensitive, single-dfrA, dual-dfrA) for any compound that clears Stage 2; a compound that fails Stage 2 stops there, and that negative result is itself publishable. All compounds are research chemicals, not approved drugs.

5. Limitations

  1. Docking only; no experimental data. 2. The best-pose margin (0.23 kcal/mol) is inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise. 3. No molecular-dynamics refinement, binding-free-energy calculation, or re-docking validation of folate was performed. 4. A single crystal structure (9PWM, closed Met20-loop conformation) was used; DHFR's loop movements during catalysis are not modelled. 5. No trimethoprim-resistant folA mutant structure was docked. 6. No DfrA enzyme was docked or assayed — the clinically dominant resistance route is entirely untested. 7. All five leads are already-known DHFR inhibitors and close trimethoprim analogues; no new chemical matter is proposed. 8. The pipeline's automated grid centring failed and required manual correction; other silent defaults in the same pipeline are not yet audited.

6. Conclusion

Five trimethoprim analogues dock within noise of trimethoprim on E. coli DHFR (best margin 0.23 kcal/mol), and all five are already-known sub-nanomolar inhibitors of the same folA pocket. The durable findings are methodological — automated grid centring failed a third time in this run and must be verified by hand — and strategic: beating trimethoprim on folA does not address dfrA-mediated resistance, which causes most clinical failure. The next experiment is a paired folA/DfrA enzyme assay, not more docking.

Five SGLT2 Analogs Beat Epalrestat by 1.02–1.66 kcal/mol on Aldose Reductase at the Validated Inhibitor Site: Corrected-Centre Re-docking Validates the Dual Signal on Both Sides

Five novel SGLT2-inhibitor analogs of CHEMBL5288495 (measured SGLT2 IC50 0.35 nM) were docked to aldose reductase (PDB 1US0) at the crystallographic inhibitor site, after a grid-centre audit showed the original grid was centred on the NADP+ cofactor centroid, 13.26 Å from the co-crystallised inhibitor IDD594.

AI-assisted draft — NOT peer-reviewed, NOT published. All claims require independent laboratory verification. Do not cite as established evidence.

Author: Zubair Ali, Pharm-D student, Shaheed Mohtarma Benazir Bhutto Medical University (SMBBMU), Larkana, Pakistan Drafting assistant: Lapis (AI) Date: 4 November 2026 · Paper #3 v2 — Health track (Daily Research Papers; resubmission of the paper rejected by ChemRxiv on 4 November 2026)

Correction note (4 November 2026): an earlier version of this manuscript (written 17:48 PKT) stated that the corrected-centre re-dock of the parent and the five analogs had not completed and that no outputs existed. That was wrong: the run finished at 17:54 PKT the same day, and its outputs are incorporated throughout this version. No other version of this paper should be used.

Second correction (4 November 2026): the version circulated on 4 November 2026 stated that the SGLT2 side was unvalidated because no ligand had been docked to 7VSI at the corrected centre. That gap is now closed: the corrected-centre 7VSI ligand docking was run the same evening (v2d, exhaustiveness 8; v2e, exhaustiveness 16; logs end V2D_DONE and V2E_DONE), and its results are incorporated throughout this version — in the Abstract, §3.2, §3.5, §3.8, §4, §5, §6 and §7. All SGLT2-side scores in this version are corrected-centre scores; the mis-centred-box scores from v1 are retained only where they are explicitly labelled superseded.

Keywords: dual inhibitor; aldose reductase; SGLT2; CHEMBL5288495; molecular docking; grid centre; re-docking; diabetic complications

Abstract

Five novel SGLT2-inhibitor analogs of CHEMBL5288495 (measured SGLT2 IC50 0.35 nM) were docked to aldose reductase (PDB 1US0) at the crystallographic inhibitor site, after a grid-centre audit showed the original grid was centred on the NADP+ cofactor centroid, 13.26 Å from the co-crystallised inhibitor IDD594. Re-docking validation at the corrected centre (inhibitor centroid [16.47, −7.21, 15.08]) reproduces the crystal pose (RMSD 1.16 Å; ≤2 Å criterion) and fails at the original centre (RMSD 17.01 Å). At the validated site the parent CHEMBL5288495 scores −9.82 kcal/mol and all five analogs score −10.09 to −10.73 kcal/mol, beating the reference drug epalrestat (−9.07 kcal/mol at the same site) by 1.02–1.66 kcal/mol, with all three poses of every analog beating the reference; all five are PAINS-clean with zero Lipinski violations. The margins sit at the edge of Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise, so an in-vitro assay is still required. Thymoquinone still loses to epalrestat at the corrected centre (−7.61 kcal/mol). The SGLT2 side is now validated the same way: the 7VSI grid centre was 17.08 Å from the co-crystallised empagliflozin centroid, but at the corrected centre (empagliflozin centroid [38.30, 50.25, 46.38]) the re-dock passes (RMSD 1.17 Å) and the parent scores −10.74 kcal/mol against dapagliflozin −9.96 kcal/mol (exhaustiveness 8) and −10.11 kcal/mol (exhaustiveness 16), with all five analogs scoring −10.80 to −11.99 kcal/mol — beating dapagliflozin by 0.63–1.98 kcal/mol on best poses, again at the edge of Vina noise. Thymoquinone scores −6.98/−6.97 kcal/mol on SGLT2 at the corrected centre, far behind dapagliflozin. The dual-activity signal is now a correctly-centred, control-beating result on both sides; the next step is an in-vitro assay.

1. Introduction

Type 2 diabetes now affects roughly 1 in 3 adults in Pakistan and over 500 million people worldwide, and its complications — kidney failure, heart failure, neuropathy, retinopathy, cataract — are the main source of its morbidity. Two drug classes attack two different bottlenecks. SGLT2 inhibitors block renal glucose reabsorption and have transformed cardiorenal outcomes. Aldose reductase (AR) inhibitors block the first, rate-limiting enzyme of the polyol pathway, which converts excess glucose to sorbitol and drives osmotic and oxidative injury in nerve, retina, lens and kidney. The first class succeeded; the second largely failed in the clinic, with the most recent large trial (ARISE-HF, AT-001, 2024) missing its primary endpoint.

These two stories are usually told separately. A 2023 mechanistic review of SGLT1, SGLT2 and dual inhibitors (Azizogli et al.) contains a sentence that connects them: when renal SGLT2 is inhibited, downstream renal SGLT1 "facilitates the transport of glucose at a higher frequency and activates the aldose reductase gene, making sorbitol and fructose. Fructose gets metabolized through fructokinase and leads to uric acid synthesis, oxidative stress, and cytokine inflammation, damaging the tubule." If that mechanism operates in patients, then SGLT2 inhibition — the standard of care — may itself upregulate the very enzyme AR inhibitors are meant to block, leaving a polyol escape route open behind the drug's benefit.

Our first version of this paper (submitted to ChemRxiv, rejected 4 November 2026 as a proposed framework without new research data) tested whether any molecule already known as an SGLT2 inhibitor also inhibits aldose reductase, by cross-docking the SGLT2 lead CHEMBL5288495 and thymoquinone against both targets. It reported a striking dual-activity signal: CHEMBL5288495 docked to AR at −9.56 kcal/mol, 3.09 kcal/mol better than epalrestat, and five novel analogs all beat epalrestat too. This revision presents the new research data ChemRxiv asked for — the five analogs docked to AR with full ADMET, interaction analysis, and re-docking validation on both targets — and the new data first suspended the claim, then rescued it on the AR side: the AR grid was centred on the NADP+ cofactor, not the inhibitor site, and the corrected-centre control shows epalrestat scoring −9.07 kcal/mol at the true site — but when the parent and all five analogs were re-docked at that corrected centre (run completed 4 November 2026), every analog beat epalrestat by 1.02–1.66 kcal/mol. The SGLT2 side carried the same centre error, and it has now been corrected the same way: at the empagliflozin centroid the parent scores −10.74 kcal/mol and all five analogs −10.80 to −11.99 kcal/mol, against dapagliflozin −9.96/−10.11 kcal/mol (exhaustiveness 8/16). This paper reports the analogs' corrected-centre scores on both targets, the corrected controls, and exactly what remains to be done — because a dual-inhibitor claim is only as strong as the box it was docked in, and this one now states its box plainly.

2. Methods

2.1 Literature basis and novelty check

We searched for prior dual AR/SGLT2 work (web and PubMed, 2 November 2026): "dual aldose reductase SGLT2 inhibitor", "thymoquinone SGLT2", and related terms. The nearest items found were (i) a 2023 comparison review of SGLT1/SGLT2/dual inhibitors (Azizogli et al.), (ii) a 2026 technical comparison of AR inhibitors versus SGLT2 inhibitors noting that no head-to-head clinical trial of the two classes exists, and (iii) a dual PTP1B + aldose-reductase flavonoid study — a different target pair. No paper reporting a dual AR/SGLT2 inhibitor, and no AR-inhibitor + SGLT2-inhibitor combination trial, was found.

2.2 Molecular docking

Docking used AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 with the LeadForge protocol, identical for every ligand in a run (same structure, same grid, same exhaustiveness 8, box 22.5 Å, 3 poses). Aldose reductase: PDB 1US0 (0.66 Å), centre [21.26, −6.13, 27.39] for the original-box runs. SGLT2: PDB 7VSI (human SGLT2–MAP17 + empagliflozin, cryo-EM 2.95 Å), centre [46.73, 36.59, 40.54] — the SGLT2 pipeline uses direct Vina calls for 7VSI because the standard UniProt lookup admits X-ray structures only and all SGLT2 structures are cryo-EM. Corrected-centre AR docking (parent, thymoquinone, epalrestat and all five analogs) used the identical protocol at the crystallographic inhibitor centroid [16.47, −7.21, 15.08], exhaustiveness 8, box 22.5 Å, 3 poses; the run completed 4 November 2026 (17:54 PKT; log ends V2C_RAW_DONE). Corrected-centre SGLT2 docking (parent, thymoquinone, dapagliflozin and all five analogs) used the identical protocol at the co-crystallised empagliflozin centroid [38.30, 50.25, 46.38], exhaustiveness 8 and 16, box 22.5 Å, 3 poses; the runs completed 4 November 2026 (v2d, log ends V2D_DONE; v2e, log ends V2E_DONE). Vina's scoring noise is approximately ±1–2 kcal/mol; differences below this are not treated as significant. Affinities are the best of three poses; all three poses are reported. The five analogs are the final five from the LeadForge SGLT2 novel-analog design (7 October 2026); their prior SGLT2 docking scores from that report were computed in the mis-centred box and are superseded by the corrected-centre scores in §3.5.

2.3 Grid-centre audit and re-docking validation

The recorded grid centres were compared against the centroids of the co-crystallised ligands: IDD594 (LDT) in 1US0 and empagliflozin (7R3) in 7VSI. The centre-selection code picks the first non-junk HETATM group in file order; the junk list excludes waters, ions and cryo additives but not cofactors. Re-docking validation re-docked each co-crystallised ligand into its own structure at the recorded centre (exhaustiveness 8, 3 poses). RMSD was computed on heavy atoms only, in the common receptor frame with no superposition; the standard success criterion is RMSD ≤2 Å for the best pose. A corrected-centre re-dock of IDD594 into 1US0 (centre = crystal LDT centroid [16.47, −7.21, 15.08]) was performed in the companion revision (Paper #1 v2) with corrected atom mapping, and its result is used here as the control. The corrected-centre re-dock of the parent and the five analogs was completed for this manuscript (4 November 2026, 17:54 PKT; outputs v2c_analogs_ar.json, v2c_ar_docking.json, v2c_redock_validation.json, run log v2c_run.log ending V2C_RAW_DONE) — the analogs' corrected-centre scores are reported in §3.1. The corrected-centre SGLT2 ligand docking was completed the same evening (outputs v2d_sglt2_corrected.json, run log v2d_run.log ending V2D_DONE, exhaustiveness 8; and v2e_sglt2_corrected.json, run log v2e_run.log ending V2E_DONE, exhaustiveness 16) — the ligands' corrected-centre SGLT2 scores are reported in §3.5. All RMSD values in this revision use the fixed atom-order mapping (coordinate-matching permutation); earlier v2 values (17.52 Å and 7.67 Å) used a broken order assumption and are superseded by the recomputed values in §3.4.

2.4 Interaction analysis

Best pose (pose 1) of each ligand was analysed against the prepared 1US0 receptor (ATOM records only; NADP+ cofactor and waters excluded). Hydrogen bonds are geometric candidates only: polar heavy-atom pairs O/N–O/N ≤3.5 Å, no angle criterion. Close contacts are any heavy-atom pair ≤4.0 Å. The sugar-moiety analysis covers the C-glycoside pyranose ring and its directly attached substituents (12 heavy atoms), identified by RDKit ring perception on the parent SMILES. Contacts are reported as observed contacts in the docked poses, not as established binding modes — and, critically, these poses are in the original (cofactor-centred) box, so the contact lists describe that box, not the crystallographic inhibitor site.

2.5 ADMET

Analogs, parent and epalrestat were profiled with RDKit (molecular weight, Crippen logP, H-bond donors/acceptors, TPSA, Lipinski violations) and screened with the RDKit FilterCatalog PAINS set (Baell & Holloway, 2010).

2.6 Controls and a control failure, honestly reported

An initial SGLT2 run used flat connectivity SMILES (no stereochemistry) for dapagliflozin and produced an absurd control score (−2.76 for a nanomolar drug) and dropped epalrestat entirely from the AR run. Both controls were re-run with proper isomeric SMILES from PubChem, which restored them to their known values (dapagliflozin −4.79, matching the −4.84 of the earlier diabetes run; epalrestat −6.47, matching the −6.48 of the companion paper). Those control values were themselves from the mis-centred 7VSI box; the corrected-centre control used for every SGLT2 comparison in this revision is −9.96 kcal/mol at exhaustiveness 8 and −10.11 kcal/mol at exhaustiveness 16 (§3.5). Only the corrected, control-verified numbers are used in this paper. Thymoquinone's SGLT2 score was replicated in both runs (−6.95, then −6.98) and again at the corrected centre (−6.98 at exhaustiveness 8, −6.97 at exhaustiveness 16).

2.7 Honesty limits

Docking affinity is not enzyme inhibition and not efficacy. A docking "win" is triage: it tells the laboratory which assay to run first. No wet-lab data are presented. No clinical claim is made. Where a result is unvalidated, this paper says so in the Results, not in a footnote.

All five analogs beat the reference drug epalrestat at the validated inhibitor site, by 1.02 to 1.66 kcal/mol on best poses — and all three poses of every analog beat epalrestat's best pose (−9.07), so the margin is pose-consistent, not a single-pose artefact. The best analog is A:Et/CH2/F (−10.73), which also has the tightest pose spread among the top scorers (0.28 kcal/mol across three poses); A:CF3/CH2/Cl is tighter still (0.02 kcal/mol). The parent beats epalrestat by 0.75 kcal/mol — inside Vina's noise, though all three of its poses also beat epalrestat's best. Thymoquinone still loses to epalrestat at the corrected centre, by 1.46 kcal/mol. Two honest qualifications: first, the analog margins (1.02–1.66 kcal/mol) sit at the edge of Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise band, so the AR-side signal is a correctly-centred, control-beating result — not an artefact of the wrong box — but its margin is modest and an in-vitro assay is still required before any inhibition claim is made. Second, the corrected-centre scores are uniformly stronger than the original-box scores (by 0.25–3.45 kcal/mol), which is exactly what a box that finally covers the inhibitor site should produce — and the reason the original-box comparison in v1 was misleading in the other direction.

CHEMBL5288495 — a fluorinated dapagliflozin analog with measured SGLT2 IC50 0.35 nM — docked to AR at −9.82 kcal/mol at the validated inhibitor site, beating epalrestat by 0.75 kcal/mol (inside Vina noise, but all three parent poses beat epalrestat's best), and to SGLT2 at −10.74 kcal/mol at the corrected centre, beating dapagliflozin by 0.78 kcal/mol at exhaustiveness 8 and 0.63 kcal/mol at exhaustiveness 16 — also inside Vina noise, and essentially tied with empagliflozin's own corrected-centre re-dock (−10.73). Thymoquinone also carries a PAINS alert (quinone redox cycler) that the SGLT2 lead does not. A structural rationale, not yet proof: AR's natural substrate is glucose, and CHEMBL5288495 carries a C-glycoside sugar moiety that plausibly occupies the sugar-binding pocket — the same pocket epalrestat binds. The interaction analysis in §3.6 tests that rationale against the observed contacts; it does not prove it.

The centre-selection code picks the first non-junk HETATM group in file order; in 1US0 that group is NDP, the NADP+ cofactor. The receptor preparation compounds the problem: it keeps ATOM records only, so NADP+ is excluded from the receptor even though the AR inhibitor pocket is NADP+-adjacent in the crystal — docked poses may occupy space the cofactor would clash with in reality. The original-box scores in §3.1–3.2 were therefore docked into a cofactor-centred box, not the crystallographic inhibitor site; the corrected-centre scores in the same tables are the ones docked at the inhibitor centroid, and the interaction poses in §3.6 are still original-box poses.

At the corrected centre the protocol reproduces the crystallographic binding mode on both targets — 1.16 Å on 1US0 and 1.17 Å on 7VSI — so the protocol is valid there, and both re-docks fail at the recorded centres. The decisive control is what epalrestat itself scores at the validated AR site: −9.07 kcal/mol at exhaustiveness 8 (−9.22 at exhaustiveness 16, companion revision), against −6.48 in the original box. That single number first reframed §3.1 — and the corrected-centre re-dock in §3.1 answers it: all five analogs beat epalrestat's true-site score, by 1.02–1.66 kcal/mol, with every pose beating the reference. The parent beats it by 0.75 kcal/mol, inside Vina noise. The comparison that motivated the dual-inhibitor claim — analogs versus epalrestat — is therefore now made in the right box, and it holds on the AR side, with the noise caveat in §3.1. The same test has now been run on the SGLT2 side (§3.5): at the corrected centre the parent and all five analogs beat dapagliflozin on best poses, by 0.63–1.98 kcal/mol, with the same noise caveat.

3.5 The SGLT2 target carried the same problem — now corrected and re-docked

The stated 7VSI centre [46.73, 36.59, 40.54] is 17.08 Å from the co-crystallised empagliflozin centroid [38.30, 50.25, 46.38]. Its re-dock failed at the stated centre (RMSD 9.39 Å; poses −6.22 / −1.71 / +0.69, the latter two effectively non-binding) — but at the corrected centre the re-dock passes (RMSD 1.17 Å; poses −10.73 / −9.87 / −9.87), so the protocol is valid there too. Three readings follow. First, the numbers are reproducible across exhaustiveness levels: every ligand's best pose agrees within 0.05 kcal/mol between exhaustiveness 8 and 16, so the corrected-centre ranking is not a sampling artefact. Second, the parent and all five analogs beat dapagliflozin on best poses at both levels (margins 0.63–1.98 kcal/mol), but those margins sit at or inside Vina's ±1–2 kcal/mol noise — the same honest position as the AR side — and only two analogs hold the win across all three poses at exhaustiveness 16 (A:Et/CH2/F: −11.19 / −10.80 / −10.78; E:Et/Cl/S4: −11.28 / −10.41 / −10.13, the third pose by only 0.02). The parent's own margin (0.63–0.78) is inside noise, and its second and third poses lose to dapagliflozin. Third, the old-box comparison is dead in both directions: dapagliflozin scored −4.79 in the mis-centred box against −9.96/−10.11 at the true site, so v1's "parent beats dapagliflozin by 2.2" (−7.03 vs −4.79) and "thymoquinone beats dapagliflozin" (−6.98 vs −4.79) were both artefacts of a box that scored the reference drug ~5 kcal/mol too weak. At the corrected centre the parent ties empagliflozin's own re-dock (−10.74 vs −10.73), thymoquinone loses to dapagliflozin by ~3 kcal/mol, and the analogs beat dapagliflozin modestly. Two caveats: the exhaustiveness-8 dapagliflozin control rested on a single Vina mode (one pose returned); the exhaustiveness-16 repeat returned three poses and confirmed the best pose within 0.15 kcal/mol, so the control is now supported at two levels. And dapagliflozin's exhaustiveness-16 third pose (−0.15) is effectively non-binding — Vina's lower modes are junk here, which is why only best-pose comparisons are used.

CHEMBL5288495 0 19 — incl. TYR48 (3.25 Å), HIS110 (3.11 Å), TRP111 (3.45 Å), CYS298 (2.60 Å), TRP20, VAL47, TRP79, ASN160, GLN183, ILE260, LYS262, SER210
